# Sub-Page: Chatham Summer Camps  - Centercourt Club & Sports
**Centercourt Summer Camps–Choose Your Adventure!  
**Centercourt offers the best summer camps in the area, providing skill-building, active fun, and memorable experiences for kids all summer long. Choose from our exciting Ninja Adventure, Tennis, Combo, and Explorer camps tailored to every age and interest! (Find more details in our !)

**EARLY BIRD DISCOUNT** when you register before May 4, 2025. Call us at 973-635-1222 or email .

**Ninja Adventure & Tennis Combo Camp**  
_For Ages 5-14_  
An action-filled day combining the best of Centercourt Ninja and Tennis!

*   **Mornings:** Ninja Course & Field Sports to build agility, strength, and confidence, plus Martial Arts, Gaga, and Free Swim.
*   **Afternoons:** Tennis skill development and games using our ball progression system (Red to Yellow Ball), ensuring growth at every level.

**Full Day Schedule:** 9 AM - 4 PM  
Includes: Lunch + Free Swim (12 PM - 1:30 PM)

**  
Ninja Adventure Camp**  
_For Ages 5-14_  
An exciting mis of activities centered around our Ninja Courses, ensuring every camper has an unforgettable Centercourt experience.

*   **Activities:** Ninja Course, Martial Arts, Gaga, Field Sports, and More!
*   **Ninja Curriculum:** Combines climbing, parkour, gymnastics, and functional movements to build balance, coordination, strength, and mental confidence.
*   **Famous Fun Fridays:** Ice cream truck, pizza, inflatables, and more!

**Full Day Schedule:** 9 AM - 4 PM  
Includes: Lunch + Free Swim (12 PM - 1:30 PM)

**  
Centercourt Tennis Summer Camps**  
_For Ages 5-16_  
Elevate tennis skills in a camp tailored to every level—from beginner to elite!

*   **On-Court Training:** Technique, athletic skill, and game knowledge, with daily competitions.
*   **Camp Levels:** Red Ball (Ages 5-8.5), Orange Ball (Ages 8.5-10.5), Green Ball (Ages 10.5-12), Yellow Ball for ages 11 and up.
*   **Famous Fun Fridays:** Ice cream truck, pizza, inflatables, and more!

**Full Day:** 9 AM - 4 PM  
**Half Day (Red Ball only):** Morning (9 AM - 1:30 PM) or Afternoon (12 PM - 4 PM)

**  
Centercourt Explorer Summer Camp**  
_For Ages 3-4_  
Keep your little ones active and engaged with age-appropriate games and activities.

*   **Activities Include:** Ninja obstacles, gymnastics, arts & crafts, swim instruction, martial arts, and field sports.

**Explorer Core Camp:** 9 AM - 1:30 PM  
**Explorer Extended Day Camp:** 9 AM - 4 PM

### physical therapy

Professional Physical Therapy, headquartered in Melville, New York, is a leading provider of outpatient physical and hand therapy and rehabilitation services throughout the New York metropolitan area, New Jersey, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire.

​

Founded in 1998, Professional operates over 180 outpatient physical and hand therapy centers, along with a 20,000 square foot sports performance training facility in Garden City, NY, as well as a fitness center in Copiage, NY. Professional's patient-centric treatment philosophy is focused on providing exceptional, compassionate care to the entire person, and not just their injury. Their licensed Physical Therapists design customized treatment plans, using the most innovative therapeutics, to help patients achieve and exceed their goals.

​

About the Clinical Director:

Elliott Luty, PT, DPT, is a lifelong New Jersey resident and has previously worked at the company's River Edge and Bernardsville clinics. Luty earned his Doctorate of Physical Therapy from the New York Institute of Technology and his Bachelor’s Degree from Ramapo College. His clinical interests include sports rehabilitation, manual therapy, and post-operative cases.

a soccer ball. It places a large emphasis on technical skill in high-pressure situations, which can be translated into the outdoor game. It is a great way to develop skills like quick decision-making, close control, speed, and agility as it demands quick reflexes, fast thinking, and pinpoint passing. ### **Winter Training Benefits** * Individual skills development * Off-season improvement * Premium indoor locations throughout New Jersey and New York * Skills Clinic and RDS options available * Multiple seasons to select from - Choose your month or register for all! * Each participant receives a new Futsal Ball ### Additional benefits: * Encourages regaining possession of the ball as a productive, fun, and rewarding part of the game. * Maximizes active participation and minimizes inactivity and boredom. * Reflects the philosophy of player development expressed in Red Bulls' playing style (high energy press/counter press) **2025 LOCATIONS** ------------------ CRANFORD REC CENTER (Cranford, NJ)

Discover the magic of the Art Barn this summer!

Let your kids unleash their creativity in this idyllic carriage house art studio.

**What makes Art Barn so special?**

Art Barn is a unique and charming art studio nestled in the beautiful town of South Orange, NJ. Built in 1892, this historic carriage-house-turned-art-studio combines an intimate and cozy setting with the perfect balance of indoor and outdoor activity. The occasional wildlife sighting, from adorable bunnies to gentle fawns, add to the studio's charm, making each visit feel magical. The Ohemeng family lovingly restored the barn in 2018, transforming it into an inviting space that has been recognized in national publications such as Better Homes and Gardens and House Beautiful, as well as the beloved neighborhood publication, Matters Magazine. Most importantly, Christine and the Art Barn staff are warm and welcoming and see to it that each camper feels seen, heard, and included.

**What makes Art Barn so special?**

Art Barn is a unique and charming art studio nestled in the beautiful town of South Orange, NJ. Built in 1892, this historic carriage-house-turned-art-studio combines an intimate and cozy setting with the perfect balance of indoor and outdoor activity. The occasional wildlife sighting, from adorable bunnies to gentle fawns, add to the studio's charm, making each visit feel magical. The Ohemeng family lovingly restored the barn in 2018, transforming it into an inviting space that has been recognized in national publications such as Better Homes and Gardens and House Beautiful, as well as the beloved neighborhood publication, Matters Magazine. Most importantly, Christine and the Art Barn staff are warm and welcoming and see to it that each camper feels seen, heard, and included.

![Image 1: A tent](https://www.nps.gov/lake/planyourvisit/images/hero_lv_bay_camp_1145_1.jpg?maxwidth=1300&maxheight=1300&autorotate=false)

Start your Adventure

Spend your next camping adventure on the lake. With over 900 camping and RV sites at 15 different locations, there is a variety of desert and lakeside landscapes sure to please everyone. Lake Mead National Recreation Area's campgrounds offer restrooms, running water, dump stations, grills, picnic tables and shade. RV's, trailers and tents welcome. Concessioner campgrounds, including recreational vehicle hook-ups, are also available within the park.

Camp Bullfrog Lake
The boathouse and lake at Camp Bullfrog Lake.

Camp Bullfrog Lake offers year-round camping, group activities and water-based recreation such as kayak rentals and fishing. Camp steps from the water in the heart of the vast, hilly Palos Preserves and fill your days with hiking, mountain biking and birdwatching adventures.

Accessible Campsites & Amenities

Accessible campsites are designed for campers with disabilities. Please only book an accessible campsite if you need it or all other campsites are booked. Camp Bullfrog Lake features:

Accessible tent campsites (campsites #6 & #7) with accessible parking, path of travel to and around the campsite, raised fire pit and accessible picnic table.
Accessible RV/tent campsites (campsites #12 & #14) with accessible parking, path of travel to and around the campsite, raised fire pit and accessible picnic table.
Accessible large cabins (cabins #6 & #7) with accessible parking, path of travel to cabin, roll-in shower with bench, accessible sink, raised fire pit and accessible picnic table.
Accessible small cabins (cabins #8 & #9) with accessible parking, path of travel to cabin, raised fire pit and accessible picnic table.
Kayak rentals with an accessible launch/landing. Private boats are not allowed on Bullfrog Lake.
Accessible fishing pier with accessible parking, a paved surface pathway to the shoreline, and railings along the fishing pier.
Accessible bathroom/shower building with a roll-in shower with a bench as well as an accessible changing area with a bench.

Fishing at Bullfrog Lake

This 16-acre lake has a maximum depth of 9.9 feet. Two bump-outs are located on the eastern shoreline. Fishing within the campground (along the southwestern shoreline) is restricted to registered campers only.

There is an accessible fishing pier on the southwestern side of the lake with accessible parking, a paved surface pathway to the shoreline, and railings along the fishing pier.

Kayak Rentals & Accessible Landing

Registered campers can rent kayaks from the camp office to launch at the accessible landing. Private boats are not allowed on Bullfrog Lake.

Single kayak: $10/hr
Tandem kayak: $15/hr

Call 312-636-9785 for more information on availability.

Boat rentals are also available at the Maple Lake Boating Center, located just east of the camp across Wolf Rd.

Things to do at this park

Reserve your standard, partial or full hookup campsite early to experience this social camping pulse with life in the summer. Generations of families continue to enjoy the blue lake ever year, as will first-timers.

Soak in the landscape from an adventurous trail, a picnic table or the one kitchen shelter. If water fun is more your style, enjoy boating, fishing, water skiing and windsurfing on the 50-mile long lake.

Winter schedule

Learn about seasonal closures and operational changes during the off-season on the Winter Schedule page.

Food and grocery
Paninis in the Park

Serving up a great selection of hot food, beverages, ice cream treats and espresso to enjoy during your visit. In addition, they also carry a variety of camp supplies including ice and firewood. Open 8 - 8 daily through Labor Day. Click to view their Food and Drink Menu and Grocery Menu.

Kayak Rentals

Providing a variety of fun water rentals including, kayaks, SUPs, a SUP Squatch and hydro bikes. Located alongside Paninis in the Park. 

Interpretive opportunities

The park maintains a roadside monument on SR 97A at Earthquake Point. This monument describes an earthquake and landslide that occurred many years ago. The force of the quake was so great that a landslide blocked the Columbia River for several days.

Another monument stands one mile east of the park. At this site, in 1945, a school bus carrying the children of Southshore residents plunged into the lake after hitting rocks that had fallen onto the roadway. The bus driver and a number of children died in the accident. The monument was erected and is maintained by the families of the children.

# Sub-Page: About Camp Prospect — Camp Prospect
#### **Our Camp**

Located in Maplewood, New Jersey, Camp Prospect is a camp for pre-schoolers and rising kindergarteners. We offer a unique multi-age, play-based camp with hours of discovery through a mix of activities, music, experiments, outdoor play, special guests and more.

#### **The Camp Experience**

Each session’s activities, projects, special visitors, science, and art projects will be related to the session’s theme, offering a varied experience for campers all summer long! With a student to counselor ratio of 5:1, campers receive lots of personalized attention throughout the session.

#### **Community Service**

All campers will also take part in a service project that fosters community and compassion. Examples of projects we have done in the past include "stuffing" the Green Bean, making gifts for residents of Winchester Gardens, and collecting items for Interfaith Hospitality Network.

---

# Sub-Page: Testimonials — Camp Prospect
Happy campers & parents!
------------------------

Read what parents say. This summer is sure to be great!

Our daughter really enjoyed Camp Prospect! The staff was awesome and the campers were a great group of kids that our daughter enjoyed being with. We would recommend to everyone and sign up again at any opportunity!

Camp Prospect was my 3 year old’s first summer camp experience. He still talks about all the fun he had at “Camp School” and the friends that he played with there. He cannot wait to go back this summer. The teachers and helpers are fantastic and it’s just the right amount of time for a preschooler to be at camp on a summer day.

My little guy couldn’t wait to get to camp every morning. And after a super-fun morning—hanging in the playground, doing crafts, running through sprinklers—I couldn’t get him to go home! The staff was very warm, caring and attentive. He will be back!

I've had three children attend Camp Prospect and for their preschool and kindergarten years we wouldn't miss it. The staff and counselors are warm, kind, and engaging. They play outside and have so much fun - it is the perfect summer experience for these ages. We absolutely love Camp Prospect!

---

# Sub-Page: Policies — Camp Prospect
#### Eligibility

Camp Prospect is a camp for preschoolers and rising kindergarteners. Children attending Camp Prospect should be 3 years old by October 1 **or** be 2.5 years old by their first week of camp and have prior preschool experience. Children can attend up until the summer before they start kindergarten.

Please contact us at with any questions about your child's eligibility.

#### Make Up Policy

We are unable to reschedule or refund missed days of camp due to illness, travel, or other circumstances.

#### Potty Training

Children do not have to be potty-trained to attend camp. However, it is our policy to call a parent or caregiver to come in to change a child's dirty diaper.

### Story Links

**SEATTLE** - Seattle U baseball will host a summer prospect camp on July 30 and 31 at Bannerwood Park in Bellevue, WA. The camp, which is open to those in the 2025-28 high school graduating classes, will focus on all aspects of the game, with an emphasis on fielding, hitting, pitching.  
  
Led by head coach [Donny Harrel](https://goseattleu.com/sports/baseball/roster/coaches/donny-harrel/1430) and his staff, camper will have a chance to showcase their skills while being instructed and evaluated by the SU coaching staff.  
  
**What is the cost?**  
$259 for position and 2-way players

### Story Links

**DETROIT (8/19/2024) --** The University of Detroit Mercy softball team will host a prospect camp on Sunday, September 8, at Buysse Ballpark on the campus of UDM.  
   
The Titan coaching staff and players will work one-on-one with campers. Each athlete has the opportunity to showcase and develop their skills in a Division I softball environment, interact with the staff and players, and learn what it is like to play softball at the next level.   
   
The Titans Softball Prospect Camp is open to all participants in grades 9-12. It is designed specifically for passionate and elite players who express genuine interest in our program and want to get on our recruiting radar.  
  
Information and registration info below.   
  
**Cost:**  
Individual camper registration. $110.00   
  
**Date:**  
September 8, 2024 (Registration closes Sept. 7)  
   
**Time:**  
9:00 - 4:00 p.m. (Check in starts at 8:00 a.m.)  
  
**Location:**  
Buysse Ballpark \- on the campus of Detroit Mercy  
4001 W McNichols Rd, Detroit, MI 48221   
University of Detroit Mercy   
  
**Prospect Range:**  
Grades 9-12   
  
**Camp Schedule:**  
9:00-12 – Skills Session with current players and coaching staff.   
12-1 – Lunch (Not Provided)  
1:00-4:00 – 10 Inning Instructional Game

### Story Links

*   [Archuleta Baseball Camp - Prospect Camp Registration](https://archuletabaseballcamps.com/content/prospect-camp-registration)

**TERRE HAUTE, Ind.** – Indiana State head baseball coach Tracy Archuleta announced the 2024 fall prospect camp dates as Sycamore baseball will host two camps for 2025-28 high school graduates.  
   
The camp dates are set for September 8, 2024, and October 20th, 2024, with both camps set to be held at Bob Warn Field.  
   
The Prospect Camp will provide an opportunity for some of the best players in the area to showcase their skills directly in front of the ISU coaching staff. ISU coaches will be providing an evaluation of the potential student-athletes.  
   
Campers will be instructed on hitting, pitching, baserunning and defensive play while also going through a pro-style workout to showcase their skills in front of the Indiana State Baseball Staff.  
   
For more information on the Fall Prospect Camps or to register, click the link [**here**](https://archuletabaseballcamps.com/content/prospect-camp-registration).  
   
**Follow the Sycamores**

You can also find the team on social media including [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/SycamoreBaseball), [Twitter](https://twitter.com/indstbaseball), and [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/indstbaseball/).  Fans can also receive updates on Sycamore Athletics by downloading the March On App from both the [App Store](https://indiana-state.app.link/launch) and the [Google Play Store](https://indiana-state.app.link/launch).

Our Programs
------------

### **Pre-K3 to Kindergarten**

The Clubhouse
-------------

The Clubhouse is a wonderful introduction to the summer camp experience for campers aged three, four and five years olds. They are introduced to arts and crafts, sports, cooking, nature, swimming and other fun activities geared to their age and ability that encourage growth, confidence and learning. Clubhouse campers also have the option of coming three, four or five days a week.

[Learn About The Clubhouse](https://campriverbend.com/clubhouse/)

[A Day in the Life: Clubhouse](https://campriverbend.com/clubhouse#video)

### **Grades 1 to 8**

Riverbend Experience
--------------------

Campers entering 1st through 8th grades explore, grow and gain confidence! During the day, each group rotates through seven different activities and has many new experiences. There are days packed full of fabulous activities and fun for kids; this is the place to make new friends and life-long memories!

[Learn About Riverbend Expererience](https://campriverbend.com/riverbend-experience/)

[A Day in the Life: Riverbend Expererience](https://campriverbend.com/riverbend-experience#video)

### **Grades 7 to 9**

Day Trippers
------------

The Day Trippers program takes young teens out of camp and on the road for day trips and short overnight trips in our region. You’ll find us down at the beach and up in the mountains. We’ll be boating, cooking, climbing, seeing the sights and exploring the world!

[Learn About The Day Trippers](https://campriverbend.com/teen-adventures/)

[A Day in the Life: Day Trippers](https://campriverbend.com/day-trippers#video)

[Want to visit? Call us: 908-580-CAMP](https://campriverbend.com/#)

# Sub-Page: New Jersey Summer Day Camp in Warren, NJ | Camp Riverbend
Our Programs
------------

### **Pre-K3 to Kindergarten**

The Clubhouse
-------------

The Clubhouse is a wonderful introduction to the summer camp experience for campers aged three, four and five years olds. They are introduced to arts and crafts, sports, cooking, nature, swimming and other fun activities geared to their age and ability that encourage growth, confidence and learning. Clubhouse campers also have the option of coming three, four or five days a week.

### **Grades 1 to 8**

Riverbend Experience
--------------------

Campers entering 1st through 8th grades explore, grow and gain confidence! During the day, each group rotates through seven different activities and has many new experiences. There are days packed full of fabulous activities and fun for kids; this is the place to make new friends and life-long memories!

### **Grades 7 to 9**

Day Trippers
------------

The Day Trippers program takes young teens out of camp and on the road for day trips and short overnight trips in our region. You’ll find us down at the beach and up in the mountains. We’ll be boating, cooking, climbing, seeing the sights and exploring the world!

# Sub-Page: Legacy & Tradition | Camp Riverbend
### **Camp Riverbend has hosted generations of families for over 60 years in Warren Township, New Jersey**

Founded by Marianne and Harold Breene in 1962, Camp Riverbend is a family affair. The four Breene children—Roger, Jill, Paul and Robin, and daughters-in-law Debbie and Miriam, now run the camp, and the newest generation of Breene great-grandchildren are becoming campers! Each member of the family is here to provide a personal, hands-on camp experience you’ll never forget! Camp Riverbend is proud to be accredited by the American Camp Association, and has been since its very first season. Camp Riverbend traditions create lifelong memories for campers. Watch the video to learn more!

Our Philosophy
--------------

Our philosophy builds “**confidence, not competition**!” We honor each camper’s talents and efforts. Camp Riverbend is a place where each child can be themself, explore the world and learn new skills in a fun and supportive environment.  We encourage every camper to participate in all activities and we applaud every achievement – from a camper’s first at-bat to a grand-slam home run!

Camp Map & Location
-------------------

Located in beautiful Somerset County, just 35 minutes from NYC, Camp Riverbend sits on a 30-acre site along the Passaic River. The environment is perfect for explorers of all ages, with vibrant woods, open fields, nature trails, a wetlands sanctuary, athletic facilities and the river bank. Take a look at all the activities and amenities Camp Riverbend has to offer!

# Sub-Page: Activities | Camp Riverbend
Camp Riverbend is located along the gentle Passaic River in Warren Township New Jersey. With approximately 30 acres, Camp Riverbend has shady woods, open fields, nature trails, a wetlands sanctuary and a variety of athletic fields. Take a look at all the activities and amenities Camp Riverbend has to offer!

Swimming
--------

We are very proud of our exceptional swim program.

Swimming is one of the most important skills to be learned at camp. Our five heated, crystal-clear pools are designed for teaching campers at all levels. The pools go from a depth of 1 foot to 11 feet so everyone feels comfortable.

Campers enjoy swimming twice a day\*, in the morning for instruction and in the afternoon for “free swim”. Our experienced staff of lifeguards and water safety instructors supervises the waterfront. Watch the video to learn more! (\*Three-quarter day campers swim once a day)

Sports
------

At Camp Riverbend our campers enjoy a complete sports program that emphasizes learning new skills, sportsmanship and team cooperation. Our sports programs help campers discover new abilities and gain a sense of achievement and success in whatever they try.  Coaches oversee and instruct sports activities in camp. Watch the video to learn more!

Adventure Course & High Ropes
-----------------------------

Our high ropes challenge course is a very popular way to teach and build trust, strong self-esteem and empower campers.

Our High Ropes course features a 30-foot tower with three different climbing challenges. A wire bridge high in the trees and a zip line provide physical challenges and exciting thrills. We also have a circuit up in the trees with a number of different elements.  In addition, there is a zip line, climbing wall and burma bridge just for our 3-5 year old campers

The newest addition is mid-level elements, too! Watch the video to learn more!

Pedal Karts
-----------

Campers ranging in age from pre-school through 8th grade can challenge themselves on our paved pedal kart track or can go “off-road” on our outdoor track through the woods.  We have pedal karts of all designs and sizes that look like go karts but are pedaled like a bike.

Spray Park
----------

Campers just love our water spray park! The unique water structures are designed for creative fun with elements that pour, dump and spray water. The Spray Park is a fun way for campers to cool off on hot summer days!

River Activities
----------------

The gentle riverbank of the Passaic River makes a great area to set our canoes and kayaks into the water, where all of our campers learn the fundamentals of safe boating from certified instructors.

Arts & Crafts
-------------

At Camp Riverbend we are proud of our extensive Arts and Crafts offerings. Campers can express their individuality and creativity through arts & crafts, ceramics, pottery, jewelry making, lanyard and woodworking lessons. Children learn new techniques for artistic fulfillment. Watch the video to learn more!

Ninja Course
------------

Camp Riverbend has a Ninja Warrior training course for all campers, large and small, with these challenging elements:

Stepping Stones, The Tunnel, The Terrace, Monkey Bars/Tumbling Dice, Rubble Over and Under, Box Jump, Curved Wall, Wooden Balance Beam, Tire Run, Tight Wire, Apex Ladder

Nature
------

The Nature program at Camp Riverbend introduces campers to the wonders of the world around us. We explore birds, animals, insects and plants in the various habitats throughout our camp site. Campers do basic science experiments to learn about wind, the sun, water and soil. Our Nature program encourages campers to treasure the natural world and take care of it through conservation, recycling and smart energy use.

Cooking
-------

Whether at the Chef’s Kitchen or Clubhouse Cooking, each week campers get to learn the basics of cooking by creating some delicious treats. Yum! The fun can continue at home, as Camp Riverbend provides Recipes of the Week like Apple Pie Bites, Golden Graham S’mores Bars, Pizza Rolls, Watermelon Salsa and Cinnamon Tortilla Chips & Berry Frozen Yogurt just to name a few…

(Recipes are adjusted to accommodate campers’ dietary restrictions.

Performing & Circus Arts
------------------------

Camp is a great place for children of all ages to explore performing arts. Our Performance program introduces campers to many techniques of performance, including improv, mime, puppetry, movement, directing, and working with props and costumes. Our Circus program introduces campers to the magic of the Big Top with juggling and clown skills. Both take place in our air-conditioned Studio.

Camper Choice
-------------

As campers get older they have the opportunity to choose more of the activities they like best. Our Club program for campers 1st – 8th grades, before or after lunch Monday – Thursday, is very flexible, and campers can switch clubs every day. In Tracking, rising 4th & 5th grade campers choose activities to explore in depth twice a week; in Superchoice, rising 6th – 8th grade campers pick their own individualized schedule of activities three times a week. With this type of flexibility campers can explore all the activities Camp Riverbend has to offer!

Indoor Facilities
-----------------

In case of rainy days, campers have plenty of indoor spaces to choose from, including the Studio, the Big Barn, Auditorium, Roller Rink, Dining Pavilion & Game Pavilion. Most of our indoor locations, including all Clubhouse cabins, are air-conditioned. Others program areas are sheltered by tents or awnings.

Our Game Pavilion, continually supervised, is the place where campers play ping pong, foosball, air hockey, bumper pool, knock hockey, billiards and other table games. Campers may go to the Game Pavilion instead of free swim in the afternoon if they choose.

Each group has a locker room, where campers change into and out of their swimsuits, and can also shelter from inclement weather.

# Sub-Page: Transportation | Camp Riverbend
For the 2025 season, all bus service will be at neighborhood or centralized bus stops, with the exception of three-quarter day afternoon bus drop offs.

Camp tuition includes either bus transportation or a place in the extended day program. Campers travel in small or large yellow school buses; each bus has a riding counselor to supervise campers during the bus route and everyone wears a seat belt.

Every bus driver has a Commercial Driver’s License with Passenger and School Bus endorsements.  To earn this license, drivers must undergo a physical exam and have significant knowledge and on-road testing for safety.  Bus drivers’ safety records are reviewed each season.

We try to arrange our bus routes so each camper’s trip is as short as possible. Most bus routes begin around 8:00 am and arrive at Camp around 8:45 am. We dismiss at 4:00 pm and almost all buses have delivered their campers home by 4:45 pm.

For the 3 and 4 year old three-quarter day Clubhouse program, morning transportation to camp is included in tuition; Camp provides bus service back to Summit, New Providence, Berkeley Heights and Westfield at 2:00 pm.  For campers in other towns, a parent or guardian must pick up three-quarter day Clubhouse campers at 2:00 pm.

If the timing of the bus does not work for your schedule, we also offer an extended day option.  You can bring your camper here as early as 8:00 am and pick up as late as 6:00 pm. Counselors supervise extended day campers in games, swimming, crafts, sports and quiet activities.

There is no extra fee for the extended day program if you use it instead of bus transportation.  There is a small extra charge to use both extended day and bus service, or bus service to two different addresses.

# Sub-Page: Lunch & Menu | Camp Riverbend
Safety & Security
-----------------

Camper safety is our number one priority, and we are committed to keeping Camp Riverbend as safe and secure as possible!

We exceed all standards of the New Jersey Youth Camp Safety Act, and through the American Camp Association we keep current with the newest developments in camp safety and operations. We undergo rigorous annual inspections by local and state officials who evaluate every aspect of Camp Riverbend including sanitation, transportation, food safety, staff qualifications, fire prevention and medical record keeping.

Visitation Policy
-----------------

Parent visits are not allowed during the camp season.

Our security staff at the camp entrance checks all adults who arrive at camp.

Our Camp Nurse
--------------

Our on-site camp nurse treats minor injuries that occur during the day, such as bug bites and scrapes.

A camper who feels sick or is injured will first go to the Nurse’s office to be evaluated. In case of serious illness or injury, the nurse will contact the child’s parents to pick the child up. Otherwise, the nurse will treat the child with over-the-counter, or prescription medications that have been authorized by the parents. Our camp doctor is on call.

**Sibling Discount**: For the 2nd child in your family, deduct $300 from the seven or six week tuition, $250 from the five week tuition, $200 from the four or three week tuition, or $150 from the two week tuition. For a 2nd child who is a Three-Quarter Day camper, deduct $250 from the seven or six week tuition, $200 from the five week tuition, $150 from the four or three week tuition, or $100 from the two week tuition. For a 3rd child in your family, deduct $600 from the seven or six week tuition, $500 from the five week tuition, $400 from the four or three week tuition, or $300 from the two week tuition.  For a 3rd child who is a Three-Quarter Day camper, deduct $500 from the seven or six week tuition, $400 from the five week tuition, $300 from the four or three week tuition, or $200 from the two week tuition.  For a Three-Quarter Day camper who attends less than 5 days a week, the sibling discount will be reduced proportionally.

**July 4 Holiday Discount:**  If you enroll only for the first two weeks of camp (the weeks of June 30 and July 7), deduct $300 from the total tuition.  For the 3 and 4-year old Three-Quarter Day program, deduct $175 from the total tuition if you sign up for only the first two weeks of the season and for five full days each of those weeks.

**Referral Discount:** If you refer a first-time family to Camp Riverbend, they should list your name when they apply under “Which family referred you to Camp Riverbend” on the application form. You earn a $100\* discount for your summer tuition for each first-time camper from a first-time family that enrolls and has listed your name. This discount does not apply to enrollment of returning campers or siblings of returning or current campers. Discount is not valid if first-time family/camper drops out before attending camp. First-time families may list only one referring name. Discount may only be applied toward paid tuition in that camp season. \*$50 discount for referred Three-Quarter Day camper.

**Application Policy:** Campers must apply for at least two consecutive weeks. Each camper’s application requires a $500 initial tuition payment which will only be charged if the camper is subsequently enrolled. There is no charge if you are waitlisted.  Submitting an application does not guarantee enrollment.  A camper will be enrolled once you receive an email from Camp Riverbend confirming that your initial payment has been processed.

Once a camper is enrolled, $200 of this payment becomes non-refundable as a registration fee. We require a second tuition payment of $1500 per child on January 6, 2025.  The final tuition payment is due on April 1, 2025.

Weeks and friend requests must be finalized by January 6, 2025, and all tuition payments made prior to and on or after that date are non-refundable, regardless of dropouts or reductions in weeks prior to or during the camp season.

There is a 2.9% fee for credit card payments; there is no charge for EFT or debit card payments.

We will gladly set up a payment plan with you if you are paying by EFT/echeck or credit card; all payments under such plans must be made by April 1, 2025.

Each camper’s tuition includes either bus transportation to and from camp OR a place in our extended day program at camp (8:00-9:00 am and 4:00-6:00 pm).  There is an additional fee if your family wants to use bus transportation AND extended day daily. For the 3 and 4 Year Old Three-Quarter Day program, transportation to camp is included in tuition; with a sufficient number of Three-Quarter Day campers in a town, we will provide afternoon bus service at 2:00 pm. Otherwise, a parent or care provider must pick up these campers at 2:00 pm

Staff & Groups

Prospective counselors undergo a rigorous screening process. All staff members, new and returning, are trained before Camp starts. This training teaches safety rules, techniques for working with children, and fun games and activities to share with campers.

There is one counselor for every 5 campers throughout Camp.

Each group of 16-18 campers has two counselors for first graders and older.  
Clubhouse groups have three counselors.

Senior staff members supervise seven to twelve camper groups and spend time with campers.

Yes, if the friend is the same sex and in the same grade as your child (Clubhouse groups and young teen groups are co-ed).  
On the application form there is a space where you can list friends with whom your child would like to spend the summer.

Camp Riverbend has a no-tipping policy for all camp staff.

Camp Activities
---------------

Our instructors teach a wide variety of skills in creative crafts, swimming, team & individual sports, performing arts, team building and nature.  
Our PIY (“Pick It Yourself”) program gives each group time to choose their favorite activities.

For more information, .

Campers entering first grade & up choose their favorite activities during club time before or after lunch Monday through Thursday.

Rising 4th and 5th graders choose a cluster of three related activities in our Tracking program for Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.

Rising 6th – 8th graders choose three individual activities to explore intensively in our SuperChoice program for Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoons.

Each Friday is a special day, with performing artists, parades or counselor talent shows. In years past we have imported “snow” for sledding in July, built and raced cardboard boats, and served giant pizza-sized pancakes. Every Friday is super fun!  See our for more details.

We pride ourselves on our excellent swim instruction program.

Each camper has a swim lesson every day.

Children are placed in lessons based on their swimming ability. Lesson groups are small, with about 6-8 campers, taught by a swimming instructor and a group counselor assisting.

The waterfront has 5 crystal-clear heated pools, designed for teaching children at all swim skill levels.

Our committed team of Red Cross certified Lifeguards and Water Safety Instructors supervise the pools at all times.

We have indoor locations for all campers on rainy days. We continue with our regular program inside.

Food
----

Camp Riverbend provides daily lunch for all campers – kid favorites and healthy choices approved by our Camp Riverbend Dietician, with options every day.

Our kitchen is “allergy aware.” We do not serve any tree nut or peanut products and can accommodate a variety of food allergies, such as: gluten, dairy, sesame and egg allergies.

All campers have an ice cream or ice pop treat as they wrap up their day.

For more information, .

Yes!  Campers can stop by the Snack Shack mid-morning or mid-afternoon for small packaged snacks, such as goldfish crackers, pretzels, popcorn, fresh fruit and fresh veggies!  All campers have an ice cream treat as they wrap up their day. As always at Riverbend, all snack items offered are tree nut and peanut free. Gluten-free items are also be available. Snacks are included in camp tuition.

We allow campers to bring food from home for lunch, however we do not permit sharing with other campers, and nothing with tree nuts or peanuts is allowed. For birthdays, we request that you send in only non-edible party favors for the group.

Visiting, Safety & Security
---------------------------

A camper who feels sick will go to the nurse, who evaluates his or her condition. In case of serious injury or illness, the nurse will contact the child’s parents to pick the child up.

Our Camp nurse treats minor injuries that occur during the day, such as bug bites and scrapes, and administers any prescription and over-the-counter medication that has been authorized by a camper’s parents

When applying, parents must select a secret password. No camper will be released to any adult without the password.

Any adult picking up a camper from Camp must give the camper’s password before the child is released to them.

Our security staff at the front of the property checks all visitors.

Camper safety is our number one priority! We are committed to keeping Camp Riverbend as safe and secure as possible.

We undergo rigorous inspections annually for safety by local and state officials, who evaluate every aspect of Camp, including sanitation, transportation, food safety, staff qualifications, fire prevention and medical record keeping.

We are accredited by the American Camp Association and the New Jersey Department of Health. Through the American Camp Association, we keep current with the newest developments in camp safety and operations

No parent visits are allowed.

The Breene Family has owned and and operated Camp Riverbend since 1962. The current owners are Roger Breene, Jill Breene Cheng, Paul Breene and Robin Breene Hetrick. The four of them, along with Roger’s spouse, Debbie Breene, and Paul’s spouse, Miriam Peretsman, supervise every aspect of the daily operation of Camp. Their involvement guarantees personalized attention to the needs of your family.

*   (908) 580-CAMP

*   (908) 580-2267

# Sub-Page: Welcome to The Clubhouse | Camp Riverbend
#### AGES 3-5

The Clubhouse is a wonderful introduction to the classic summer camp experience for campers ages 3-5 years old (rising pre-K and kindergarteners). All our Clubhouse campers are in co-ed groups in a designated area of the camp built just for them. Everything is kid-sized, right down to the chairs and the athletic field, so they are right at home and comfortable!

The Clubhouse daily schedule alternates between quiet and dynamic activities and includes a rest time after lunch. Swimming is an important part of each day, with group instruction each morning and a “free” swim in the afternoon for splashing around and having fun (three-quarter day campers have a “free” swim immediately after their morning lesson). Other fun activities for our Clubhouse Campers include: sports, crafts, cooking, canoeing and nature.

Three-Quarter Day Programs  
for Three and Four Year Olds
---------------------------------------------------------

Our youngest campers may come three, four or five partial days a week from  
9:00 am – 2:00 pm and experience all the fun of Camp Riverbend! Campers must be toilet trained.

Full-Day Program  
for Four and Five Year Olds
----------------------------------------------

Children entering their last year of preschool or Kindergarten and ready for a full day at camp attend our regular full-day, week-long program.

Supervision
-----------

Three counselors supervise about 16 boys and girls in each Clubhouse group. Smaller groups have two counselors.

The head group counselors are educators with experience in early childhood education.  The assistant group counselors are college and older high school students who really enjoy being with young children. We nurture our Clubhouse campers with lots of individual attention and age-appropriate fun and exploration.

#### Contact Us

Campers entering 4th & 5th grades choose their own afternoon schedules twice a week in our tracking program. Campers entering 6th, 7th and 8th grades choose their own individualized afternoon schedules three times a week with “SuperChoice.”

# Sub-Page: Day Trippers | Camp Riverbend
#### GRADES 7-9

Welcome to the Day Trippers!
----------------------------

Day Trippers is an option for boys and girls currently in 6th – 8th grades who want to be home each night. This program gives teens a safe and supportive environment for learning social skills and independence, along with the excitement of new activities all around our tri-state area.

Children currently in 6th and 7th grades can participate in our in-camp program or Day Trippers, or a combination of both (pending availability).

Day Trippers Program
--------------------

The group takes day trips every day, traveling on a regular camp bus.  For summer 2025, we’re planning trips to the Jersey shore, amusement parks, volunteering, yoga, challenge courses, kayaking and paddleboarding, making art, water polo, martial arts, cooking, and many more fun activities.

Four days a week the Day Trippers return back to camp in time to go home on the regular bus or into the extended day program.  One night a week is a late night; parents must come to camp around 5:30 pm for pick up.

Supervision
-----------

The Day Trippers counselors are experienced, mature male and female teachers who work with and understand young teens.

Ben Appelbaum Day Camp Conference
---------------------------------

#### October 8th, 2024 | Camp Riverbend

Join the ACA, NY & NJ as we pay tribute to camp legend Ben Appelbaum’s enthusiasm and service to our industry through an event dedicated to day camp programs. Hosted by different camps each year, attendees take part in a guided tour of the host camp’s facility, giving staff an opportunity to bring new insight and ideas back to their own program.

Join us for the 2024 Ben Appelbaum Day Camp Conference, hosted by Camp Riverbend in Warren, NJ. Going back to our roots, the conference this year will focus on touring one incredible camp; seeing the facilities and learning about the program. We will also have targeted programming and loads of networking including lunch! We hope you will join us to tour camp, re-connect post camp with your peers and learn from each other.

**Broadway STARZ WEEKLY SessionS**
==================================

Our popular Broadway camp is back! This is a class where students will work together to create and perform a show based on a new theme each week! At the end of the week, we ask our parents to join the last 15 minutes of camp to see what we have learned! Students will unleash their creativity where they will learn to collaborate on telling a story through movement and song. Join us each week for a new adventure! Classes run Monday through Friday from 9:30am - 12:30pm. Classes are for ages 3-6, drop-off only. All students must be potty trained. There is no class on Friday 7/4.

There is a $100 non-refundable deposit due upon registration. This deposit can be transferred to another camp if you need to change weeks.

**Program is $350 per weekly session, and a one-time 2025 Summer enrollment fee of $35.**

archives.") \> Camps Programs -------- Camps ----- It's camp time at CHA! ---------------------- We have 9 weeks of summer camp plus multiple mini camps throughout the year! ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- **CHA Family Membership is required for all camp activities**. Memberships are valid for one year and can be purchased [here](https://interland3.donorperfect.net/weblink/weblink.aspx?name=corahart&id=2) or at the same time as your camp registration. Campers must be at least 4 years old and able to use the bathroom alone at the start of a camp session, no exceptions.
Squirrel Scouts
4 year olds and Kindergarteners
Explorers
1st and 2nd graders
Naturalists
3rd and 4th graders
April Mini Camp --------------- April 14-18, 2025 ----------------- **Squirrel Scouts:** 9 AM-Noon[![Image 3](https://hartshornarboretum.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WhatsApp-Image-2024-08-21-at-9.58.25-AM-4.jpeg)](https://hartshornarboretum.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WhatsApp-Image-2024-08-21-at-9.58.25-AM-4.jpeg) $75/day or $350/week +$20/day for Kindergarten Extension **Explorers:** 9 AM-3 PM $95/day or $450/week Spring time at the Arboretum give campers chance to explore new growth in the forest. From tiny flowers to newly hatched insects, the forest is teeming with life at this time of year. During this camp week, children will identify signs of spring, search for plants and animals throughout the forest, and enjoy the warm weather in the woods. All programs are taught by seasoned environmental educators and include activities such as guided hikes, crafts, games, story time, and animal encounters. All campers should bring a snack and an extra set of clothes. Please ensure campers are dressed for the outdoors. Explorers and kindergarteners in extension should also bring a lunch. Pre-registration, health forms, and membership are required. You can register for one day or the whole week. [Register Here](https://hartshornarboretum.org/camp-sign-in/) Registration opened February 1, 2025 June Mini Camp -------------- June 16-20 & June 23-27, 2025 ----------------------------- **Squirrel Scouts:** 9 AM-Noon[![Image 4](https://hartshornarboretum.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WhatsApp-Image-2024-08-07-at-2.17.15-PM-7.jpeg)](https://hartshornarboretum.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WhatsApp-Image-2024-08-07-at-2.17.15-PM-7.jpeg) $75/day or $350/week +$30/day for Kindergarten Extension **Explorers:** 9 AM-3 PM (Available June 23-27 only) $105/day or $495/week Summer is here are we can wait to explore the lush green forest! We are excited to offer two weeks of June mini camp for Squirrel Scouts and, for the first time, a week of Explorers June mini camp as well! This mini camp offers opportunities to experience nature through stories, crafts, games, scavenger hunts, hands-on science, and animal encounters. The forest is thriving at this time of year and we welcome campers to learn all about the living and non-living things that can be found in the woodlands at this time of year. All campers should bring a snack and an extra set of clothes. Please ensure campers are dressed for the outdoors. Explorers and kindergarteners in extension should also bring a lunch. Pre-registration, health forms, and membership are required. You can register for one day or the whole week. [Register Here](https://hartshornarboretum.org/camp-sign-in/) Registration opened on February 1, 2025 Summer Camp ----------- June - August 2025 ------------------ Close to nature, close to home.[![Image 5](https://hartshornarboretum.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/20230804_143208b-scaled.jpg)](https://hartshornarboretum.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/20230804_143208b-scaled.jpg) Provide your child with the gift of nature this summer! CHA’s Nature Discovery Camp is a place to not just learn about, but also experience nature through hands-on-science, themed story time, crafts, songs, and an abundance of time outside among the trees. With guidance from experienced environmental educators, campers will explore a variety of week long topics throughout the summer. All summer camp sessions require a full week of registration. Pre-registration and health forms are required. [Login/Register Here](https://hartshornarboretum.org/camp-sign-in/) Registration opened on February 1, 2025 at 6 AM Squirrel Scouts --------------- 4 year old to Kindergarteners 9am-12pm Kindergarten Extension Option until 3pm (for rising kindergarteners only) $350 per week +$150 per week for kindergarten extension
June 30-July 3
Animal Jobs

The animals are hard at work, so come on down to the arboretum to see just what they’re up to. Discover how ecosystems stay balanced with builders and clean up crews, as well as planters and pollinators. Learn about animals big and small that make a difference in the wild world around us. 

July 7-11
Plant Power

Trees, leaves, and flowers: do you know that plants have powers? Take a look into the life cycle of a plant, and explore the forest’s trees, shrubs, and wildflowers. Identify parts of plants and learn to distinguish between various species of plants in our forest. 

July 14-18
Incredible Invertebrates

Dive into the world of insects. Get outside and learn about their homes, body parts, and life cycles. Discover what makes various species similar and what makes them unique? What’s more – meet live insects like bees, butterflies, and beetles.

July 21-25
Habitats

What makes a good habitat? Learn all about different habitats around the world and what makes them the perfect place for various plants and animals to live. Get hands-on experience in our deciduous forest habitat and discover deserts, oceans, rainforests, and more through stories, biofacts, and play-based learning.

July 28-August 1

Brilliant Birds

“Soar” through the arboretum as you study birds and what makes them unique. Learn about their eggs, nest building, feathers, and specific adaptations that allow them to survive and thrive in the wild. Identify various species of birds that live in an around CHA during the summer months.

August 4-8

Art in Nature

Explore lines, patterns, symmetry, colors, and shapes that occur naturally in our world. Discover why art is important to scientists and how elements and principles help naturalists observe species. Each day, create works of art with, in, and inspired by nature. 

August 11-15
Water Week
Water is all around us, but where does it come from, and where does it go? Learn about the water cycle and ways in which water serves as a survival tool and enrichment. Don’t forget to cool down with water games and interactive water play. 
August 18-22
So You Want to Work at an Arboretum

Arboretums don’t run themselves! Learn what it takes to be a botanist, entomologist, forester, or a variety of other nature-based careers from the scientists themselves! Discover how these people keep our natural lands not only beautiful, but healthy as well.

August 25-29
Nature Detectives
Get your magnifying glass and notepad ready, because it’s sleuthing time! Inspect your surroundings and determine what wildlife has been hanging around. Learn about nature’s most wanted and track them down using your five senses!
[Login/Register](https://hartshornarboretum.org/camp-sign-in/) Explorers ------------ **Additional Camp Sessions Now Available!** 9am-3pm Rising 1st and 2nd Graders $495 per week
June 30-July 3
Metamorphosis
Spring and summer are full of growth and change. Familiarize yourself with the act of metamorphosis and study a variety of animals that go through this incredible process.
July 7-11
Brilliant Birds
“Soar” through the arboretum as you study birds and what makes them unique. Learn about their eggs, nest building, feathers, and specific adaptations that allow them to survive and thrive in the wild. Identify various species of birds that live in an around CHA during the summer months.
July 14-18
Senses
Can snakes smell? How do turtle hear? Using research and observation skills, answer these questions and more! Use your own senses of smell, touch, hearing, and sight to experience the natural world and determine ways in which animals’ senses differ from our own. 
July 21-25
Spineless Creatures
Dive into the world of invertebrates. Get outside and learn about their homes, body parts, and life cycles. Discover what makes various species similar and what makes them unique? What’s more, meet live creatures like bees, butterflies, beetles, and spiders.
July 28-August 1
Wonders of Water
Water is all around us, but where does it come from, and where does it go? Learn about the water cycle and ways in which water serves as a survival tool and enrichment. Don’t forget to cool down with water games and interactive water play.
August 4-8
Wonders of Water Week 2

Water is all around us, but where does it come from, and where does it go? Learn about waterways and the macroinvertebrates that inhabit them. Discover how water can be used as both a survival tool and enrichment. Don’t forget to cool down with water games and interactive water play.

*This week is combined with the Naturalists camp group

August 11-15
Spineless Creatures

Dive into the world of invertebrates. Get outside and learn about their homes, body parts, and life cycles. Discover what makes various species similar and what makes them unique? What’s more, meet live creatures like bees, butterflies, beetles, and spiders.

*This week is combined with the Naturalists camp group

[Login/Register](https://hartshornarboretum.org/camp-sign-in/) Naturalists -------------- 9am-3pm Rising 3rd and 4th Graders $495 per week
August 4-8
Wonders of Water
Water is all around us, but where does it come from, and where does it go? Learn about waterways and the macroinvertebrates that inhabit them. Discover how water can be used as both a survival tool and enrichment. Don’t forget to cool down with water games and interactive water play.
August 11-15
Spineless Creatures
Dive into the world of invertebrates. Get outside and learn about their homes, body parts, and life cycles. Discover what makes various species similar and what makes them unique? What’s more, meet live creatures like bees, butterflies, beetles, and spiders.
August 18-22
Community Science

From in-the-field experience to data collection, community science is the program for all science and nature-loving campers. Use scientific instruments and processes to observe the forest ecosystem. Then make and test hypotheses in search of answers to your own questions. 

August 25-29
Survival
If you were lost in the woods, how would you survive? Under the guidance of environmental educators, campers will learn basic skills including shelter building, map and compass orienteering, and first aid.

Our drop-off PreK 2 and 3 programs aim to help children socialize and improve their social-emotional learning and self-regulation. Our curriculum provides reading and math learning opportunities through play, developing a foundation for academic success in PreK, K, and beyond.

Classes cap at 5 children in each.

​​

Limited availability for remaining '24-'25 School Year! [Email to register!](mailto:info@curiouskidsnj.com?subject=Register%20for%20PreK%20Drop%20Off)

​​

Registration Open for '25-'26 School Year

​

​

​​​

Are you searching for the perfect full time preschool alternative that combines the best of learning and play in a nurturing and supportive environment? Look no further than our PreK 2 Drop Off & PreK 3 programs– two tailored options to suit your child's age and developmental stage!

​

For children aged 2 and up, our two-hour PreK 2 Drop Off provides a dynamic and innovative program designed to ignite their curiosity and prepare them for the exciting world of preschool and beyond! For children aged 3 and up, our four-hour PreK 3 offers an extended half day experience, allowing for deeper exploration and enrichment to further enhance their readiness for PreK 4, Kindergarten, and beyond!

​

All programs prioritize the social, emotional, and cognitive development of each child, embracing the concept of Maslow before Bloom. Before diving into academic content, we ensure that children's basic needs for safety, belonging, and emotional support are met. Guided by our qualified staff, children engage in enriching activities that promote socialization, improve social-emotional learning, and foster self-regulation – essential skills for successful learning and development.

​

Our curriculum is carefully crafted to provide learning opportunities in both reading and math through play, laying a strong foundation for future academic success. From art and music to science, our play-based activities provide children with endless opportunities to explore, create, and discover.

​

Each class is capped at 5 children, allowing for individualized attention and ensuring that every child's unique needs and interests are met. Whether your child is exploring their first steps away from their caretaker or diving into deeper levels of independence and confidence, our teachers are here to ensure that every child feels safe, secure, and supported as they embark on their learning journey.

Are you ready to give your child the gift of a fun and enriching preschool experience? Enroll them in our PreK 2 or 3 program today and watch as they blossom into confident, curious learners with the skills and confidence to succeed in school and beyond.

​

Spaces are limited – register now to secure your child's spot in the next school year. Contact us today to learn more about our curriculum, enrollment process, and schedule. We can't wait to welcome your child to our preschool community and embark on a journey of learning and discovery together!

Please Note Curious Kids' policies before registering:$50 yearly registration fee will be added to your account when you sign up for a class.  This fee will be charged yearly for our Drop Off schedule which runs September- August.

Curious Kids does not offer refunds under any circumstance.

Classes canceled because of dangerous travel conditions due to weather will be made up at the discretion of the owners.  Classes canceled because of a mandated closure will immediately go virtual.  Refunds/ Credit will not be offered for classes that are offered virtually.

If enrolling in our Preschool Workshop Drop Off program students who move on from the program before the end of the school year will incur a $250 termination fee.  Curious Kids does not offer trial classes.

Before enrolling make sure to read our waiver and other policies included in registration information.

# Main Page: summer camp — Diamond Gymnastics
Enrollment for the 2025 Summer Camp season will begin on Monday, February 3rd.

Please note that online enrollments will be submitted as “requests” and your cart will show zero. Once submitted, we will follow-up with you to confirm or deny the request. If approved, we will automatically process the $50/week/camper non-refundable deposit and provide the receipt.

### Diamond's 2025 **Summer Camp** is an 9-week program that runs from LATE JUNE through the end of August.  ALL of our camps can be attended for individual weeks or for all 9 weeks.

**Full Day Camp** is offered to boys and girls ages 5-12 years.  The camp operates Monday to Friday from 9:00am to 4:00pm.  Camp activities include gymnastics instruction, rock climbing, outdoor play, arts and crafts, water activities and more.  A great staff mixes instruction with fun, making for a Great Summer!

**Half-Day Mini Camp** is for 4, 5 and 6 year-olds and runs Monday to Friday from 9:00am to 1:00pm.  Gymnastics instruction, arts and crafts, creative indoor/outdoor games, story telling and more than a few surprises keep the little ones very active for the Summer!

**Half-Day Camp** for ages 7 to 11 is also available from 9:00am to 1:00pm. A popular recent addition to our summer season, campers will get to enjoy gymnastics, rock climbing, indoor field activities and outdoor backyard play. Great Fun!

### Diamond Camp IS where it's at for summer fun!

**2025 Summer Camp Weeks**

1.  June 23 - June 27
    
2.  June 30 - July 4 (4 days)\*
    
3.  July 7 - July 11
    
4.  July 14 - July 18
    
5.  July 21 - July 25
    
6.  July 28 - Aug 1
    
7.  Aug 4 - Aug 8
    
8.  Aug 11 - Aug 15
    
9.  Aug 18 - Aug 22
    
    \*pro-rated for 4 day week
    

**Cost per Week**

**\#  weeks attending**          **Full-Day / Half-Day**

1 week for 1 child          $450 / $295

2 - 3 weeks for 1 child         $430 / $280

4 - 5 weeks for 1 child          $410 / $265

8 - 9 weeks for 1 child  $355 / $235

Late pick up          $45 / -

10% discount for second child in family

### Preschool Gymnastics

#### Gym Kids (Walking – 5 YRS)

Gym Kids is a movement education and early gymnastics program right here in Park City. The curriculum consists of four different class levels. The focus is on the young child and his or her basic developmental needs. Our themed lessons change every two weeks and are specifically designed to inspire each age group to meet physical, cognitive, and social objectives in a fun-filled learning environment.

* * *

#### Diaper Daredevils (Walking – 2 YRS)

This is a coed adult & tot class for children from walking – 2 years of age. This class promotes early cognitive development, spatial awareness, and gross motor development. Curriculum uses music, colors, and numbers in addition to teaching props and apparatuses specifically designed for our little ones. A parent or adult age guardian must be present on the floor. We ask that you leave non-registered young children in the care of others during class time.  
[View Classes](https://blackdiamondgym.com/2025/01/14/preschool-gymnastics/#anchorclass)

* * *

#### Tumble Bugs (2 – 3 YRS)

This is a coed adult & tot class. Lessons are designed to foster early social development with other students, enhance fine and gross motor skill development, coordination and balance, as well as introduction to colors and letters. A parent or adult age guardian must be present on the floor. We ask that you leave non-registered young children in the care of others during class time.  
[View Classes](https://blackdiamondgym.com/2025/01/14/preschool-gymnastics/#anchorclass)

* * *

#### Tumble Bees (3 – 4 YRS)

This coed class is the first opportunity for children to experience independence from an adult partner under the guidance of a BDG instructor. In addition to creating a comfortable transition for the children, lessons are designed to increase strength and muscle control, develop fine and gross motor skills, as well as focus on hand-eye coordination and body awareness.

[View Classes](https://blackdiamondgym.com/2025/01/14/preschool-gymnastics/#anchorclass)

* * *

#### Tumble Frogs (4 – 5 YRS)

Students will be introduced to new gym apparatuses in an exploratory way in this coed class, preparing them for the next step in our gymnastics program. They will gain physical strength, flexibility, and mastery in their numbers and colors.  
[View Classes](https://blackdiamondgym.com/2025/01/14/preschool-gymnastics/#anchorclass)

* * *

# Main Page: Dingers NJ
SOFTBALL CAMP AT DINGERS
------------------------

#### DETAILS

*   **Dates:**  June 23, weekly through August 22, 2025 (9 weeks)
*   **Age Group:** 7-13
*   **Schedule:** Monday-Friday, 9:00am-3:00pm - check in begins at 830am.
*   **Location:** Maplecrest Park, Springfield Avenue, Maplewood.  **Indoor:** **DINGERS**, 50 Burnett Avenue, Maplewood. 
*   **Check-In:** Begins 30 minutes prior to the camp start time.
*   **Meals:** Bring your own lunch. Bring a water bottle.   

#### OVERVIEW

*   _**Coach Mia Testa**_ is back  and will be joined by present and former players from the Columbia High School squad!
*   Campers will spend the mornings at Maplecrest Park working on softball training and instruction with a focus primarily on hitting, fielding, base-running, and game situations including actual game play.   
*   After lunch the campers will enjoy various fun activities and games in the park and at the **DINGERS** facility.   

#### WHAT WE OFFER

*   **Supervision:** Campers are supervised by staff during camp hours with Low Camper to Instructor Ratio.
*   **Indoor/Outdoor facilities** - we won't have rain outs or heat advisory cancellations.
*   **HitTrax\*** softball simulation
*   **MAPLEWOOD POOL DAYS!** 
*   **DINGERS** T-Shirts, **DINGERS** Baseball Hats, and Other Prizes!
*   **ICE CREAM FRIDAYS!** 

#### PRE-CAMP CHECKLIST

Below is a suggested list of clothes, equipment, and personal items you will want to make sure you have!

*   Athletic clothing: t-shirt, shorts, softball pants (recommended)
*   Gym/baseball bag/backpack
*   Warm-up jacket for cooler mornings
*   Hat
*   Cleats & sneakers for indoor facility
*   Softball glove
*   Softball bat
*   Helmet and mask
*   Catcher’s gear (if applicable)
*   Sunscreen
*   Water bottle
*   Packed lunch and snacks 

#### POOL DAYS

Weather permitting, we are planning on 2 afternoons each week at the Maplewood Pool.  Campers not wishing to swim can enjoy other activities at the Pool.

#### AFTER CARE

Aftercare available at the DINGERS facility from 3p-6p.

Guest Services & Event Planner/Photographer

Baylee Dean

Baylee is an Arizona Native. She played softball growing up for both recreation and school. Her love for sports turned to the creative side of capturing the moment and telling stories through her camera lens. Expert photographer, Baylee was the Senior Photo Editor at Desert Vista High School and recently graduated. She is all about making your visit the best it can be and if you are looking for a great photographer, you have found her!

*   [![Image 5: Instagram](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/11062b_55e4be1e75564866b6c28290f9a9d271~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_25,h_25,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/11062b_55e4be1e75564866b6c28290f9a9d271~mv2.png)](https://www.instagram.com/peak.photographyaz/)

Guest Services & Softball Hitting Instructor

Raedyn Hedlund

Raedyn is a versatile softball player whose passion for the game started at the tender age of five. Excelling in both the outfield and on the pitcher's mound, Raedyn has showcased her talents in various competitive arenas—from the hustle of little league to the strategic plays in club games, and the high-energy challenges at Higley High School. Her #1 focus is our guests and she will ensure your experience is top notch!

![Image 7: bed7de0529.jpeg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/2ff817_e6a5e524aba547cbba488bb3bf232b8c~mv2.jpeg/v1/crop/x_0,y_0,w_960,h_813/fill/w_412,h_354,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/bed7de0529.jpeg)

Guest Services & Camp/Clinic Assist

Lindsay Hipke

Lindsey, a standout from Basha High, is a fierce competitor representing AZ Storm Tull 18U. Known for her swift infield tactics and precision on the field, she brings that same energy and dedication to every aspect of her interactions. Whether she’s in the game or off the field, Lindsey’s focus, enthusiasm, and passion shine through, guaranteeing that every guest feels not just welcomed but truly valued. A natural leader with a competitive spirit, she’s committed to creating positive, impactful experiences for everyone she meets.

![Image 8: IMG_9073_edited.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/2ff817_2804847d2d58466dbf24a4648ba7e629~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_412,h_354,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/IMG_9073_edited.jpg)

Guest Services & Camp/Clinic Assist

Mason Dean

Mason has been playing baseball since he was 3 years old. He is currently a Freshman at Desert Vista High School. He plays MIF on the Freshman baseball team as well as All 9 club team. When guests come in to the facility, his number one focus is taking care of them and providing a great experience!

![Image 9: BH4I7878.jpeg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/2ff817_c4de03aaea054071aedd663ac0925c3d~mv2.jpeg/v1/crop/x_0,y_159,w_1824,h_1566/fill/w_412,h_354,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/BH4I7878.jpeg)

Guest Services & Camp/Clinic Assist

David Poldoian

Currently a senior at Crismon High School, David has been a Varsity player since the program’s start, earning honors like All-Region MVP and All-Conference 1st Team. Next fall, he’s excited to continue his baseball career at Ottawa University Arizona while pursuing a business degree.

Off the field, he enjoys spending time with family and coaching with his dad. He’s thrilled to join the AZ Dingers team, sharing his love for the game and helping players grow their skills and passion for baseball!

![Image 10: IMG_3770_edited.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/2ff817_1f59886a58b04269bee28f6fd6ac6fdd~mv2.jpg/v1/crop/x_0,y_43,w_396,h_340/fill/w_412,h_354,al_c,lg_1,q_80,enc_avif,quality_auto/IMG_3770_edited.jpg)

Guest Services & Camp/Clinic Assist

Conner Cullen

Conner has been passionate about baseball since the age of 5! A Senior at Higley High School, he’s a proud third-year varsity player and also competes with the Scottsdale Dirtbags. Conner is a versatile utility player and a skilled switch hitter who brings his A-game to every inning. Known for his constant smile and upbeat personality, he's the kind of teammate that lifts everyone’s spirits both on and off the field!

# Main Page: HISTORY | FUNKY FUN ART
![Image 1: 100_1784_edited.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/305915_d275a36eb30d4cd3900b57172011c378~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_378,h_283,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/100_1784_edited.jpg)

Funky Fun Art started in March of 2014! Our first studio was in the craft room of The Baird in South Orange. Prior to its renovation the craft room was located on the first floor of The Baird and had easy access to the outdoors but only one window! This remained our home until December of 2018 when The Baird closed for renovations!

In December of 2018 Funky Fun Art moved to the 3rd Floor of The Woodland in Maplewood! The third floor needed a complete overhaul and the Funky Fun Art team got to work! Clearing the junk, painting, redoing the floors, redoing all of the lighting and adding in our special touches! Partnered with Maplewood the studio continued to thrive in 2019!

![Image 2: 78324_edited.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/305915_d5961284ec1f463698693a20facfa8b5~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_433,h_278,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/78324_edited.jpg)

![Image 3](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/305915_69fc55d6852d4666acfbbfc74355b532~mv2_d_2788_2018_s_2.jpg/v1/fill/w_433,h_314,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/305915_69fc55d6852d4666acfbbfc74355b532~mv2_d_2788_2018_s_2.jpg)

In February 2020 Maplewood decided to hire Denise and give her the position of Art Director for the town! Denise held this position until April 2024. The studio continued to grow and bring joy to so many SOMA children! After an unfortunate incident Denise decided to resign from Maplewood to find a safe space for her staff and program to continue!

In June of 2024 Funky Fun Art moved back to its original starting spot at The Baird in South Orange! The newly renovated building was the perfect spot to celebrate its 10 Year Anniversary! For the summer we will be using the stunning new third floor space!

COMING BACK HOME WAS A HUGE BLESSING! South Orange welcomed us back with open arms! We are so grateful!

![Image 4: IMG_20240125_161543.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/305915_af9607f642be4e9d8f6fe0b89f3061ad~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_477,h_215,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/IMG_20240125_161543.jpg)

![Image 5: Screenshot_20240123_143203_Instagram_edi](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/305915_5e7c18da3ac747daa58b2f7761f17880~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_421,h_341,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Screenshot_20240123_143203_Instagram_edi.jpg)

Funky Fun Art has grown into one of the leading art programs in the SOMA community! With over 40 employees made up of a variety of local creatives, former students, and a bunch of talented artists! You are always guaranteed to connect with someone on staff due to their wide range of skills, hobbies, interests, and personalities! We love creating a warm and inviting environment where everyone is welcome and met with kindness and love!

Funky Fun Art Offers:

Workshops

Summer Camp

Enrichment Classes

Holiday Workshops

Town Art Events

Public Art Pop-Ups

Custom Art Designs

Custom Art Events

Custom Art Parties

​

Contact us! We would love to plan something artsy for you!

​

[FunkyFunArtStaff@gmail.com](mailto:FunkyFunArtStaff@gmail.com)

908-635-1595

CAMP TUMBLESON LAKE
-------------------

#### **Day Camp**

#### **Ages 7-12**

![Image 5: Camp Tumbleson Lake](https://www.ymcanoco.org/sites/default/files/styles/hero_banner_mobile/public/2024-08/tumbleson-scenery4_0.jpg.webp?itok=q7mYf22x) ![Image 6: Camp Tumbleson Lake](https://www.ymcanoco.org/sites/default/files/styles/hero_banner_desktop/public/2024-08/tumbleson-scenery4_0.jpg.webp?itok=WmhDHKR_)

![Image 7: Tumbleson Day Campers](https://www.ymcanoco.org/sites/default/files/styles/ping_pong/public/2024-08/tumbleson-daycamp_0.jpg.webp?itok=i3XNLlV0)

Join us at the Y’s brand-new lakeside mountain day camp located just 20 miles from Boulder. YMCA Camp Tumbleson Lake is a beautiful 300-acre outdoor adventure camp that celebrates exploration, nature education and recreation.

Campers will get to experience many of the joys and adventures of traditional overnight camp while being able to come home each night with stories to share. Campers will grow their outdoor skills and knowledge while connecting with the camp community and building confidence and resilience… and of course, having a mountain of fun. YMCA Camp Tumbleson Lake will be unlike any day camp in Boulder County.

[Register](https://my.ymcanoco.org/s/registration?searchKeyword=Tumbleson%20Lake%20Day%20Camp)

**Dates:**

Monday-Friday weekly sessions run June 9 to Aug 8.  
_No day camp the week of July 4; we will offer a shortened residential camp that week._

**Weekly Session Pricing:**

Non-member $575, member $525

_Registration requires a $50 deposit per week of camp (goes towards balance for week). Parents/guardians will be charged a one-time $100 registration fee per child that covers all YMCA 2025 summer camps._

**Transportation:**

The Y will bus campers to and from camp each day; pick up and drop off available at the Lafayette and Boulder Ys.   
Lafayette Y: Bus departs for camp at 8am\*; 5:45pm camper pick-up  
Boulder Y:  Bus departs for camp at 8:40am\*, 5:15pm camper pick-up

\*Check-in will begin 20 minutes before departure.

_Please note: We do NOT provide lunch. We provide two snacks daily. Campers should bring a packed lunch daily._

![Image 8: Tumbleson Nature Trail](https://www.ymcanoco.org/sites/default/files/styles/ping_pong/public/2024-08/tumbleson-naturetrail_0.jpg.webp?itok=k5QsBhIg)

#### DAILY ACTIVITIES 

*   Water obstacle course 
*   Paddle sports and water play on our own lake 
*   Fishing 
*   Climbing, rappelling, bouldering, and low ropes 
*   Target sports: archery and slingshots 
*   Field games 
*   Mountain biking 
*   Nature/STEM, including NASA Globe curriculum 
*   Hiking/Leave No Trace 
*   Unit games (Capture the Flag, etc) 
*   Arts and Crafts 
*   Camp traditions, songs and chants 
*   And more!

### NEW THIS YEAR:

##### We are using a new platform for emergency medical information, medication information and waivers.

Once registered, you will be sent login information from CampDoc to provide us with your emergency and medical information. This profile must be completed 2 weeks prior to your child attending camp. Some medication administration will need additional time to work with our nurse and train staff.

# Main Page: Plan Your Visit: Locations, Hours, Admissions & Directions | Curious Kids' Museum & Discovery Zone - St. Joseph, MI
##### Curious Kids’ Museum, 415 Lake Boulevard & Curious Kids’ Discovery Zone, 333 Broad Street,

##### St. Joseph MI ~ 269-983-2543

##### \*A FEW THINGS YOU SHOULD KNOW BEFORE RESERVING YOUR TICKETS:

##### 1) We have TWO locations!!!! Make sure you’re reserving for your correct LOCATION, DATE and TIME!

##### 2) Admission: **Curious Kids’ Museum/$8 per person** (12 mos & up). **Curious Kids’ Discovery Zone/$6 per person** (12 mos & up). Yes, per person – adults are people too!

##### 3) We require online reservations all **Summer and every school break/vacation (including Thanksgiving/Christmas/Spring and Saturdays all year).** You’ll love the limited capacity!

##### 6)  Scroll & click for reservations AT THE LOCATION & DATE you’d like to visit. When the page changes, “Register” or “Sign in” in the **yellow header** _before_ choosing your date and time.
