Summer Camp
Summer Camp
Leadership. Confidence. Independence. Community. FUN!

We strive to provide summer camp programs that build campers' leadership, confidence, independence, and sense of community. Our camps are committed to providing opportunities for Girl Scouts in our council and beyond, creating and connecting a diverse sisterhood that helps campers unlock their potential and discover the world all while developing life skills and making memories and friendships that last a lifetime. Registration is now open for a Wild Summer Camp Experience! 

Join us at our Day Camp (The OVAL, Maplewood) or Sleepaway Camp (Camp Hoover, Middleville) for a week or more of outdoor fun, friendship and adventure!

We offer six full sessions - check out all the program options in the Camp Guide!

REGISTER NOW
Join us for the Summer of 2025
GSHNJ operates The OVAL, our day camp, in the South Mountain Reservation in Maplewood, and our sleepaway camp, Camp Hoover, in Middleville. Beyond the fun, friendship, and skill-building, the activities campers engage in at Girl Scout summer camp foster life skills they can’t gain elsewhere. We incorporate the Girl Scout Leadership Experience into everything we do, which means they’ll do more, grow more, achieve more, and leave ready to unleash their inner go-getter, innovator, risk-taker, and leader as they say, “I did that!”
Our camps provide a wide range of program options for campers entering kindergarten through 12th grade. There is something for everyone!
Anyone who identifies as a girl is welcome to participate in our summer camp programs regardless of race, religion, physical ability, economic status, or national origin.
Not a current Girl Scout not a problem! Sign up for a week (or more!) of camp and we will guide you through the Girl Scout registration process! Full instructions can also be found on page 28 in the Camp Guide.
Financial assistance is available for registered GSHNJ Girl Scouts and can be applied for during the registration process in UltraCamp.
Questions? Reach out to summercamp@gshnj.org – our team is ready and waiting to help you register your camper for summer!
Join us at a Tour or Open House!

Want to learn more about our camps (summer camp, programs, rentals, event opportunities, a la carte programs, and more)? Join us at one or more of our upcoming Tours/Open Houses!

Register using the links provided – we can’t wait to meet you!

 

	

The OVAL

	

Camp Hoover

Join Our Summer Camp Team!

Make a difference this summer—work at GSHNJ camps! Build skills, lead adventures, and inspire Girl Scouts.

APPLY NOW!

Why working at camp is right for everyone:

Looking to build a resume full of relevant skills that employers value ? Working at our summer camps helps you develop essential skills like:

Leadership
Communication
Teamwork
Creativity
Thinking on your feet
Decision-making

And the best part?  , You’ll make lifelong friendships!

Looking for an internship? Our camp directors may be able to help. Contact  summercamp@gshnj.org  for our day camp and Deb Hooker(dhooker@gshnj.org) for our sleepaway camp.

What are the benefits?

Discounts for your campers.
Certifications ranging from CPR/First Aid to Mental Health First Aid to Lifeguarding, at no cost to you.
Employee referral program – bring a friend and earn a bonus (your camp director can provide details and requirements)!
Opportunities for year-round per diem work.
Transportation to camp for day camp staff (ride the bus for free and get paid as a bus counselor!).

Want to know more about our camps?
Contact  summercamp@gshnj.org for our day camp and Deb Hooker(dhooker@gshnj.org) for our sleepaway camp.

APPLY NOW!
 
 
Can’t wait for the summer?

Stay tuned to our Event Calendar for exciting year-round programming! This is your chance to visit our camps, experience the outdoors, meet our staff, and  dive into the camp experience – both for you and your camper! Reach out to summercamp@gshnj.org to register and learn more.

 
Get to Know Us!

Are you looking to take your troop camping, planning for the summer, looking for an event location or family camping trip? Our three camps offer a variety of opportunities for you! We have facilities to host a family gathering, your next camping trip, a wedding, or special event.

Interested in taking a tour or  speaking with the Camp Director – email rentals@gshnj.org to learn more about what we offer, how to book your next event with us, and what we can provide to create a memorable experience for all.

 

Service Opportunities

Our camps are always looking for groups, troops, or individuals to help with projects and maintaining our sites. Corporations and partnerships are welcome, and we would love to connect to develop a lasting relationship.

Our three properties offer a wide array of projects that can be completed year-round. Projects include cleaning sites, making small repairs, painting, trail cleaning, carpentry projects, and more! These projects are essential to maintaining our camp properties and the hours worked can be applied to Hearts of Service. .

Troops interested in completing a High Award project are welcome to submit a fully prepared proposal for consideration.

 Ready to help at Camp Hoover? Reach out to Deb Hooker at dhooker@gshnj.org.For The OVAL and Camp DeWitt – reach out to  summercamp@gshnj.org

Introducing the January patch of the month: the Presidential Inauguration Patch!

The Presidential Inauguration Patch Program aims to help engage and educate Girl Scouts on the United States presidential inauguration process. From researching past presidential history to designing their own oval office and exploring the significance of this historic tradition, Girl Scouts can earn this special patch while learning about leadership, democracy, and the power of civic engagement.

Get started on earning your patch today!

[https://www.gscnc.org/.../Inauguration\_Patch\_Program\_FY24...](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gscnc.org%2Fcontent%2Fdam%2Fgscnc-redesign%2Forganized-forms-and-documents%2Fmembers%2Ffor-girl-scouts%2Fpatches%2FInauguration_Patch_Program_FY24.pdf&h=AT2AhxABZHKxNbrewGGcMg07tSbBLY9pEg0WHstJQ7Zr-g8pl-PoYoCVsPwVULp7U4lsmBXwXhg_AkVAuwb4Y1iPQVX9tY84d0vSQcbtLap4b3acFXs2aUlCUlnvHi8Uv-Tou2bEZjwUeAxTCdA50FehuaKsig1rFObVikjt&__tn__=-UK-R&c[0]=AT3J8u6sH7L6vO4eHQz4tL16rZpJ4c0OsIUn2xDr0CfnAAwoWV4PQvozlvo1Kw9Ot3RTPFq4_Zn88PpT-n6s6mqkdNaq0v3__E12tA7zcOMWAILbYBQCujmWLvvxAnGFk-jpjSq3RvKDA3z8Md7gH6ngB5rgd-PoVcz_kUyjLDijJKmCoSIwnvr13oL7lrSMhw)

To order that Presidential Inauguration patch email gsshop@gscnc.org or call 202-274-3312

Girl Scouts is a non-partisan organization that encourages education on civic duty and engagement within their communities.

\-

Presentamos el parche del mes de enero: ¡el parche de inauguración presidencial!

El Programa de Parches de Inauguración Presidencial tiene como objetivo ayudar a involucrar y educar a las Girl Scouts sobre el proceso de inauguración presidencial de los Estados Unidos. Desde investigar la historia presidencial pasada hasta diseñar su propia oficina oval y explorar la importancia de esta tradición histórica, las Girl Scouts pueden ganar este parche especial mientras aprenden sobre liderazgo, democracia y el poder del compromiso cívico.

Explore a Hidden Gem Girls Only Day Camp
========================================

The OVAL, a day camp nestled in the South Mountain Reservation in Maplewood, offers a touch of wilderness in Essex County. Surrounded by lush forests, rustic cabins, and an expansive field, The OVAL provides Girl Scouts with a blend of adventure, learning, and fun. Campers entering kindergarten through 10th grade explore activities like hiking, archery, and outdoor skills while building confidence, leadership, and friendships. With progressive programming that caters to all skill levels, The OVAL ensures every camper grows at their own pace. Led by dedicated staff rooted in Girl Scout values, this camp creates transformative summer experiences for children entering kindergarten through 10th grade.

# Main Page: Age Divisions — HARBOR HAVEN
![Image 1](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/8fd03196-04f5-4ffd-85c1-b7e179eee615/IMG_1472.JPG)

PROGRAMS FOR ALL AGES
---------------------

![Image 2](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/1ddb57c1-452f-4464-ac23-a970e1953dd7/IMG_1089.jpg)

Bright Beginnings
-----------------

#### (Ages 3-5)

### The proof is in the progress. Experience the difference.

Harbor Haven is especially known for our ages 3-5 programming.  "Bright Beginnings" is uniquely constructed to provide younger special needs children, with a comprehensive approach that supports them in all areas. This includes our learning center, social skills, speech, and occupational therapies.

**_Camp Activities_**

*   **_Swim Instruction_**
    
*   **_Water Play_**
    
*   **_School Readiness Reinforcement_**
    
*   **_Social Skills Training_**
    
*   **_Sensory Motor and Language Group_**
    

Bright Beginnings campers can attend a full day from 9 am-3:30 pm or a mini-day from 9 am-12 pm. Mini-day campers have the option to extend up to 2 afternoons. Special components will take place prior to 12 pm mini-day dismissal.

MAIN CAMP
---------

#### (Ages 6-15)

Lower Camp
----------

#### (Ages 6-8)

![Image 3](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/85114f88-ca42-4b90-867d-09d52bbd23ae/IMG_00A547250E01-1.jpg)

Lower Campers get to experience everything Harbor Haven has to offer including **swim time**, creative arts, sports of all sorts, karate, gymnastics, music, drama, bicycle riding/instruction, food fun, computers, Junior Clubhouse (the most amazing indoor playroom ever!), playground, social skills group and facilitation, learning center, speech & OT groups, and our special events!

Middle Camp
-----------

#### (Ages 9-12)

![Image 4](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/3686c59e-8424-4e8b-8aec-067a32ff7e33/IMG_A8D93ABB18BB-1.jpeg)

A special feature of Middle Camp programming is Hobbies. Hobbies feature a round of special fun that reflects appropriate age-trending hobbies and interests.

Middle Campers have **swim time**, creative arts, athletics, karate, yoga, music, drama, nature, bicycle riding/instruction, food fun, computers, special events, social skills group, Challenge Sector, learning center, speech & OT group, and Fun Zone!

![Image 5](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/37fc05e8-bd79-4ba1-851f-f28cc81d8c22/IMG_06DB0F23387F-1.jpg)

Upper Camp
----------

#### (Ages 13-15)

The excitement never stops for Upper Campers at Harbor Haven!  There is certainly no shortage of activities for Upper Campers - **swim**, creative arts, athletics, tennis, Gaga, karate, yoga, performing arts, special events, food fun, nature, bicycle riding, computers/media, social skills groups, Challenge Sector and Fun Zone.

Upper Campers also go on **4 planned trips**! All trip locations are thoroughly vetted by Harbor Haven for health and safety protocols. Trips are planned at outdoor locations. If there is inclement weather on a trip day, alternative exciting activities are planned at camp.

**_\*All trips and entertainment are subject to cancellation based on CDC and/or NJ Health Department guidelines, community health data and other health and safety factors._**

![Image 6](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/88e3d4ec-1586-4cc9-9350-e9e7e34b338b/PXL_20220708_162931846.jpg)

LIFE Program
------------

#### (Ages 16-18)

**The LIFE program at Harbor Haven provides support for meeting transition goals.  It is a balanced combination of structured learning experiences that promote growth in the following areas:**

*   Daily/independent living skills; personal care, housekeeping, health and safety
    
*   Development of employment readiness skills
    
*   Financial literacy
    
*   Real-world reading and writing
    
*   Computer and executive functioning skills
    
*   On-site jobs with coaching; guest speakers for employment opportunities
    
*   Hobbies and socialization
    
*   Exposure and access to community resources
    
*   Exploring post-secondary options
    
*   Meal planning/preparation, nutrition
    
*   Travel training through out-of-camp trips\*
    
*   Yoga, swimming, sports, crafts, music and more!
    
*   Individual speech and occupational therapy is available at an additional cost
    

**A high staff-to-participant ratio is maintained. An intake is required.**

[**_TravelQuest Program_**](https://www.harborhaven.com/programs/programs/travelquest/) **_-_** After the conclusion of the 5-week LIFE Program, teens may continue for one or two weeks in our exciting day travel program**_._**

**_\*All trips and entertainment are subject to cancellation based on CDC and/or NJ Health Department guidelines, community health data and other health and safety factors._**

_LIFE is a unique full-day summer program created by Harbor Haven's team of professionals for 16-18-year-old teens with mild special needs._

TravelQuest
-----------

#### (Ages 16-18)

![Image 7](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6534459f7eaa193cf2df97f6/3cbd7914-bb21-4972-8c8c-a9519dff5e39/IMG_BFE2D6F6CE4F-1.jpeg)

TravelQuest is a two-week day travel program for 16-18-year-olds with mild special needs, created and operated by Harbor Haven.  Teens can participate as a natural extension of the acclaimed 5-week LIFE Program at Harbor Haven or as a stand-alone one or two week summer experience.

TravelQuest is a fun social way for your teen to interact and experience new adventures with compatible young adults.  It is designed for teens with mild special needs.  In the TravelQuest program your teen is supported and supervised by professionals in the field of special education.

#### More details about this terrific opportunity for your teen:

*   Travel days include a fun trip, snacks, beverages and lunch.
    
*   All trip/lunch locations will be thoroughly vetted by Harbor Haven for health and safety protocols.
    
*   Trips are planned at both indoor and outdoor locations. If there is inclement weather on an outdoor trip day, an alternative activity will be planned.
    
*   All trips leave from and return to Harbor Haven.
    
*   Participants choose one or two weeks.
    
*   Centralized location transportation can be provided in most cases (at an additional cost).
    
*   All trip expenses are included in the tuition.
    
*   Three TravelQuest shirts and a backpack are included in the cost of the program.
    
*   Calendar of scheduled trips available in late winter.
    
*   All scheduled trips are subject to change due to weather conditions or other variables.
    
*   A virtual interview may be required.
    

**_\*All trips and entertainment are subject to cancellation based on CDC and/or NJ Health Department guidelines, community health data and other health and safety factors._**

SUMMER WORKSHOP PROGRAM
-----------------------

##### COMBOS

Rehearse each day with a small ensemble – the “small combo” is at the heart of jazz, providing the space and freedom for musicians to improvise and create at the highest levels. Performance opportunities will include outdoor community concerts.

##### VOCAL JAZZ ACADEMY

Calling all singers! Study with distinguished New York City-based faculty for advanced jazz ensemble singing, coupled with an exciting curriculum of vocal technique, theory and repertoire development. Vocal Academy students will participate in jam sessions and sing with small jazz combos in outdoor community concerts. Vocal large ensemble open to instrumentalists who sing as well.

##### FACULTY + GUEST ARTISTS

Work with an incredible core faculty every day that includes more than 25 leading jazz musicians, composers and educators! Our own 8-time GRAMMY Award-winning bassist [CHRISTIAN McBRIDE](https://jazzhousekids.org/people/christian-mcbride/) leads masterclasses and coaches ensembles on a variety of techniques and subjects, as well as many weekly special guests. Past guests include Ron Blake, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Anat Cohen, Antonio Hart, Louis Hayes, Ingrid Jensen, Ashley Kahn, Geoffrey Keezer, Oliver Lake, Harold Mabern, Rudresh Mahanthappa, Russell Malone, Eddie Palmieri, Christian Sands, Norman Simmons, Akiko Tsugura and Steve Turre.

##### CHiCA POWER **Ⓡ**

Rise and Improvise! Be part of this “girls only” initiative that empowers young women and the next generation of female jazz musicians, while having fun playing this great American art form and learning about the rich contributions of women in jazz. Masterclasses are led by internationally celebrated female jazz artists such as Dee Dee Bridgewater, Ingrid Jensen, Michela Marino Lerman, Anat Cohen, Regina Carter, and Camila Meza.

##### TV & FILM SCORING

Get the “tools” needed to navigate avenues open to today’s composers. This custom track focuses on technical skills and the composition process while students learn about musical ideas, sketches, revisions and performance for TV & film scoring.

##### COMPOSITION

Experiment with writing concepts and expand your improvising voice through composition! Students will improve their musicianship by recording their creations as well as by performing on other student composed pieces.

##### MUSIC PRODUCTION

Students will explore the essential recording and production techniques necessary to create their own songs. In an ever increasing ‘do-it-yourself’ environment, musicians who are able to produce their own material certainly have a leg up!

##### FAMILY BBQ

All students, faculty, friends and families are invited to meet and mingle (socially distant!) for an outdoor BBQ picnic and student jam.

Clubs are where jazz was born and where it will live on! Perform on the same stage as jazz legends at the acclaimed Dizzy’s Club at Jazz at Lincoln Center with its panoramic views of the New York City skyline, hosted by Artistic Director Christian McBride.

##### COMBOS AT THE CONCERT HALL

Perform on stage in the state-of-the-art Leshowitz Recital Hall at Montclair State University, live-streamed on our Facebook page.

Workshop students will hold their final performances all day on Saturday, August 16th at the annual Summer Showcase, before an audience of jazz fans, family and friends. Excitement builds as professional bands take the stage to close out the evening.

Past guests include Ron Blake, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Anat Cohen, Antonio Hart, Louis Hayes, Ingrid Jensen, Ashley Kahn, Geoffrey Keezer, Oliver Lake, Harold Mabern, Rudresh Mahanthappa, Russell Malone, Eddie Palmieri, Christian Sands, Norman Simmons, Akiko Tsugura and Steve Turre.

##### CHiCA POWER **Ⓡ**

Rise and Improvise! Be part of this “girls only” initiative that empowers young women and the next generation of female jazz musicians, while having fun playing this great American art form and learning about the rich contributions of women in jazz. Masterclasses are led by internationally celebrated female jazz artists such as Dee Dee Bridgewater, Ingrid Jensen, Michela Marino Lerman, Anat Cohen, Regina Carter, and Camila Meza.

##### TV & FILM SCORING

Get the “tools” needed to navigate avenues open to today’s composers. This custom track focuses on technical skills and the composition process while students learn about musical ideas, sketches, revisions and performance for TV & film scoring.

##### COMPOSITION

Experiment with writing concepts and expand your improvising voice through composition! Students will improve their musicianship by recording their creations as well as by performing on other student composed pieces.

##### MUSIC PRODUCTION

Students will explore the essential recording and production techniques necessary to create their own songs. In an ever increasing ‘do-it-yourself’ environment, musicians who are able to produce their own material certainly have a leg up!

##### FAMILY BBQ

All students, faculty, friends and families are invited to meet and mingle (socially distant!) for an outdoor BBQ picnic and student jam.

SUMMER WORKSHOP PERFORMANCES
----------------------------

##### BIG BANDS AT DIZZY’S

Clubs are where jazz was born and where it will live on! Perform on the same stage as jazz legends at the acclaimed Dizzy’s Club at Jazz at Lincoln Center with its panoramic views of the New York City skyline, hosted by Artistic Director Christian McBride.

##### COMBOS AT THE CONCERT HALL

Perform on stage in the state-of-the-art Leshowitz Recital Hall at Montclair State University, live-streamed on our Facebook page.

##### FINAL PERFORMANCE!

Workshop students will hold their final performances all day on Saturday, August 16th at the annual Summer Showcase, before an audience of jazz fans, family and friends. Excitement builds as professional bands take the stage to close out the evening.

RESIDENTIAL LIFE
----------------

JAZZ HOUSE Summer Workshop students hail from all over the country and the world, including regular cohorts who come year after year from Mexico, the United Kingdom and Peru. All students registered in the workshop may opt to stay in the dorms, including weekends, at Montclair State University’s Bloomfield College, a short ride away from the Cali School of Music and a quick train to Manhattan. Students are chaperoned by JAZZ HOUSE staff. Space is limited; submit the housing supplement with your online Summer Workshop registration today!

*   Modern air-conditioned double occupancy dorms
*   Transportation provided
*   All meals included
*   After-hour + weekend activities and excursions
*   On-site laundry services

The $25 Registration Fee will be applied to any future program your child may register for at the JAZZ HOUSE in 2023. There is a 50% refund (less the $125 initial deposit & registration fee) June 2 – July 1. There are no refunds beyond July 1st.

All students from beginner to advanced ages 12-18 are welcome! Students outside of age range will be accommodated based on experience level.

ALL STUDENTS must prepare and submit video auditions to place them in the appropriate class. Audition guidelines and materials can be found on the Audition Process page on our website. The same audition will be used for Fall 2025 classes.

Audition links can be submitted in the “Link to audition video on YouTube” line of your registration form. All audition materials are due June 1, 2025. For more information on the audition process.

WHAT WE DO
----------

![Image 23: Access](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

### Access  

We remove barriers and create opportunities for everyone to access instruments and practice spaces, enjoy performance and mentorship programs, and participate in unparalleled live jazz experiences.

![Image 24: Learning @ JAZZ HOUSE](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

### Learning

Our year-round programming nurtures a love for jazz and centers jazz as intervention, empowering students ages 8 to 19, at every level of experience, to rise and improvise.

![Image 25: Career Development](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

### Career Development

Through jazz, we prepare young people to become community leaders and global citizens, empowering them to find their voice both on and off the stage.

![Image 26: JAZZ HOUSE KiDS working in the community](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

### Community Building

We foster communities of informed listeners, uplift marginalized voices, and create meaningful connections among emerging musicians, working artists, master practitioners, and lovers of jazz.

Saturday, August 17 | Montclair State University, Kasser Theater

### **When school is out, the JCC is in!**

#### **Grade School Vacation Program**

Join us for trips, fun, and excitement during school vacations. December vacations, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President’s Day, Spring Break, and more – we’ve got you covered.

**Providing a fun all-day vacation program for kids in Grades K–6.**  
9:00am – 5:00pm • Member: $90/day or Non-Member: $100/day  
Before Care: M-F starting at 8am ($10 fee)  
After Care: M-Th until 6:00pm & Fridays until 5:45pm ($10 fee)

_Please remember to pack a swimsuit for pool time on selected days and a kosher dairy, nut-free lunch. Children are required to wear a swim cap which may be purchased from the JCC for $5._

[**WAIVER FORM**](https://jcc-metrowest.formstack.com/forms/vp_waiver) [**PAYMENT FORM**](https://jcc-metrowest.formstack.com/forms/vp_payment)

Counselors/Staff: Our staff are high school and college students who have experience working at our Kids Club Program or Camp Deeny Riback. They absolutely love the vacation program and the kids love them!

* * *

**  
Monday, March 31 • All Things Delicious (REGISTRATION FULL)**  
_Must register by 03/27_   
Spend the day slicing and dicing, whipping, and dipping as we cook delicious appetizers and decadent desserts. Whether this is your first time cooking or you’re a mini master, everyone will have a great time bringing out their inner chef.

* * *

_  
\*Packed lunches are required to be Kosher for Passover (KFP, OU-P, STAR-K P). Please contact the office if you have any questions._

**Monday, April 14 • TEKI Day**  
Is your child tech-savvy? Then they would love this day filled with computer technology programming. Don’t forget about gym and swim.

**Tuesday, April 15 • Liberty Science Center**  
Spend the day with us as we visit Liberty Science Center for a day filled with exploration of Science and Technology including the Wild About Animals exhibition, dino dig adventures, go through the touch tunnel and so much more!

**Wednesday, April 16 • Skyzone**  
Come jump, soar, and have fun at Skyzone! Don’t forget to pack a swimsuit for pool time and sneakers for the gym after the trip. _Must fill out this Skyzone waiver to participate:_ [https://waiver.haveablast.roller.app/SkyZoneSpringfieldNJ/home?ubid=JCmystJJbkCEqKJUfVG\_3w](https://waiver.haveablast.roller.app/SkyZoneSpringfieldNJ/home?ubid=JCmystJJbkCEqKJUfVG_3w)

**Thursday, April 17 • FunPlex**

**Friday, April 18 • Movie & PJ Day**  
We will enjoy a movie in our favorite PJ’s followed by swim and gym. We will also have a chance to play in the game room!

* * *

**Thursday, June 19 • Cookies & Canvas**  
Learn to bake and eat delicious cookies while you paint a one-of-a-kind canvas! Don’t forget to pack a bathing suit, towel, and swim cap for free swim and sneakers for the gym.

**Friday, June 20 • Splashplex/Funplex**  
Spend the day as we take a ride on the exhilarating water slides, lay back on the lazy river, or play in the foam frenzy! Pack a bathing suit and towel for a day at Splashplex and change into sneakers for the Funplex.

#### IMPORTANT: Policies and Procedures

*   Programs are open to Members and Guests of the JCC.
*   Cancellation Policy: Cancellations 48 hours prior to a Vacation Program will receive a JCC credit. Cancellations made less than 48 hours prior to a Vacation Program will receive no refund.
*   Please bring a kosher dairy, nut-free lunch each day.
*   Please remember to pack a swimsuit for pool time on selected days. Children are required to wear a swim cap. Please contact us to purchase a swim cap from the JCC for $5.
*   Any child who requires a Shadow Counselor must coordinate this arrangement with our Special Needs Director. The Shadow Counselor is paid separately by the parent.
*   Low registration may result in program cancellation.

_JCC MetroWest strives to ensure access and meaningful participation by all members of the community. If you would like to participate in any of our programs, but need additional support to be successful, please contact Marisa Cohen, Director of Special Needs Services at mcohen@jccmetrowest.org or at 973-530-3478. # Sub-Page: About Jeff Lake Summer Day Camp, New Jersey
For more than 60 years, Jeff Lake Day Camp has been one of the top family-run summer day camps in New Jersey. Our history, ongoing connection to former campers, counselors, and generations of families that come and go makes our day camp incredibly unique. We proudly maintain a level of connection and continuity to our community with unparalleled devotion and love.

Watch Video Trailer

Jeff Lake campers have the chance to explore and grow through this strong tradition of quality programming and FUN — all while making life-long friends! Our experienced staff guides campers through a wide range of classic day camp activities, as well as special days and events that reflect the spirit of Jeff Lake Day Camp. Ever since 1958 when the first group of children arrived at Jeff Lake Day Camp, we have provided a fun and loving environment for our campers to have the summer day camp experience of a lifetime…and just be kids!

---

# Sub-Page: Kids' Day Camp Leadership & Staff at Jeff Lake | Summer Day Camp in NJ
Jeff Lake is lucky to have a wonderful team of men and women who are responsible for the day-to-day well-being of our campers. Cumulatively, our Division Heads have been at camp for over 100 years! They are educators, guidance counselors, school administrators, parents, and former Jeff Lake campers. All of our age groups consist of multiple Division Heads and Assistant Division Heads to assist your campers on their daily needs as well as all parent outreach. We round out our Leadership Team with our Special Events Director, Tour Director, Specialist Director, Programming Director and our Allergy Specialist.

SUE RYNAR
---------

#### DIRECTOR

Sue began her career at Jeff Lake Day Camp more than 40 years ago and has since worked her way up through the ranks. She was a biking specialist, worked at the pool, and eventually became our Waterfront Director — The number of day camp kids who learned how to swim under Sue’s watch is far too many to count! Equipped with a Masters Degree from Boston University, her role as a full-time Director means stepping in and working with the leadership team to create a fun, yet safe environment for campers. This is an easy job for Sue as her whole family has strong ties to Jeff Lake Day Camp — She met her husband here and both of her boys were campers and counselors!

JUSTIN EFROS
------------

#### DIRECTOR

Justin is a Jeff Lake Day Camp “lifer,” having spent the better part of his life here — nearly three decades in total as a camper, counselor and member of the senior staff! He has been working for Jeff Lake full-time for the past 12 years, overseeing transportation, food, maintenance, and capital projects, and ensuring that the “behind the scenes” aspects of camp life function smoothly. His lifelong relationship with Jeff Lake has provided him with important insight into the value day camp holds for campers and staff alike. He and his wife Diana live in Randolph, and are the parents of two children, Joshua and Jordyn.

JILL ARZONICO
-------------

#### DIRECTOR OF ADMINISTRATION

Jill has been a beloved member of the JLC year round office staff since 1985. There is nothing that Jill does not know about camp! During the year, Jill is in charge of all the administrative aspects that go into running camp successfully all year long.

EMILY KAGAN
-----------

#### DIRECTOR/OWNER

Emily is third generation at Jeff Lake. Her grandfather, Ira Fish, founded Jeff Lake in 1958 and her parents, Jane and Dan Kagan, are the current owners. Emily brings years of camp experience as a camper, counselor, group leader and division head to her role as Assistant Director. She earned her Bachelor’s degree from Franklin and Marshall College and her Masters in Social Work from Columbia University. It is a dream come true for Emily to be at Jeff Lake, preserving and continuing her and her grandfather’s shared passion for summer camp and the powerful impact it has on children.

ADAM BARANKER
-------------

#### DIRECTOR

Adam started at Jeff Lake in 1992 at the age of 4 and has been a part of the Jeff Lake Family ever since. His mother was a Jeff Lake camper and counselor in the 70’s, so it was natural when he followed suit. During his 28 years at Jeff Lake, Adam has been a camper, CIT, AIDE, Junior Counselor, Senior counselor, Color War Captain, Assistant Director and now Director. Aside from always leading cheers and camp spirit, Adam is the CIT/AIDE Director, manages the camp’s Social Media, Staffing, and assists in Special Events and Programming.

JANE AND DAN KAGAN
------------------

#### OWNERS

Jane and Dan live and breathe summer camp! As the daughter of Jeff Lake Day Camp founder Ira Fish, Jane spent 25 summers at Jeff Lake as a camper, counselor and assistant director gaining the values and training that provided the foundation for her career in day camp. With her husband Dan, Jane returned to Jeff Lake in 2011, and together they are involved in all aspects of the day camp business. Jane and Dan are committed to carrying on the proud New Jersey day camp legacy established by “Uncle Ira.”

IRA FISH
--------

#### DIRECTOR EMERITUS

“Uncle Ira” founded Jeff Lake Camp in 1958. For 54 years, he lived ten months for two! Jeff Lake was his lifelong passion and a labor of love. He has provided thousands of children with incredible camping experiences, lifelong friendships, and special memories. His legacy will live on as all of the wonderful traditions that he brought to Jeff Lake continue for generations to come.

Jeff Lake’s Leadership Team includes our Directors and Division Heads. Together, they have over 300 years of Jeff Lake experience. Many of them started as campers, and went on to become counselors and supervisors. They have extensive professional experience in education and child development. Your child’s Division Head is out and about during the camp day in order to stay connected to each child’s experience. From supervising and guiding staff to participating in activities, to addressing the needs of individual campers, the Division Heads are devoted to making sure that your child receives the best care.

The key to a fantastic Jeff Lake summer is our loyal and talented staff. Our staff is made up of dedicated counselors and specialists. Each group of campers has two to three counselors, depending on group size. All counselors go through an extensive selection and training process in order to ensure that the most outstanding individuals are working with your children. Our counselors are enthusiastic young adults and teachers. Our Specialists run individual program areas, teaching skills and helping and encouraging campers to discover new talents. They come to us with backgrounds in teaching and coaching.

At Jeff Lake, we are one big family. 70% of our campers return to become counselors, and over 85% of our staff return summer after summer.

# Sub-Page: Five Star Summer Day Camp Facilities! | Jeff Lake Camp, New Jersey
The Jeff Lake Experience is unparalleled, due in large part to our spacious five-star summer day camp facilities — The best in New Jersey! Every day, the cheers and songs of our campers can be heard all around campus as they make their way from our namesake lake to our age-appropriate playing fields, and everywhere in between.

### Our Day Camp Facilities Include:

*   50 acres of Jefferson Lake waterfront for fishing, boating, kayaking, sailing, swimming, recreation and more
*   Five heated swimming pools that vary in depth to meet the needs of campers of all ages and skill levels
*   Separate Freshman Camp facilities for Pre-K and kindergarten campers
*   Freshman Clubhouse, providing air-conditioned space for yoga and creative play for our Pre-K and K age groups
*   Air-conditioned dance studio
*   Fine arts complex with ceramics studio
*   Drama playhouse for camp performances and special events
*   Modern kitchen facilities and dining pavilion
*   Athletic fields for soccer, lacrosse, baseball, basketball and volleyball
*   Adventure course with high and low ropes, rock climbing walls and team-building initiatives
*   State-of-the-art gymnastics pavilion
*   Hockey rink
*   GaGa court
*   Nature complex
*   Archery range
*   Tennis courts
*   Miniature golf course
*   Creative playgrounds for free play
*   Mountain biking and hiking trails
*   Bunks for changing and beautiful new restroom facilities

---

# Sub-Page: Transportation by New Jersey CDL-certified Bus Drivers for Jeff Lake
At Jeff Lake Day Camp, our day starts the moment your child steps on board the camp bus. Our bus counselors are trained to provide a safe and FUN ride to and from day camp. Our most important responsibility is ensuring your child’s safety, starting on the way to camp and ending with the ride home. That’s why Jeff Lakers ride to camp on a reliable 54-passenger bus. Every camp vehicle is equipped with seat belts and a two-way radio. Each counselor travels with a cell phone so they are always in contact with the camp. Our day camp bus drivers are New Jersey CDL-certified professionals, not counselors or parent volunteers, and our Transportation Director is always available to discuss your child’s transport to and from camp.

---

# Sub-Page: Summer Day Camp in New Jersey | Jeff Lake Day Camp
Any kid will tell you that food is one of the most important parts of day camp! At Jeff Lake Day Camp, our nutritious food is prepared daily on-site. We use the freshest ingredients and whole grains to whip up healthy, kid-friendly lunches that please even the pickiest campers! All meals are served in our brand new open air Dining Pavilion with counselors and Division Heads on hand to make certain that every camper leaves stuffed and satisfied!

#### Daily Entrees can Include

*   All-white meat baked chicken nuggets
*   Oven-baked pizza
*   Barbeque with kosher hot dogs, hamburgers and veggie burgers
*   Pasta

#### We Always Offer  

*   Extensive salad bar
*   Bagels
*   Soy Nut Butter & Jelly
*   Fresh turkey sandwiches
*   Fresh Fruit

If your camper has specific dietary needs or food allergies, our Food Service Manager and your child’s Division Head will work with you to accommodate any special needs. Our Food Allergy Specialist is in the Dining Hall each lunch period and oversees all allergy meals. We accommodate all food allergies including Gluten free options, as well as Kosher and vegetarian families. Jeff Lake Day Camp is a nut-aware camp. We do not serve products that contain nuts.

Why should my camper start Jeff Lake as a pre-schooler?

In the hussle-bussle of our lives there are very few ‘traditions’ we can offer our children; attending the same camp summer after summer is one of them. Each camper that starts Jeff Lakes as a pre-schooler soon feels JLC is their summer ‘home away from home’. With longevity comes a sense of belonging to a community.

Our Freshman Campus offers a small nurturing campus with its own soccer, basketball, and baseball fields, cabins and bathroom facilities. We are acutely aware of the developmental needs of pre-schoolers – feeling secure at camp and having strong self-esteem. Our Freshman staff, consisting of certified teachers, are focused on that goal. A 4 to 1 camper/counselor ratio allows for the hands on care necessary at that age.

We are often asked if our pre-schoolers take advantage of the wonderful facilities at Jeff Lake. The answer to that question is absolutely yes! Your camper will boat on our lake, hit a tennis ball, climb a mini-climbing wall, and make a pot in pottery. Our program director will ensure that your pre-schooler will utilize our facilities with the most efficient use of their energy. For example, if your camper is scheduled for project adventure period one then second period will be next door at gymnastics.

Swim instruction is scheduled daily. Our pre-school swim program is designed to focus on each camper’s individual skill development. At the pre-school level, we have campers ready to learn to rhythmic breath and others reluctant to dunk their heads. Each camper is taught at his/her skill level. Jeff Lake Camp is known for its swim instruction progress and our pre-schoolers are no exception!

  

Can you tell me about the van ride?

Camp begins the moment a camper enters his/her JLC vehicle. Our well- trained bus counselors ensure that your child is safely buckled in the seat and well supervised during the ride. But what our bus counselors are most loved for is…FUN! Each day a different activity is scheduled on the bus so that the ride to Jeff Lake becomes an event. Crazy Sock Day, Dress as Your Parent, Breakfast on the Bus, Bingo, Trivia, Pass It Up, and Halloween Day make each ride special. Campers decorate their bus and create songs and cheers to promote spirit. Start collecting buttons for Button Day and don’t throw away that ridiculous man’s tie – it may win your child a blue ribbon on Crazy Tie Day!

We leave the driving to professionals. Neither parents nor counselors drive Jeff Lake vehicles. Our bus drivers drive for school systems during the school year and become our camp drivers during the camp season. Professional drivers coupled with efficient routing make the ride to JLC as short as possible. Air- conditioned buses keep our campers comfortable as they transition from home to camp.

  

How is competition addressed at camp?

We emphasize skill development by teaching the fundamentals of each sport. One-on-one sports instruction is available with our Athletic Director or a qualified senior counselor. We believe that even the most reluctant camper becomes a participant if he/she feels successful, that is why Jeff Lake Campers do not sit on the sidelines!

All games are played with enthusiasm, good sportsmanship, and counselor participation. Teams are always picked by the counselor to ensure that teams are evenly matched. No camper is consistently picked first or last.  
Yes, sometimes one team wins and another loses however there is always an emphasis on sportsmanship.

Many of our sporting activities are individual sports such as swimming, boating, archery, and karate where competition is not a factor. In addition, we have an extensive Arts department that balances our athletic facilities. The same camper who is shooting baskets in the morning is likely to be throwing a pot on the potter’s wheel in the afternoon.

  

Is size a factor in choosing a day camp?

The size of Jeff Lake allows us to maintain a carefully selected and trained staff of approximately 275, a 50-acre lake with two water-trampolines, a water climbing wall, an extensive fishing program, a boating waterfront comparable to most over-night camps, miles of mountain biking trails and numerous sports and art activities over our extensive shaded acreage. We never feel ‘crowded’ and there is plenty of land and water room for the development of new activities. Your child will never out-grow our camp. Your senior camper will continue to be challenged. Our CIT/Teen program will provide the necessary transition between senior camper and junior staff.

But for our campers, Jeff Lake is only as large as the number of campers in their specific group. We foster group cohesiveness and spirit. For each child the summer revolves around the 15-18 campers and Senior and Junior  
counselors that lead his/her group.

Ask a Jeff Lake camper if JLC is ‘big’ and they will say “big in spirit” and “big in fun”.

  

What if my child is not athletically inclined?

Jeff Lakes is best suited to the active child but not necessarily the athlete. On a typical day, sports (basketball, archery, volleyball, etc) games (4-squares, running bases, gaga) and art activities (pottery, Native American crafts, music, dance) will be programmed. From first grade on, our campers can individualize one period per day. If you are interested in less athletics and more art activities, then you can use Hobby Hour to select photo, arts & crafts, cooking, etc. By fourth grade, our campers have two choice periods per day and can further individualize their schedule.

Athletic activities will always be part of a child’s life be it physical education at school or swimming on family vacations. Many of our campers who come to JLC feeling that they are not ‘athletes’ are in fact lacking confidence in their athletic skills but not lacking potential. Our expectation is not to make an athlete out of each camper but to make a camper a comfortable participator. Through developmentally appropriate skill development coupled with lots of positive reinforcement, many ‘non-athletes’ leave the summer feeling ready for the challenges of the ‘physical’ world. On the other hand, many of our strong athletes develop an appreciation of the artistic side of themselves. We want each child to learn and grow. Risk taking, on the ball field, in the art studio, or during social interaction, is a behavior reinforced through successful experiences. Jeff Lake Camp is the perfect environment to ‘take a risk’.

  

Who are my camper's counselors?

Our talented staff of junior, senior, and specialty counselors live in the same communities as our campers. Many of the 75% returning staff each year were JLC campers and CITs. They bring back to our camp community the ‘traditions’ that make Jeff Lake so strong. Our counselors are thoroughly interviewed and background checks are done on any camp member not familiar to JLC. Our staff undergoes 18 hours of training and orientation so that they are well prepared from the moment your child begins our program. A 4:1 ratio of camper to counselor ensures that each camper has the necessary supervision. Our counselors are mentored by a Division Head who provides guidance to the staff and keeps the lines of communication between parent and camp flowing.

Staff is the backbone of any camp. We pride ourselves in the quality of our counselors and in the extremely high percentage of returning staff each year. Each staff member is dedicated to providing the quality of experience you expect from Jeff Lake Camp.

  

Can I rent out the Jeff Lake Camp facility for a corporate picnic or private party?

Absolutely! Check out for more information.

# Sub-Page: Employment Opportunities: Jobs at Jeff Lake Day Camp, New Jersey
General Counselors
------------------

General Counselors are responsible for the physical and emotional well-being of the campers in their group. Working in teams of three, General Counselors supervise between 12 and 18 campers as they go about their daily summer camp activities. General Counselors get to know their campers well and provide them with leadership, support and guidance throughout the summer. Each group is led by a college aged Senior Counselor. Alongside the Senior Counselor are Assistant Counselors who are entering their Freshman year of college and/or Junior Counselors who are entering 11th and 12th grade.

Specialists
-----------

Specialists are instructors who have expertise in a specific activity and work full-time in that program area. All Specialists are responsible for the physical and emotional well-being of the campers attending their program area. Specialists also assist with trips and special events.

Nurses
------

Our medical staff members are a crucial part of the camp community. Jeff Lake Day Camp employs a staff of full-time RNs who dispense all medications (prescription and over-the-counter), triage and treat campers and staff at the Health Center, and supervise campers not well enough to attend activities. Nurses must be licensed RNs who love and understand children and must obtain New Jersey licensing. Nurses may also be asked to help supervise day trips and help address general community health and hygiene issues.

Kitchen & Maintenance  

------------------------

Our kitchen and maintenance staff works tirelessly for all of our campers and staff. The kitchen staff assists in the preparation, serving and cleanup of daily meals and snacks. Our maintenance team consists of highly skilled carpenters, landscape artists and facility operators who take pride in the upkeep of our day camp.

-------------------------------------------------------------------

From that first summer in 1958, Jeff Lake Day Camp has grown to become one of the premier family-owned summer day camps in New Jersey and the Northeast. Much of that success can be attributed to the devoted support of past campers and staff. Many of our current campers have siblings, parents, aunts, uncles and even grandparents who attended or worked at Jeff Lake, and we are incredibly fortunate to have so many alumni among the ranks of our leadership staff! Whether sharing stories about “Wigwam in the Woods,” or waving good morning to Art or Pearl as the buses roll into camp, our current families cherish the legends of Jeff Lake past, and they love hearing new tales of what Jeff Lake Day Camp is like today.

We welcome the chance to keep in touch with our Jeff Lake Day Camp alumni! Reunite with your Jeff Lake extended family by exploring the alumni section of our website. Stay connected to current happenings on Facebook and Twitter and keep your eyes open for exciting alumni events. Once a Jeff Laker, always a Jeff Laker!

Days Until Camp

Jeff Lake Day Camp is a Premier New Jersey Summer Day Camp for Children Ages 3 to 15
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Jeff Lake Day Camp, located in beautiful Sussex County New Jersey, offers an exciting, creative summer day camp experience for children. With facilities normally seen only at overnight camps, Jeff Lake Day Camp’s 350 acres provide endless opportunities for children to explore and learn. Key to this camping environment is a 50-acre lake with our inflatable lake playground, fishing, stand up paddle boards, sailing, kayaking, canoeing, paddle boats and row boats. Tennis courts, ropes & climbing courses, sports fields, dance & gymnastics, science, art & pottery studios, and 5 heated pools are just a few of the other great facilities at Jeff Lake Day Camp.

Over 60 Years of Family and Tradition

# Sub-Page: Counselor-In-Training (CIT) | Jeff Lake Day Camp
Tenth Grade
-----------

At Jeff Lake Day Camp, being in high school doesn’t mean a camper’s days here have to end. Tenth graders make some of their best camp memories in the Counselor-in-Training (CIT) program.

CIT Program

CITs learn how to work with children and staff in a closely supervised environment. Each day they divide their time between a field assignment, free choice and scheduled CIT activities organized by the CIT Director.

The summer isn’t all about learning and responsibility, though; there are plenty of fun times to be had! CITs go on seven out-of-camp day trips, including rushing water slides at Mountain Creek, relaxing in the sun at the Jersey Shore, zipping around the roller coasters at Dorney Park, and the highly anticipated annual Mystery Bus Trip!

The CIT program at Jeff Lake helps teenagers adjust and strike the proper balance between responsibility and recreation. The spirit, tradition, friendships and teamwork that are part of our leadership development program help teens gain the confidence to become participants in camp life — not just spectators.

#### Summer Camp 2025!

#### We are so excited to offer  
8 WEEKS of camp this summer.  
 Our first 4 weeks will be Half Day Camps (9am-1pm)  
with the option to extend to 3pm.  
These camps are for ages 4yrs old-1st Grade (rising or exiting).  
We will share a short presentation with parents at the end of each week.  
  
Our next 4 weeks will be Full Day Camps from 9am-3pm.  
These camps are for grades 1st- 5th (rising and exiting).  
We will create a short show to share with the parents at the end of each week. 

![Image 5: 0E1727F1-545C-4B8F-B68A-5E2AA1DF6505.JPG](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_297c0405018d42afacebb84707e62b17~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_161,h_216,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/0E1727F1-545C-4B8F-B68A-5E2AA1DF6505_JPG.jpg)

Games, Crafts, Singing, Dancing, Acting,  
Small Group time, Large Group Time

Teamwork, creativity, the building blocks of  
theatre vocabulary and dramatic skills,  
fun, communication, diligence, camaraderie

Ready...rocket ship... goooo! Join us as we use activities and our creativity to celebrate the planets, astronauts, stars, sun and moon in a week based on adventures in our solar system! We have lots of artistic exploring to do!

\*option to extend to 3pm

June 30th-July 3rd

Ages 4yrs-1st Grade (Rising & Exiting)

$320/child

Mermaids, fish, sea turtles, jellyfish, sharks... our activities and creativities will be based on all the wonderful things you can find Under The Sea!

\*option to extend to 3pm

July 7th-July 11th

9am-1pm\* @ St George's in Maplewood

Ages 4yrs-1st Grade (Rising & Exiting)

$395/child

Under The Sea

# Main Page: Class Descriptions | Little Apple Arts
#### Class Descriptions

![Image 1: Green Eggs and Ham.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_fc209496b01e4bed9192582874d220b4~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_238,h_235,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Green%20Eggs%20and%20Ham.png)

#### Storybook Theatre is for our youngest  
(drop off) artists. In this class, we introduce and explore basic theatre knowledge and skills in a fun and friendly way. Inspired by  
a storybook each session, we'll play games and build a presentation with guided dialog, singing and movement to share with family at the end of the session.   Ages 3-5   

![Image 2: Snow White.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_cb8a5529da4849f6a266ba9ca25bf853~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_238,h_235,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Snow%20White.png)

#### In Musicals Then we will learn about a 20th century musical. Throughout the session, we will continue to extend your child's theatre vocabulary and skills while we build an ensemble based song and scene to share with family at the end of the last class! Classes will include acting, singing, dancing and games. K-1, K-3

![Image 3: Newsies.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_4693e577c3b34c578345a7f3da5121b5~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_238,h_235,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Newsies.png)

#### In Musicals Now we will learn about a 21st century musical. Throughout the session, we will continue to extend your child's theatre vocabulary and skills while we build an ensemble based song and scene to share with family at the end of the last class! Classes will include acting, singing, dancing and games.  K-1, K-3

![Image 4: CYO Exploration.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_b3712aba18ad486989992f9147f6422c~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_238,h_235,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/CYO%20Exploration.png)

#### In our Create Your Own Play class, your child will work as a team with their classmates to create an original own short play. Based on the theme (this session is Exploration!), the writing is driven entirely by student imagination and creativity. We'll share the play with family at the end of the session.  Grades 2-5   

![Image 5: Charlotte's Web.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_24e7f09457b244e187df279113eb942e~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_238,h_235,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Charlotte's%20Web.png)

#### In our Scene Work class, we'll dig deeper into acting moments from a popular and/or classic children's novel. This class includes games and acting exercises with a focus on acting in small group scenes. We'll create a short presentation to share with family at the end of the session.  Grades 2-5

![Image 6: Level UP - 6.JPG](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ba411b_b271e0d993ad4f3cad49ee8c1aef5c7e~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_238,h_235,al_c,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Level%20UP%20-%206_JPG.jpg)

#### For our returning students, Level Up is the way to take your theatre skills to the next level. This class includes singing, dancing and acting, small group scene study, a group song/dance, character development, games, and more! Focus and memorization are important skills for this class.   Grades 2-5

The Little Foxes
================

Written by Lillian Hellman

Directed by Lyndsey Turner

Performances

Monday - Saturday, 7.30pm  
Wednesday & Saturday matinees, 2.30pm

**Previews**: Monday 2 - Tuesday 10 December

_**There are people who eat the earth and eat all the people on it.   
Then there are people who stand around and watch them eat it.**_   
   
After a lifetime spent watching her brothers grow rich, Regina Hubbard (**Anne-Marie Duff**) has had enough of standing around. When a businessman offers the family the prospect of untold wealth and power, a sequence of events unfolds that sets brother against brother, father against son and Regina against the whole pack of them.

A story of greed, ambition and a family on the edge, **Lillian Hellman**’s _The Little Foxes_ receives a savage new staging by Olivier Award-winning director **Lyndsey Turner** (_The Witches, The Crucible_).
