# Main Page: The Little Foxes
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

| The Little Foxes |
| --- |
| [![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/6/69/The-Little-Foxes-1939-FE.jpg/250px-The-Little-Foxes-1939-FE.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The-Little-Foxes-1939-FE.jpg)First edition (1939)
 |
| Written by | [Lillian Hellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lillian_Hellman "Lillian Hellman") |
| Characters | 

*   Regina Giddens
*   Horace Giddens
*   Leo Hubbard
*   Oscar Hubbard



 |
| Date premiered | February 15, 1939 |
| Place premiered | [National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederlander_Theatre "Nederlander Theatre")  
[New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") |
| Original language | English |
| Genre | [Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama "Drama") |
| Setting | Alabama in 1900 |

_**The Little Foxes**_ is a 1939 play by [Lillian Hellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lillian_Hellman "Lillian Hellman"), considered a classic of 20th century drama. Its title comes from Chapter 2, Verse 15, of the [Song of Solomon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_of_Songs "Song of Songs") in the [King James version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authorized_King_James_Version "Authorized King James Version") of the [Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible "Bible"), which reads, "Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes." Set in a small town in [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama "Alabama") in 1900, it focuses on the struggle for control of a family business.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-theaterscene-1) [Tallulah Bankhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallulah_Bankhead "Tallulah Bankhead") starred in the original production as Regina Hubbard Giddens.

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/The-Little-Foxes-Bankhead-1.jpg/170px-The-Little-Foxes-Bankhead-1.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The-Little-Foxes-Bankhead-1.jpg)

[Tallulah Bankhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallulah_Bankhead "Tallulah Bankhead") as Regina Giddens in _The Little Foxes_ (1939)

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/The-Little-Foxes-Breakfast.jpg/330px-The-Little-Foxes-Breakfast.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The-Little-Foxes-Breakfast.jpg)

Tallulah Bankhead, [Charles Dingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dingle "Charles Dingle"), [Carl Benton Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Benton_Reid "Carl Benton Reid") and [Dan Duryea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Duryea "Dan Duryea") in the original Broadway production of _The Little Foxes_ (1939)

The play's focus is Southerner Regina Hubbard Giddens, who struggles for wealth and freedom within the confines of an early 20th-century society where fathers considered only sons as their legal heirs. As a result of this practice, while her two avaricious brothers Benjamin and Oscar have wielded the family inheritance into two independently substantial fortunes, she has had to rely upon her manipulation of her cautious, timid, browbeaten husband, Horace. He is no businessman, just her financial support; although he is pliable enough for her ambition, that ambition has driven him into becoming merely the tool of her insatiable greed. He uses a wheelchair.

Her brother Oscar married Birdie, his much-maligned alcoholic wife, solely to acquire her family's [plantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantations_in_the_American_South "Plantations in the American South") and cotton fields. Oscar now wants to join forces with his brother, Benjamin, to construct a [cotton mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotton_mill "Cotton mill"). They need an additional $75,000 and approach Regina, asking her to invest in the project. Oscar initially proposes marriage between his son Leo and Regina's daughter Alexandra—first cousins—as a means of getting Horace's money, but Horace and Alexandra are repulsed by the suggestion, as is Birdie. Horace refuses when Regina asks him outright for the money, so Leo, a bank teller, is pressured into stealing Horace's railroad [bonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bond_(finance) "Bond (finance)") from the bank's safe deposit box.

Horace, after discovering this, tells Regina he is going to change his will in favor of their daughter, and also claim he gave Leo the bonds as a loan, thereby cutting Regina out of the deal completely. When he has a [heart attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_attack "Heart attack") during this chat, she makes no effort to help him. He dies within hours, without anyone knowing his plan and before changing his will. This leaves Regina free to blackmail her brothers by threatening to report Leo's theft unless they give her 75% ownership in the cotton mill (it is, in Regina's mind, a fair exchange for the stolen bonds). The price Regina ultimately pays for her evil deeds is the loss of her daughter Alexandra's love and respect. Regina's actions cause Alexandra to finally understand the importance of not idly watching people do evil. She tells Regina she will not watch her be "one who eats the earth," and abandons her. Having let her husband die, alienated her brothers, and driven away her only child, Regina is left wealthy but completely alone.

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Lillian-Hellman-1939.jpg/170px-Lillian-Hellman-1939.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lillian-Hellman-1939.jpg)

Lillian Hellman in 1939

The fictional Hubbards in the play are reputedly drawn from Lillian Hellman's Marx relatives. Hellman's mother was Julia Newhouse of [Demopolis, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demopolis,_Alabama "Demopolis, Alabama"). Julia Newhouse's parents were Leonard Newhouse, a Demopolis wholesale liquor dealer, and Sophie Marx, of a successful Demopolis banking family. According to Hellman, Sophie Marx Newhouse never missed an opportunity to belittle and mock her father for his poor business sense in front of her and her mother. The discord between the Marx and Hellman families was to later serve as the inspiration for the play.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-demopolisfam-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-southernlittrail-3)[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-4)

The title "The Little Foxes" was suggested by [Dorothy Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Parker "Dorothy Parker").

In 1946, Hellman wrote _[Another Part of the Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Another_Part_of_the_Forest "Another Part of the Forest")_, a [prequel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prequel "Prequel") chronicling the roots of the Hubbard family.

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/The-Little-Foxes-Rawls-Bankhead.jpg/170px-The-Little-Foxes-Rawls-Bankhead.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The-Little-Foxes-Rawls-Bankhead.jpg)

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/The-Little-Foxes-Bankhead-2.jpg/250px-The-Little-Foxes-Bankhead-2.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The-Little-Foxes-Bankhead-2.jpg)

Bankhead played every performance of _The Little Foxes_ on Broadway and on tour, and she was angry when [Bette Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bette_Davis "Bette Davis") was awarded the role of Regina in the [1941 motion picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes_(film) "The Little Foxes (film)").[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-Carrier-5): 90

Produced and directed by [Herman Shumlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herman_Shumlin "Herman Shumlin"), the original Broadway production of _The Little Foxes_ opened February 15, 1939, at the [National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederlander_Theatre "Nederlander Theatre"). It closed February 3, 1940, running for 410 performances before its two-season tour of the United States.[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-vault1-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-7)

*   [Tallulah Bankhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallulah_Bankhead "Tallulah Bankhead") as Regina Hubbard Giddens[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [Patricia Collinge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Collinge "Patricia Collinge") as Birdie Hubbard[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [Frank Conroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Conroy_(actor) "Frank Conroy (actor)") as Horace Giddens
*   Lee Baker as William Marshall[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [Charles Dingle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dingle "Charles Dingle") as Benjamin Hubbard[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [Dan Duryea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Duryea "Dan Duryea") as Leo Hubbard[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [John Marriott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Marriott_(actor) "John Marriott (actor)") as Cal[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [Abbie Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abbie_Mitchell "Abbie Mitchell") as Addie[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   [Carl Benton Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carl_Benton_Reid "Carl Benton Reid") as Oscar Hubbard[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)
*   Florence Williams as Alexandra Giddens[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)

On October 30, 1939, [Eugenia Rawls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenia_Rawls "Eugenia Rawls") replaced Florence Williams in the role of Alexandra Giddens. Rawls had made her Broadway debut as one of the students in Lillian Hellman's 1934 play, _[The Children's Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Children%27s_Hour_(play) "The Children's Hour (play)")_, which was also produced and directed by Herman Shumlin.[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-9) Rawls played Alexandra for the rest of the play's Broadway run and the national tour that followed.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-IBDb-8)[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-10)

The 104-city tour of _The Little Foxes_ began February 5, 1940, in Washington, D.C., and ended April 15, 1941, in Philadelphia.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-Carrier-5)

[Tallulah Bankhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallulah_Bankhead "Tallulah Bankhead") won _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ magazine's citation as best actress of the 1938–39 Broadway season.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-Carrier-5): 22

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/Greer_Garson_Franchot_Tone_The_Little_Foxes_Hallmark_Hall_of_Fame_1956.jpg/170px-Greer_Garson_Franchot_Tone_The_Little_Foxes_Hallmark_Hall_of_Fame_1956.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Greer_Garson_Franchot_Tone_The_Little_Foxes_Hallmark_Hall_of_Fame_1956.jpg)

[Greer Garson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greer_Garson "Greer Garson") and [Franchot Tone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchot_Tone "Franchot Tone") in the 1956 _[Hallmark Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallmark_Hall_of_Fame "Hallmark Hall of Fame")_ TV adaptation of _The Little Foxes_

Lillian Hellman wrote the [screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screenplay "Screenplay") for a [1941 film version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes_(film) "The Little Foxes (film)"), a [Samuel Goldwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn "Samuel Goldwyn") production directed by [William Wyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Wyler "William Wyler"). Other contributors to the screenplay included [Arthur Kober](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Kober "Arthur Kober"), [Dorothy Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Parker "Dorothy Parker") and [Alan Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Campbell_(screenwriter) "Alan Campbell (screenwriter)"). The touring production of _The Little Foxes_ went on hiatus for three months during filming, and Patricia Collinge, Charles Dingle, Dan Duryea, John Marriott and Carl Benton Reid all reprised their stage roles in their motion picture debuts. [Bette Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bette_Davis "Bette Davis"), [Herbert Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Marshall "Herbert Marshall") and [Teresa Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teresa_Wright "Teresa Wright") star as Regina, Horace and Alexandra Giddens.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-11)

_The Little Foxes_ was presented on _[Philip Morris Playhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Morris_Playhouse "Philip Morris Playhouse")_ October 10, 1941. The radio adaptation starred [Tallulah Bankhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallulah_Bankhead "Tallulah Bankhead").[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-12)

In 1949, the play was adapted for an opera entitled _[Regina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_(Blitzstein) "Regina (Blitzstein)")_ by [Marc Blitzstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Blitzstein "Marc Blitzstein").

George Schaefer produced and directed Robert Hartung's television adaptation of _The Little Foxes_ for the _[Hallmark Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hallmark_Hall_of_Fame "Hallmark Hall of Fame")_, broadcast December 16, 1956, on [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC"). The cast included [Greer Garson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greer_Garson "Greer Garson") (Regina), [Franchot Tone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchot_Tone "Franchot Tone") (Horace), [Sidney Blackmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Blackmer "Sidney Blackmer") (Ben), [E. G. Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._G._Marshall "E. G. Marshall") (Oscar) and [Eileen Heckart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eileen_Heckart "Eileen Heckart") (Birdie).[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-13)

[Mike Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Nichols "Mike Nichols") directed a production that opened October 26, 1967, at the [Vivian Beaumont Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Beaumont_Theater "Vivian Beaumont Theater") in [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts"), then transferred to the [Ethel Barrymore Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethel_Barrymore_Theatre "Ethel Barrymore Theatre"). It ran a total of 100 performances. The cast included [Anne Bancroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Bancroft "Anne Bancroft") as Regina, [Richard A. Dysart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_A._Dysart "Richard A. Dysart") as Horace, [Margaret Leighton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Leighton "Margaret Leighton") as Birdie, [E.G. Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.G._Marshall "E.G. Marshall") as Oscar, [George C. Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_C._Scott "George C. Scott") as Benjamin, and [Austin Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Pendleton "Austin Pendleton") as Leo. Costume design was by [Patricia Zipprodt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patricia_Zipprodt "Patricia Zipprodt").[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-vault2-14) In reviewing the production, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ said, "An admirable revival of Lillian Hellman's 1939 play in Lincoln Center demonstrates how securely bricks of character can be sealed together with the mortar of plot. Anne Bancroft, George C. Scott, Richard Dysart, and Margaret Leighton are expertly guided by Director Mike Nichols through gilt-edged performances."[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-time-15) The production was profiled in the [William Goldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Goldman "William Goldman") book _[The Season: A Candid Look at Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Season:_A_Candid_Look_at_Broadway "The Season: A Candid Look at Broadway")_.

[Geraldine Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_Page "Geraldine Page") played Regina in a production in which she starred opposite her husband [Rip Torn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rip_Torn "Rip Torn") (in the role of Benjamin Hubbard) directed by Philip Minor. It was staged for the Academy Festival Theater at [Barat College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barat_College "Barat College") in [Lake Forest, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Forest,_Illinois "Lake Forest, Illinois") and received a rave review from William Leonard of the _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_: "Geraldine Page is giving one of the greatest performances of her glorious career in Lake Forest and she is surrounded by a cast so superb that the Academy Festival Theater's production of _"The Little Foxes"_ becomes a powerful, searing, unforgettable show... it is a harrowing and ennobling evening in the theater-the kind that comes along all too seldom. We have seen other stars in the role of the malevolently, ruthlessly scheming Regina Giddens—[Tallulah Bankhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallulah_Bankhead "Tallulah Bankhead") years ago in her greatest triumph, [Eileen Herlie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eileen_Herlie "Eileen Herlie") five seasons back at the Ivanhoe. Geraldine Page is a whole new story—I have seen Geraldine Page in innumerable roles, ever since she was playing in _[East Lynne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Lynne "East Lynne")_ with the Lake Zurich Players back in the '40s. I've never seen her more thrillingly convincing than in this production."[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-16) The legendary [Kim Stanley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kim_Stanley "Kim Stanley") once said of Page's Regina that it "was possibly the finest performance" she had ever seen.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-17)

Austin Pendleton directed a production at the Parker Playhouse in [Fort Lauderdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Lauderdale "Fort Lauderdale") for three weeks that transferred to the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Center_for_the_Performing_Arts "John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), for six weeks before opening on Broadway. The production opened on May 7, 1981, at the [Martin Beck Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Hirschfeld_Theatre "Al Hirschfeld Theatre") for 123 performances and eight previews. The cast included [Elizabeth Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Taylor "Elizabeth Taylor") as Regina, [Tom Aldredge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Aldredge "Tom Aldredge") as Horace, [Dennis Christopher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Christopher "Dennis Christopher") as Leo, [Maureen Stapleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maureen_Stapleton "Maureen Stapleton") as Birdie, and [Anthony Zerbe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Zerbe "Anthony Zerbe") as Benjamin. [Florence Klotz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Klotz "Florence Klotz") was the costume designer.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-vault3-18) In a _Time_ article prior to the Broadway opening, Gerald Clarke reported nearly $1 million worth of ticket sales during the week after advertisements announcing Taylor's appearance appeared in _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-clarke-19) Taylor received nominations for both the [Tony Award for Best Performance by a Leading Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Performance_by_a_Leading_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Performance by a Leading Actress in a Play") and the [Drama Desk Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_Desk_Award "Drama Desk Award") for Outstanding Actress in a Play. Tony nominations also went to Pendleton for [Best Direction of a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Direction_of_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Direction of a Play"), Aldredge for [Best Featured Actor in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Performance_by_a_Featured_Actor_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Performance by a Featured Actor in a Play"), Stapleton for [Best Featured Actress in a Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Performance_by_a_Featured_Actress_in_a_Play "Tony Award for Best Performance by a Featured Actress in a Play"), and the play itself for [Best Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Revival "Tony Award for Best Revival").

A 1997 revival, again at the Vivian Beaumont, ran for 27 previews and 57 performances from April 3 to June 15. Directed by [Jack O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_O%27Brien_(director) "Jack O'Brien (director)"), the cast included [Stockard Channing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockard_Channing "Stockard Channing") as Regina, [Kenneth Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Welsh "Kenneth Welsh") as Horace, [Brian Kerwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Kerwin "Brian Kerwin") as Oscar, [Brian Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Murray_(actor) "Brian Murray (actor)") as Benjamin, and [Frances Conroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frances_Conroy "Frances Conroy") as Birdie. Murray was nominated for the Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Play and won the Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Featured Actor in a Play, and John Lee Beatty was nominated for the [Tony Award for Best Scenic Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Scenic_Design "Tony Award for Best Scenic Design").[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-vault4-20)

The production was revived at The [Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare_Theatre_of_New_Jersey "Shakespeare Theatre of New Jersey"), from June 3 to 28, 2009, with [Venida Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venida_Evans "Venida Evans"), Ron Brice, Deanne Lorette, Brian Dykstra, Fisher Neal, Kathryn Meisle, Einar Gunn, Philip Goodwin, Lindsey Wochley, Bradford Cover, and directed by Matthew Arbour.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-shakes-21)

Another revival was produced by [Cleveland Play House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Play_House "Cleveland Play House") in the 75th anniversary year of the original Broadway production, September 12–October 5, 2014, in the [Allen Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Theatre "Allen Theatre") ([Playhouse Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playhouse_Square "Playhouse Square")) in Cleveland, Ohio. The production was directed by Artistic Director Laura Kepley.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-cph-22)

Kyle Donnelly directed a revival at [Washington, DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_DC "Washington, DC")'s [Arena Stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arena_Stage "Arena Stage") from September 23 to October 30, 2016. The cast included [Marg Helgenberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marg_Helgenberger "Marg Helgenberger"), [Edward Gero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Gero "Edward Gero"), [Isabel Keating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabel_Keating "Isabel Keating"), and Jack Willis.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-helgenberger-23)

[Manhattan Theatre Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_Theatre_Club "Manhattan Theatre Club") produced a Broadway revival that began previews on March 29, 2017, and opened officially on April 19 at the [Samuel J. Friedman Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_J._Friedman_Theatre "Samuel J. Friedman Theatre"). It starred [Laura Linney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Linney "Laura Linney") (who was nominated for a Tony Award—Performance by a Leading Actress in a Play) and [Cynthia Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cynthia_Nixon "Cynthia Nixon") who alternated the roles of Regina Giddens and Birdie, with direction by [Daniel J. Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_J._Sullivan "Daniel J. Sullivan"). Cynthia Nixon won the Tony Award for Featured Actress in a Play for her turn as Birdie. The production team included [Scott Pask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Pask "Scott Pask"), Justin Townsend, [Jane Greenwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Greenwood "Jane Greenwood"), Fotz Patton, and Tom Watson.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-25)[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-26) It played its final performance on July 2, 2017.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-27)

The [Gate Theatre, Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gate_Theatre,_Dublin "Gate Theatre, Dublin"), was going to show a revival in 2020, directed by Blanche McIntyre, but this was postponed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Little_Foxes#cite_note-28)

The [Young Vic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Vic "Young Vic") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") produced a 3-month revival that opened December 2, 2024 starring [Anne-Marie Duff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne-Marie_Duff "Anne-Marie Duff") as Regina.

##### [21/12/2024](https://theatre.revstan.com/2024/12/video-review-the-little-foxes-young-vic-theatre.html)

Video transcript:
-----------------

I'm going to have to plead ignorance because when I booked to see The Little Foxes at the Young Vic, or rather, when my friend booked for us, I hadn't heard the play. I didn't know it was an American classic.

I knew nothing about it, but that meant I went into it with no expectations but I can fully understand why it is a classic.

This is such a tight, tense family drama. It has very meaty dialogue with lots of subtext, lots of politics going on in the family - man0euverings, manipulations and people trying to outmanoeuver each other.

I was gripped pretty much from about 10 minutes in and throughout. I was hooked.

The cast is superb: Anne-Marie Duff, Mark Bonnar, Anna Madeley. John Light and Stefan Rhodri - all superb.

I thought that it was a fascinating, fascinating story. And it's interesting who you root for. I definitely recommend it.

Stan's rating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Production details:
-------------------

The Little Foxes, Young Vic Theatre

Written by Lillian Hellman

Directed by Lyndsey Turner

Cast: Mark Bonnar, Andrea Davy, Anne-Marie Duff, John Light, Freddie MacBruce, Anna Madeley, Stanley Morgan, Steffan Rhodri and Eleanor Worthington-Cox.

Running time: 2 hours and 15 minutes, including an interval.

Booking until 8 Feb 2025; for more details and to buy tickets, visit the [Young Vic website](https://www.youngvic.org/whats-on/the-little-foxes).

# Sub-Page: About Us
**_Magic for Muggles Summer Day Camp, created and directed by veteran educators Kevin McCarthy, Ed.M., and Adam Scribner, Ed.D., is back for year twenty one!_**

Our program will once again make the magic of Hogwarts School come alive for youngsters – whether they have read all the books or have seen a single movie. It’s our hope and belief that children will be inspired to read about the adventures of Harry Potter, for the first time or for repeated enjoyment. Our camp is geared for girls and boys, ages 7-12, but we have had no problem integrating slightly younger or older campers. There are always exceptions. (Please see the FAQ’s for more information on student ages.)

This year, we intend to continue with several of our tried and true activities that are children favorites – playing quidditch, wand making, Harry Potter Jeopardy (we always encourage reading), dueling, learning about magical creatures, making house banners – plus there are always surprises! Experienced animal handlers and spell-binding magicians add to the long list of fun and exciting daily activities. From the moment our Hogwarts students are sorted into houses, the magic begins!

Magic for Muggles takes place at St. John’s Episcopal Church’s Parish Hall, 55 Montclair Avenue – a block away from Woodman Field. This spacious, Gothic-looking facility provides a real Hogwarts feel to our program and gives us all the room we need.

Please know that in 2025, we will once again be following the recommended CDC Covid-19 guidelines for summer camps including continuous cleaning. Also, the building we use is air conditioned and has a MERV 13-ventilation system intended to filter the air to remove virus particles.

Magic for Muggles will be offering four sessions in summer 2025 with 48 spaces per session.  They are:

**Session one: July 7th -11th Full**

**Session two: July 14th-18th Full**

**Session three: July 21st-25th Full**

**Session four: July 28th-August 1st**

_**All sessions run from 9am – 1pm.**_

The camp starts and activities begin daily at 9AM and do not stop until 1PM.  The cost per camper, per week is $345. **_Due to demand, early registration is advised as all previous sessions have sold out._**

_Refund policy: refunds are only provided for cancellations when the space can be filled by another camper. Please provide a minimum of two-weeks notice._

Let us assure you that your child’s safety is our paramount concern. No child is ever left unattended – from the time they’re dropped off until they’re picked up, there is adult supervision. This program is fully insured.

All inquiries can be sent to Kevin McCarthy at kmc216@optonline.net

Magic for Muggles Summer Day Camp is owned and operated by K and A Camps, LLP.

# Sub-Page: F.A.Q.s
**MAGIC FOR MUGGLES – FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS**

**WHAT ARE THE AGES FOR YOUR CAMP?** Our core group is between 7-13. We have also had 6 year-olds who know a little bit about HP or attend with older siblings.  Students should be old enough to understand the storyline of the first book or movie.

**DO THE SESSIONS FILL UP?** Since we began in 2004, we have filled every session offered.

**ARE THERE ANY PROBLEMS WITH THE AGE GROUP DIFFERENCES?** We’ve never seen it. The children are randomly divided into the HP Houses and one of the neat things about our camp is how well these groups bond and work together. The children become very supportive of one another during the week and the older ones really help the youngsters in all of the activities.

**DOES ONE HAVE TO HAVE READ THE HP BOOKS?** No, our activities are designed so all can participate without having read a book or seen a movie. Our hope is that those who haven’t read the books will be inspired to begin the series. Often times it starts with parents reading the books to younger children.

**DOES A CHILD HAVE TO HAVE A WIZARD ROBE TO PARTICIPATE?** Absolutely not (though we have had some children tell their parents that!). Campers are encouraged to wear their HP robes, hats, t-shirts, etc. – it definitely adds to the atmosphere, but many campers make their own costumes.

**DO YOU HAVE BEFORE AND AFTER CARE?** Sorry, we don’t. _**Our doors open at 8:45 a.m. and there’s an adult outside to see the children in. Likewise, we dismiss at 1 p.m.** **sharp**_, again, under adult supervision. (We have families too and have a ways to go to see them.)

**IS THERE AN OPPORTUNITY TO BUY LUNCH?** No, students must bring their own lunches. We take a short break at noon for students to eat, sit and talk with their friends from other houses, and watch a few minutes of a film or special. Students can bring extra drinks.

**WHAT IF MY CHILD HAS FOOD ALLERGIES?** Before every lunch we remind students not to share food because of allergies. We will also alert parents to this when we send out a notice before camp begins. As for foods that we provide students, there are only three things offered to children during the week: (1) A single flavored jelly bean on two occasions for our “guess the flavor” of the magic beans team competition. We use store bought Jelly Bellies jelly beans. (2) Three days a week after going outside and playing quidditch, we give students an ice pop on their return indoors. These are the multi-flavored pops you would get in Shop Rite. (3) On Fridays, we give the campers “butterbeer” which is essentially a vanilla ice cream/soda float in a paper cup. Please contact us if you have any concerns.

**DO YOU HAVE AIR CONDITIONING?** Yes, Saint John’s Church has air conditioning that has a MERV 13-ventilation system to filter the air to remove harmful pollen and virus particles.

**WHO IS WORKING THE CAMP?** Kevin McCarthy and Adam Scribner are long time educators and Harry Potter fans. This is their twentieth year directing Magic For Muggles. Magic for Muggles staff includes certified public school teachers and top-notch college students (many of whom were Magic for Muggles campers).

**ARE THERE OUTDOOR ACTIVITIES?** Definitely. We go outside at least three days during the week for an hour or so to a small park (aka “The Magic Forest”) which is located a half a block away. We are “unplugged” all week and do not use computers at any time.

**HOW EXACTLY DOES THE CAMP WORK?** Students are grouped into one of the four Harry Potter Houses of Hogwarts School. For one week they follow a daily schedule of activities. They earn house points for completing tasks. At times, special guests drop in – a real magician, a reptile specialist, maybe a HP personality- to entertain us. No House EVER gets too far ahead in the point totals. In fact, somehow it always magically comes down to the last activity on the last day to determine a a house winner. Ultimately, however, everyone is recognized and goes home with a certificate of wizardry!

**IS IT POSSIBLE FOR A CHILD TO SIGN UP FOR MORE THAN ONE WEEK?** Definitely, though we think two is just right. And even though the same activities are repeated in a second session, the majority of the campers are new, the students are in different houses and, therefor, the outcomes of each activity will be different. Plus, it’s just a lot of fun to go through the week again!

**DO YOU TAKE CREDIT CARDS?**  Yes, we use PayPal – and it accepts both credit cards (Visa, MasterCard, American Express, and Discover) and PayPal payments. We use PayPal to keep your information secure.

**WHAT IS YOUR REFUND POLICY?** Refunds are only provided for cancellations when the space can be filled by another camper.  Please provide a minimum of two-weeks notice.

**HOW IS YOUR CAMP ADDRESSING COVID-19?** In 2025, we will once again be following the recommended CDC guidelines for summer camps including continuous cleaning. Also, the building we use is air-conditioned and has a MERV 13-ventilation system was installed to filter the air and remove Covid-19 particles.

**ARE YOU HIRING?** All staff hired are certified teachers and college students hired as helpers.  We do not hire middle or high school camp interns due to insurance reasons. All staff positions are filled at this time for the upcoming summer sessions.

**DO YOU DO BIRTHDAY PARTIES FOR CHILDREN?** Sorry, we don’t do birthday parties during the year despite several requests (all staff members have full-time teaching jobs and they like to hold onto their weekends), but **_you do not need to hire someone to run Harry Potter-themed birthdays!_** Our advice has always been to have fun, keep it simple, and plan your own. Have the kids make magic wands out of cut dowels, make magic potions using small “potion bottles” from local craft stores. Play quidditch by passing a ball around and throwing it through hoops. Have the “keeper” be the goaltender by holding a broom. Improvise games you know like bingo and word scrambles only using HP words.  And, of course, “sort” the kids into houses (this can be done simply by picking something out a hat). Good luck and have fun!

# Main Page: Art Camp with Ms. Tio Summer 2025!
![Image 1](https://luisatio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/img_0648.jpg)

**Join Ms. Tio for 3 great camp sessions of art and imagination and fun!**

**Harry Potter Camp (June 23-27, 2025) is 2/3-day (8:30-12:30) and will be held outdoors in Del Ray, and** **Art of Architecture (June 30- July 4, 2025) and French Impressions of Art (July 7-11, 2025) are full day (8:30-2:30) and will be held indoors in Del Ray. Please pack a lunch for your child. We will have an outdoor recess each day.To register for camp, please click here to print and complete the [Art Camp Registration Form 2025](https://luisatio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/art-camp-registration-form.2025-7.pdf), and then mail it with a $50 supply fee deposit to Luisa Tio, P.O. Box 2442, Alexandria, VA, 22301. You may also Venmo the deposit to @Luisa-Tio Please make sure to write your child’s name and the camp session. Please also send four weeks before camp your child’s [Emergency Contacts, Health, Media and Walking Field Trip Forms (Summer 2025)](https://luisatio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/emergency-contacts-health-media-and-walking-field-trip-forms-summer-2025-1.pdf) and the remaining tuition.**

**Our 2025 Summer Camps are:**

**Harry Potter and Hogwarts School of Magic and Wizardry  June 23-27, 2025  8:30-12:30 $315**

Leave the muggle world behind and enter Hogwarts. We will visit Diagon Alley to get our magic wands and other school essentials. We’ll play quidditch (after we are sorted into houses, of course!). We will create our favorite wizard cards, and learn to care for magical creatures. We will study all of the magical arts, such as divination, spells, and magic potions and end our camp with a banquet, complete with butter beer. Enroll in Hogwarts for a week of art, magic, and fun!

**Art of Architecture  June 30 – July 4, 2025  8:30-3:30 $435 (includes fees for a field trip)**

Want to learn to paint on canvases as big as houses or make sculptures as big as city blocks? That’s what architects do every day! This week it’s our turn. We’ll explore how and why architects design the works of art we live and work in, and then design, paint, and build our own. We will also visit either the National Building Museum or Frank Lloyd Wright’s Pope-Leighey House to deepen out knowledge of architecture.  Camp WILL be held on July 4.

**Art of the Impressionists: Painting, Drawing and Sculpture  July 7-11, 2025 8:30-2:30 $435 (includes fees for a field trip)**

We’ll be impressed by the likes of Monet, Renoir, Cassatt and Degas, and other greats of French Impressionism and their Post-Impressionist contemporaries like Van Gogh (with and without his ear). We’ll draw and paint in _plein air_, bring the ordinary to life, and learn how to capture movement in 2D and 3D. Join Ms. Tio as we travel “artistically” to France and soak in the beauty of French art and culture. We will visit the National Gallery of Art to be inspired by the great Impressionists.

**Registration.** To register your artist for camp, please complete the **[Art Camp Registration Form 2025](https://luisatio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/art-camp-registration-form.2025-7.pdf)**[.](https://luisatio.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/art-camp-registration-form.2023.pdf) Once the registration form is completed, please mail it with a $50 supply fee deposit to Luisa Tio, P.O. Box 2442, Alexandria, VA, 22301. You may also Venmo the deposit to @Luisa-Tio and please include your child’s name and camp session. Please complete and send to the same address the forms for **[Emergency Contacts, Health, Media and Walking Field Trip Forms (Summer 2025)](https://luisatio.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/emergency-contacts-health-media-and-walking-field-trip-forms-summer-2025-1.pdf)** and the remainder of the tuition 30 days preceding camp.

**Director and Instructor: Luisa Tio** will lead each session. Luisa is a full-time art teacher at Naomi L. Brooks Elementary School in Alexandria with many years of experience directing and teaching art and creative camps. She also is an artist herself who loves to create. She earned her B.A. in Art from Duke University and her M.A. in Studio Art from NYU.

**More Questions?** Please send Director [**Luisa Tio**](https://luisatio.com/about/) an e-mail at luisastio@outlook.com or call/text her at 703-599-7923.

Halloween comes early to Billings with Harry Potter-themed summer camp
======================================================================

Moss Mansion hosts multiple themed summer camps during the year, Harry Potter being one of them

Prev Next

The Moss Mansion in Billings hosts multiple summer camps throughout the year, Harry Potter being one of them.

![Image 13](https://cf.cdn.uplynk.com/ause/slices/d3f/04469fe8a7064764bca317654e17b0b4/d3f822d9eab94993806e6161843fae79/poster_a1b49afa9d94484ba4c49401fb0691be.jpg)

  ![Image 14: Harry Potter summer camp](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/90d24cb/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F20%2F46%2F3cbb39194650b5426d9dbd84f155%2F3e179e86-546f-4862-9bc8-530bf6525335.png)

[![Image 15](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/461e1ed/2147483647/strip/true/crop/360x360+132+0/resize/300x300!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F63%2F0e%2Fd88dcff84cacbfe761018f2a90b3%2F3b709755-95ce-41f5-ba1f-fb65b3cde79a-4-5005-c.jpeg)](https://www.ktvq.com/mack-carmack)

By: [Mack Carmack](https://www.ktvq.com/mack-carmack)

Posted 11:41 AM, Jun 28, 2024

and last updated 11:41 AM, Jun 28, 2024

BILLINGS — For most, October is the spookiest time of year, but at the [Moss Mansion](https://mossmansion.com/), Halloween comes a few months early.

If you visit the Moss Mansion during the month of June, the inside might look a lot more like Hogwarts, the famed wizard school from the Harry Potter universe.

![Image 17: Harry Potter summer camp](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/53f94fa/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F3f%2Fd1%2Fda4cc5d14cb3bf60971c58827045%2Fcd3d0cee-80ed-418d-89be-1f21eef50241.png)

Mack Carmack, MTN News

"You're not going to find another place like this," says Moss Mansion Executive Director Aly Turner.

![Image 18: Aly Turner, Moss Mansion](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/71d124e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2Ff6%2Feb%2F4dbfc51f4f579ab334fd726e1394%2F70ef851c-1a9d-441f-b3be-53e4238d538c.png)

Mack Carmack, MTN News

For the past four years, the Moss Mansion has brought Halloween, magic, and the summer together with its [Harry Potter-themed summer camp](https://mossmansion.com/event/harry-potter-summer-camp-3/2024-06-21/).

![Image 19: Harry Potter summer camp](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1789b35/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fcb%2Fcf%2F29a3cdda4a24bd61e0af37bd3412%2Ff43c1d7b-f907-4118-8238-7d412db19d7f.png)

Mack Carmack, MTN News

There are two sessions hosted during the month of June, with the second session ending June 28.

But if you've missed this, don't worry as Moss Mansion is also hosting a [Percy Jackson](https://mossmansion.com/event/camp-half-blood/2024-07-15/) and etiquette-themed summer camp.

"It's a great home for the set up of this camp and for Harry Potter. The house is a little reminiscent of Hogwarts," camp counselor and social media manager Gabby Heggem says.

![Image 20: Gabby Heggem, Moss Mansion](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/f85fc42/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F2b%2Fe5%2F52bf7daa44ac9975887efdfbde6e%2F20ad0da3-44bc-4b2a-8d5c-c5d5ae744bf0.png)

Mack Carmack, MTN News

From 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. Monday through Friday, camp counselors Roslyn Visser and Heggem teach young muggles all about Harry Potter.

![Image 21: Rosalyn Visser, Moss Mansion](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/edca19b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fb7%2F36%2F70497d7841a6b672e2e3373b8f82%2F5bf6e946-4ec2-4a2a-a4a9-13d09ec727e6.png)

Mack Carmack, MTN News

The kids play quidditch, design their own wands, and even take classes like herbology.

"Why do a Harry Potter event in a historical house like this? It's like, we want you to explore the house in a new way," said Turner.

Turner and other staff at Moss are passionate about getting tourists in the mansion multiple times a year. So, they have different events and activities in the same building.

Even though this summer camp may be coming to a close, other wizard events are on the way. On July 20, the Moss Mansion is holding a Harry Potter "Tri-Wizard Tournament," which will feature spirit testing, a trivia contest, and magic-themed games.

![Image 22: Harry Potter summer camp](https://ewscripps.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/d95e14e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1920x1080+0+0/resize/1280x720!/quality/90/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fewscripps-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F08%2F42%2Faa5ce10c44ed94e9c7e95894a848%2F07f13abe-031e-4930-a555-140cfee9f94c.png)

Christy is the founder and director of Maplewood Outside School, a forest preschool in Maplewood, NJ. Christy has a Master's degree in Early Childhood Education from Hunter College and has been certified by Cedarsong Nature School, based in Seattle, WA. Christy has taught and learned from some of the best schools throughout Brooklyn and Manhattan, including The Blue School, Community Roots Charter School, The Co-Op School, and Maple Street School.

Christy spent a few years at Brooklyn Nature Days and watched it grow into one of the most successful forest schools in the country. At Brooklyn Nature Days, Christy was a head teacher and worked closely with the founder to grow the program. She then started Maplewood Outside School in 2017.

She is a New York Master Naturalist (level 2) through Cornell University’s Cooperative Extention and an Environmental Steward through Rutgers University Cooperative Extention. Christy joined the South Mountain Conservancy in 2018 and is the Coordinator of the Forest Regeneration Corps and oversees the Wildflower Preserve. She gained her Waldorf Early Childhood Teaching Certificate through Sunbridge Institute in 2022.

Christy is overjoyed to be involved with the BK Natur(ed) team to create new opportunities for children to discover the joy of being in nature.

# Sub-Page: About Us - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
Our goal at Meadowbrook is to create the best possible Camp Community in which children can thrive. We believe Camp is a place where children have the opportunity to try new activities, learn valuable life skills, take on new challenges, increase their self-esteem and grow socially and emotionally in a safe, nurturing, fun environment. We accomplish this through our intentional program emphasizing exciting, age and developmentally appropriate, activities.

Our staff is what makes Meadowbrook truly unique. All staff members are carefully selected and trained, and they understand the importance of acting as positive role models for our Campers. Our staff members reinforce our signature TIGER Values Program on a daily basis with our Campers. Every staff member knows that it is his or her job to find the greatness in every Camper and help create positive “indelible” memories for each member of our Meadowbrook Family.

---

# Sub-Page: Staff - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
We appreciate that your family is part of our special Meadowbrook Country Day Camp Family!

A strong, cohesive staff is one of the keys to Meadowbrook’s success. Our mature and highly trained staff members are committed to creating positive, indelible memories for our Campers. We hire positive role models who embrace our TIGER (Teamwork, Integrity, Generosity, Enthusiasm, Respect) character building philosophy.  Our large Leadership Team assists with staff training during orientation and provides ongoing opportunities for professional development throughout the Summer.

Working at Meadowbrook is a rewarding experience. We are highly selective with respect to who we hire. Opportunities exist for Group Counselors, Waterfront Staff, Athletic Staff, Challenge Course Staff, Creative Staff, Specialty Counselors, and Bus Drivers. Senior Counselors must have completed at least 1 year of college. Junior Counselor opportunities are available for High School students entering their Junior or Senior Year as well as entering college Freshmen. Students entering 10th grade can be Assistant Counselors. All Staff must be available for the full 8-weeks of Camp. To apply for a position at Meadowbrook, download a Staff Application  and submit it to the Camp office. For additional information, contact Rich Sherer at 908-876-3429.

---

# Sub-Page: Facility - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
The Meadowbrook campus is a magnificent 50-acre facility surrounded by natural beauty and nestled in the hills of Long Valley, NJ.

Many visitors to Camp compare it to the facilities that are typically seen only at overnight Camps. The beautiful wooded campus provides natural shade in many areas. We supplement nature with tented structures throughout Camp to provide an additional break from the sun. Water and sunscreen stations are strategically located around Camp to provide a safe, comfortable experience for our Campers.

Meadowbrook Transportation, DOOR TO DOOR
========================================

At Meadowbrook, transportation is fun!  We look at the bus ride to and from camp as the first and last periods of the day.

The bus ride is not a way to get to the fun, but the start and end of it. Our Campers are transported in mini yellow school buses. ALL of our bus drivers are employed directly by Meadowbrook and many of them have been driving our Camp families for years. Each MCDC bus driver is interviewed, screened, and trained by our own Transportation Director ensuring that we have the best quality CDL licensed drivers. Additionally, each one of our buses is staffed by a Bus Counselor to engage your children with fun activities & songs throughout the ride, further ensuring that our Drivers can fully concentrate on the road and keeping your children safe.

# Sub-Page: Programs - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
The Meadowbrook program is extremely creative…always changing…and customized around 8 Weekly Themes that change each year.  Meadowbrook offers a “traditional” Day Camp program which includes a wide variety of athletic, aquatic, ropes and nature activities.  Our program is carefully designed to include not only all the traditional Camp activities, but unique ones as well, such as Bumper Boats, Mountain Boards, Fishing, an amazing High & Low Ropes Course, Earth/Wind & Fire and our Game Room (featuring all Camper friendly games and free play).  We also boast an outstanding Teen Travel Program for Campers entering grades 7-9, which combines travel with a traditional day-camp experience.

Each Camp day includes 10 periods.  Campers are grouped by school grade, and our program is designed to provide the right mix of activities on appropriately sized facilities.  As Campers get older, their daily schedule evolves to include additional activities that challenge their newly acquired abilities and improving skill levels. For example, starting with Campers entering 2nd grade, there is a double "Choice Period" each day where Campers choose the activity in which they want to participate.

Meadowbrook’s Waterfront program offers Campers a variety of activities in our 3 heated pools and one of our two lakes. Our Swim program follows the Red Cross skill level program. Your child's daily schedule will always include instructional swim in the morning and free swim in the afternoon. Our 9,000 square foot pool complex includes 3 heated pools for a variety of swim activities. Our Boating program, on our own private lake, features Canoes, Kayaks, Power Paddlers, Pedal Boats, and everyone’s favorite: Bumper Boats!

Each and every week is filled with innovative special events which match our 8 weekly themes, including the famous Meadowbrook Dance Show. Campers also get to experience our annual "Color War", Blue vs. Yellow in which all camp participates.

# Sub-Page: TIGER Philosophy - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
TIGER represents the 5 core values that we believe create an exemplary Camp community member. Those 5 value are Teamwork, Integrity, Generosity, Enthusiasm and Respect. Campers will be encouraged and motivated to display these 5 qualities through continuous recognition of their efforts. When a Counselor, Division Head, Director of any other Leadership Team member sees a Camper exhibiting exemplary TIGER qualities, the staff member will award the Camper a “Fuzzy” or a TIGER Camper sticker.  Additionally, each day, one Camper in every group will be recognized as the “Camper of the Day” and be awarded a special certificate along with a “Fuzzy”. That award is further reinforced by the explanation of TIGER values and clearly explaining why that Camper earned “Camper of the Day” today.

At the end of each week, one Camper from each Division who consistently models exemplary TIGER characteristics will be given a special Meadowbrook TIGER Award. Additionally, every Friday, one Division is awarded the “TIGER Cup” in recognition of outstanding demonstration of TIGER qualities and values throughout the entire week. We continue to instill these values by recognizing group collaborative efforts through clean bunk awards, (among other awards) to recognize the continuing efforts of our Campers contributions to the greater good of our Camp community.

Our TIGER Program is turned into an even bigger success when our Parents partner with us. Help teach our Campers (your children) how to be a responsible member of our Camp community.

# Sub-Page: Future Families - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
Why We Do It?

We’re here at Meadowbrook all year long planning and preparing for the Summer because our goal is to make a positive difference in the lives of our Campers and their families.

How We Do It?

Our Meadowbrook Program is focused primarily on helping our Campers learn and practice valuable life skills.  These include independence, resilience, perseverance, goal-setting, responsible risk-taking, making friends, sportsmanship, creative problem solving and so many more.  These are skills that our Campers will develop during their Summers at Meadowbrook and take with them throughout their lives, and they are proven life skills that lead to a happier, more successful and fulfilled future.

What We Do?

It isn’t about the facility - - pools, challenge course, fields, specialty areas or the lake. It’s about the people who create the experience for our Campers.  We have a large Leadership Team made up of mature professionals who work with children all year long.  All of the Division Heads are parents themselves so they connect with their Campers and communicate with our families from a parent perspective with a unique level of understanding and empathy.  Our Specialty Staff are all highly skilled and trained in their specific activity areas, and they create age and developmentally appropriate curriculum whether it’s at a creative area, a nature area, on an age-appropriate size field/court or anyplace at Camp. Our Group Counselors are hired and trained with a clear understanding that they are role models and mentors for our Campers.  They recognize that part of their responsibility is to consistently set an example of our core TIGER (Teamwork, Integrity, Generosity, Enthusiasm, Respect) values for our Campers.  The overall “personality” of Meadowbrook sparks from the passion that every member of our tremendous staff team has for Camp.  This passion shines through in the way we invest in our program and facility to keep it fresh and exciting as well as when you see and feel the spirit and enthusiasm that surrounds us at Camp all Summer long!

# Sub-Page: Visiting Camp - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
We believe that the best way to choose a Camp for your children is to visit during the Summer and see Camp “in action” on a typical day.

Every Camp has its own unique personality and no matter when you visit we feel that it is imperative to meet the Owners who are responsible for the care of your Campers. This is the best way to ensure that the Camp you choose for your family is a Camp that supports the values you instill at home and a Camp where your children will make new friends and learn life skills for the future.   
At Meadowbrook, we offer personal tours by appointment throughout the year, including during the Summer.  During the winter, we also hold several weekend Open Houses.  Please call the office to schedule a time to visit us.

---

# Sub-Page: FAQ - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
#### Who is the Camp Owner? Is he Full-Time at Camp?

Mason Goldberg is the Owner/Director of Meadowbrook. He is here onsite every day running Camp.  He is extremely passionate about camp and enriching the lives of Children on a daily basis. Mason solely focuses on Meadowbrook and has no other business interests.

#### What are the hours of Camp?

The Camp day goes from 9am - 4pm. Before Care is available starting at 7:30am and After Care is available until 6pm.There is no transportation for the Before and After Care programs.

#### Will my child learn to swim?

Swimming is a very important life skill that we focus on at Meadowbrook. Each Camper swims at least twice daily. All Campers up through our 6th Grade Campers have a swim lesson every morning.Our 27 Lifeguards plus 3 Waterfront Directors utilize the Red Cross Swim Program to teach all of our Campers to Swim. Our parents rave about the swim progress their Campers make at Meadowbrook!

#### What do you do in the rain?

We have pre-set rainy day schedules that utilize our extensive indoor and covered areas. These schedules feature fun activities that we don't do on regular days, like Karaoke, Dance Parties, Game Shows, and Special Arts & Crafts. Some older Campers may leave Camp for the movies or bowling, but as part of our focus on age and developmentally appropriate activities, Campers up through 4th Grade never leave Camp there are so many fun indoor activities, they don't have to!

#### How will my Camper get back and forth to Camp?

Meadowbrook tuition includes door-to-door transportation on state inspected and air-conditioned mini-yellow school buses. School buses are the safest way for children to travel.  All of our buses are driven by state licensed CDL Bus Drivers that are Meadowbrook Employees!  This ensures that they have been hired, trained, and background checked by us, and they are accountable to us for operating a safe and fun bus ride to Camp each and every day.There is also a Bus Counselor on board who is responsible for organizing fun games and exciting bus events each and every day.

#### What is included and what are extras? What about Tipping?

Meadowbrook is an all-inclusive Camp…EVEN ALL TIPS! Transportation, Lunch, Photos, day trips are all part of tuition. The only thing not included is Optional Trips for our Travel Campers…because they are optional.

#### Why are tips included?

At Meadowbrook, we have an extremely professional staff.  We treat them as professionals, we train them as professionals, and we compensate them as professionals. This applies to all of our Group Counselors as well as our Bus Drivers (who are all Meadowbrook Employees) and our Bus Counselors.

#### How many Counselors are there with each group?

Up to entering 1st Grade for our Girls and 2nd Grade for our boys, each group has at least 3 Group Counselors with them at all times, and many have 4. Older groups have 2-3 Counselors with them. Additionally, all groups are joined by 1 or 2 Activity Specialists at all of their Camp activities.

#### How old are the Counselors?

All Tiny Toons Groups (those entering Pre-K and Kindergarten) are run by a Group Leader who is an experienced “mommy” (an adult female who has children of her own…not in the group).  All other groups are led by Senior Counselors who have all finished at least 1 year of college.  Junior Counselors must be HS Graduates or entering their Jr. or Sr. Year.  Assistant Counselors have finished at least 1 year of High School.  There are NO CIT’s at Meadowbrook!  Everyone responsible for taking care of your Camper is a true staff member…hired by Meadowbrook…fully trained…and paid to work.  Additionally, each Division has a Division Head who is an adult with experience both working with children and as a parent.

#### Do you provide lunch?

A healthy, kid friendly hot lunch is included everyday at no extra cost to you. There are also many alternative options every day as well as a fresh Salad Bar. We also carry fresh fruit daily.

#### Do you have a Nurse on premises?

We always have 2 Registered Nurses at Camp in our modern, air-conditioned Nurses Office.

#### How will you communicate with me during the Summer about my child?

One of our many Division Heads will call you regularly throughout the Summer. You should also feel free to reach out to them at any time. We post photos on our password protected site daily. Younger Campers receive a personalized “Meadowgram” every week and Swim Reports every other week. A full camp newsletter is emailed home at the end of each week.

# Sub-Page: Tiny Toons - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
Our goal at Meadowbrook is to ensure a positive and successful first Camp experience for our youngest Campers.  We want them to develop a love of Camp right from the start.  All of our Tiny Toon Campers are under the careful supervision of a mature staff that is cognizant of the social, physical and emotional needs of young children.  Each Tiny Toons group is staffed with 3 Counselors including a female Group Leader who is always a parent herself, providing a superior level of nurturing care and experienced judgment when dealing with our youngest Campers.  Meadowbrook also has 2 Division Heads, all with children of their own, that supervise our Tiny Toons Divisions (Pre-K, Kindergarten Girls, Kindergarten Boys) providing an extremely high level of care for our youngest Campers.

Tiny Toons have their own air-conditioned changing rooms, their own morning assembly area and eat lunch in their own lunch pavilion. Each day when our Tiny Toons Campers step off the buses, they are met in our bus arrival area by staff that escorts them to their groups.

Tiny Toons Campers participate in many of the same activities as our older Campers; however, they participate on customized facilities at a level designed for their age and abilities. Early childhood sports experts teach all large motor activities on specially designed, age appropriate facilities. Whether at Soccer, Gymnastics, Hockey, T-ball, Tennis or Basketball, Campers will learn their skills correctly.  Tiny Toons Campers also participate in a very wide range of creative programs, including Dance, various Arts & Crafts and cooking programs.  They enjoy Bumper Boats on our Private Lake and our Kindergarteners are introduced to Fishing.  They also have their own indoor Gymnasium, Playground and Ropes Course designed especially for them!  Additionally, our Tiny Toons participate in daily Swim Instruction and Free Swim under the careful supervision of our large team of Red Cross Certified Lifeguards and Water Safety Instructors.

Tiny Toons Campers also participate in everything that makes Summers at Meadowbrook truly special and memorable.  They have morning assembly and all of the fun and excitement that comes with starting the Camp day. They participate in each of our special weekly themes and they see all of the special shows that come to Camp.  Like everything else at Meadowbrook, these events are customized to provide an age appropriate experience for our Tiny Toons Campers.

---

# Sub-Page: Main Camp - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
Our Young Adventurers Division continues to participate in many Meadowbrook favorites such as Archery, Tennis, Fishing, Cooking, Chocolate, Boating, Mountain Boarding and Mountain Biking. The Creative and Performing Arts play an important part in the schedules for our YA girls. All of the girls groups also participate in the Meadowbrook Dance Show during the 6th week of Camp. Meadowbrook’s High Ropes Course and Climbing Tower focus on individual Camper accomplishments.  Just with all Main Camp Divisions, our Young Adventurers play an important part in all of MCDC creative weekly themes and special events.  In addition to a daily double choice period, our Young Adventurers have a Daily Clubs Period which offers them another elective period in their schedule.

Campers in 5th & 6th Grade participate in two Late Night programs each Summer. An exciting element that is added to the Young Adventurers program is four scheduled out of Camp trips during the Summer to such exciting places as Tomahawk Lake Water Park, Powerhouse Studios, Indoor Laser Tag, and more fun locations! In the unlikely event of rain, they may also travel out of Camp as part of our creative rainy day program.

Parents of our older Campers are kept informed of their child's progress in Camp through our bi-weekly Meadow Grams, Swim Reports, weekly Meadow View Newsletter, and direct contact with the Division Head. Visiting Day for our Young Adventurer Campers is at night in conjunction with our Family Late Night. Our website is also constantly updated throughout the Summer with pictures from the Camp day.

---

# Sub-Page: Swim - Meadowbrook Country Day Camp
2017 starts my 64th summer at CAMP!!  I have literally been in camping from the time I was 4 years old as a camper, until now.  When I was 17 years old, I started working at Pierce Camp Birchmont (where I went as a camper) starting in the kitchen as a Shift Leader, General Counselor, Athletic Specialist, Assistant Group Leader, and three summers as a Division Head. I spent the next 25 years as Athletic Director and several years as also Program Director. I have been here at Meadowbrook since 1999.  My first role was as the Ropes Director and after that first year, I’ve since been Camp’s Waterfront Director.  As you can see Camping has been my life’s love.

I retired from Mendham HS in 2011 after 43 years of teaching and coaching.  I have continued to coach Football and Golf since retiring.  I have been honored by the Mendham community by being elected to the Mendies Hall of Fame for the 1975 State Championship in football and in December 2015 was inducted into the Mendham HS Hall of Fame.  In November of 2016 I was inducted to the Roselle Park Hall of Fame for our 1969 undefeated State Championship.  I am also a member of the New Jersey Wrestling Officials for nearly 50 years, and a winner of the Richard Mershack Award for outstanding contribution to Wrestling.  I have also been a volunteer for 40 years with the Madison Fire Department, spending the last 8 years as Battalion Chief.

To me, Camp is a wonderful life experience. You have a chance to meet and make new friends, learn new and exciting activities in a warm, safe, caring environment. In my 17 years at MCDC I have seen great advances in the development of all aspects of camp life.  The facility has been updated from top to bottom. The installation of new bathrooms, a new fieldhouse, new tents, newly renovated athletic fields, upgraded athletic equipment and newly planted trees throughout camp.

The best part of camp is the warm, caring, loving professionals that oversee the daily adventure of the campers & staff.  I look forward to continuing my role at Meadowbrook as we continue our devotion to the personal development and happiness of our members of our Camp family.

I live in Landing with my lovely wife Loretta.  We are blessed with six children (3 each) also rounding out the family is eight grandchildren - 6 Girls, 2 Boys and 2 dogs.

**Enrollment**  
Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Admission is first come First served.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Children are three by October 1st of the year of entry.  Our program is a two year program in a multi-age classroom of 3 and 4 year olds.

We offer two classes:  AM 8:30-11:30  and  PM 12:30-3:30

Your child may attend 3, 4, or 5 days per week.

**3 Sessions/week     $6,854  (Wednesday - Friday)**

**4 Sessions/week     $7079  (Tuesday - Friday)**

**5 Sessions/ week   $7303**

**Fees are per year and are broken down into four installments.**

You may add a day at any time during the year whenever your child is ready, the increase in tuition will be pro-rated.

We accept each child at any stage of toilet training development.  Most children quickly acquire toileting skills with the encouragement of friends at school.

Our program is nondenominational.  We incorporate holidays by inviting all families to share their traditions with the class.

[Apply Here](https://www.jovial.org/millburncoop/hello)

**_Spots fill quickly so feel free to reach out for more information on availability._**

Applications will only be processed after both the application form and a $75 nonrefundable application fee are submitted through the Jovial Portal.

Once we receive your application and fee, a parent recruiter will contact you to set up a classroom visit. Current families have until January 1st to register, then registration will open to those on our application list from the community.

Please feel free to contact our school at

[**info@millburncoop.org**](mailto:info@millburncoop.org)

or call **(973) 379-2778** with any questions.

*   Miss Shona’s Performing Arts Center (as featured on the Today Show) offers both private and group classes for all ages and skill levels in the performing arts. Our high-quality training supports those with professional aspirations, as well as those looking for a fun opportunity to express themselves. All classes have one thing in common, an emphasis on fun! At Miss Shona’s PAC, we pride ourselves in creating an opportunity for students to expand their knowledge and skills in the world, while “performing with a purpose”. In a positive and encouraging learning environment, we focus on having a strong technique to prevent injury, increase good form and to establish a firm foundation for the future. We believe that the arts are a true expression of the inner self and continually encourage students to identify their reason for performing.
    
    [MEET OUR TEAM \>](https://missshona.com/our-team/)

        has a deep understanding of how to meet the individual  
        needs of each child in her classes. Our children adore  
        her, and the grown-ups in our house do too!
        
    *   Miss Shona is one of my daughter’s favorite  
        dance instructors. Her dance routines especially  
        for modern dances, are dynamic,  
        fresh, challenging and expressive.
        
    *   Miss Shona is a dance teacher who strives to solicit  
        the best in each young dancer because she believes  
        in their potential and their capabilities.  
        My daughter has learned so much from her and  
        gained confidence to perform competitively and on stage.
        
    

*   ##### Whether you are a teen serious about a life in the performing arts,  
    a parent who wants to introduce your child to music, dance  
    or acting, or if you’re just looking for a fun, active, social experience.  
    Miss Shona’s PAC can meet your needs.

# Sub-Page: Our Team – Miss Shona
*   #### Shona Roebuck
    
    ###### Owner/Performing Arts Teacher
    
    A B.A. graduate from Rutgers University, Shona Roebuck has many years experience working on stage and film. Shona has had key roles in well-known musical productions such as Carrie, Legally Blonde, Little Shop of Horrors, Into the Woods and Grease. Shona has also had dramatic roles in Streetcar Named Desire, Crucible and La Chanatrice Chauve, a French language production. Shona pulls from all of her singing, dancing and acting experience from stage and film to deliver tutorship, inspiration and mentoring to her classes. Although Shona knows that hard work and dedication are important to achieving one’s goals and dreams, she also believes that learning should be engaging and above all fun, especially for the younger members of her classes.
    
*   #### Lauren Kirk
    
    ###### Dance Teacher
    
    Miss Lauren first found a love for dance at the age of three. During her early years she competed nationally and was a company member at Broadway Dance Center’s children and teen program in New York City. In high school Miss Lauren attended the New Jersey Governor’s School for the Arts, a summer program that selects top arts students from high schools across the state and in 2011 graduated from Rutgers University with a BA in Dance and American Studies. During her time at Rutgers she danced with the modern dance company Insurgo Stage Project and performed/choreographed for several student performances. Upon graduation, she began teaching jazz, hip hop, and ballet in various studios throughout northern New Jersey. During the day Miss Lauren can be found working at the national music ed non-profit, Little Kids Rock. At Little Kids Rock she has had the opportunity to choreograph for music students who perform at the annual benefit with artists such as Bonnie Raitt, Nathan Sykes, Wiz Khalifa, and Jon Batiste. Miss Lauren started working at Miss Shona’s PAC in 2017 and loves sharing her joy of dance with her students!
    
*   #### Tom Frascatore
    
    ###### Acting Coach
    
    Mr¬. Tom found a love for the stage at the young age of 13 and has not been able to leave it since. Performing and directing for over 40 years, Mr. Tom has developed a love for the preparation and technique for actors of all ages. Well versed in helping Actors discover and chart character evolution in relation to the greater piece, resource management and creative space utilization. Mr. Tom has directed and taught all over the tri-state area including the local Paper Mill Playhouse. Mr Tom is honored to be the Acting Teacher/Coach at Miss Shona’s PAC where he started in 2017 and loves bringing a passion for the craft to each of his students.
    

*   #### Jenna Burniston
    
    ###### Dance Teacher
    
    Miss Jenna is originally from Maplewood and is an elementary special education teacher in SOMSD! She loves to connect her passion for education with her love of dance and theatre through teaching at Miss Shona’s PAC. Miss Jenna joined Miss Shona’s PAC in 2017 and can be seen teaching summer classes, assisting in musical theatre classes, subbing, and working in the office. She is also the Camp Manager at our partner organization, MMTC (Morrow’s Musical Theatre Camp)!
    
*   #### Melina Soriano 
    
    ###### Dance Teacher
    
    Melina Soriano is a creative artist and holistic healthcare advocate who recently received her BFA from Montclair State University with a minor in psychology. Prior to Montclair, Melina studied under Raegan Wood, director of The Taylor School, while performing with Paul Taylor’s Teen Ensemble. Melina also attended High Tech High School and under the guidance of Trista DeFilippis found a keen interest in choreography. Melina has performed works by Paul Taylor, Ohad Naharin, David Parsons, Fredrick Earl Mosley, Tiffany Rea-Fisher, Yusha-Marie Sorzano, and Larry Kegwin. Her first choreographed film work Cerulean Dream was released summer of 2021. Melina has shared her love for dance since 2017 where she began teaching along Raegen Wood for the Teen K-12 Outreach Teaching Artist Program in New York City. Since then she has taught at Montclair State University alongside Julia Burrer, Greenhouse Arts Center alongside Lauren Panzica, as well as Nimbus Art Centers’ Summer Arts Program, and more recently Dance to Learn. Melina is currently a nursing student at Chamberlain School of Nursing, with the goal of combining the arts and healthcare. She is thrilled to be joining the team at Miss. Shona’s PAC!
    

*   #### Lindsey Garnhart 
    
    ###### Dance Teacher
    
    Lindsey Garnhart is a dance artist who holds a BFA in Dance and a minor in Business from Temple University. Prior to college, she studied ballet, modern, jazz, and tap for 15 years at Center for Dance Education. She is currently a member of and has performed with Freespace Dance Company, APDance Inc, and rachelanddancers in New York City, and with Klassic Contemporary Ballet Company in Philadelphia, PA. Her recent choreographic work has been presented at The Secret Theater in Queens, NY, Conwell Dance Theater in Philadelphia, PA, and in virtual settings. Lindsey is a rotating assistant for Tracie Stanfield’s virtual classes at Broadway Dance Center. She also teaches at several dance studios in the tristate area. In addition to dance, she is the administrator for Group Motion in Philadelphia, PA and APDance Inc in New York City, and worked on the social media team at American College Dance Association and Boyer College. She is so excited to be a part of the Miss Shona’s PAC family!
    
*   #### Jillian DeGironimo 
    
    ###### Dance Teacher
    
    Jillian recently moved from Maplewood to her first home in Union with her husband and two cats Artemis and Ceres! She is a practicing Speech Language Pathologist with a Bachelor’s degree from Geneseo State and a Master’s degree from Seton Hall University. Jillian found dance at eight years old and it immediately became her passion. She has danced and studied many styles throughout her life including ballet, jazz, modern, lyrical, and tap. Jillian has taught dance classes to children of all ages. In her free time, Jillian enjoys practicing yoga, reading a good book, and spending time with friends and family! Jillian is excited to embark on her first year teaching at Miss Shona’s Performing Arts Center!
