#### K/1 Program

[View More](https://www.newhorizonsdaycamp.com/our-program)

Our Pre-K - Kindergarten -1st Grade Program is open to campers that are entering Pre-K through 1st Grade in Fall 2025.  
  
Featuring a dedicated K/1 Program Director, 3.5 to 1 Staff Ratios, and a proctored schedule that exposes your child to all our camp has to offer, this is the perfect way for your camper to launch their camp career!

![Image 18: Gaga Cropped.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/e09dd3_fc060f90f1374a38850ee990c230ca2d~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_208,h_208,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Gaga%20Cropped.png)

#### 2nd - 8th Grade

[View More](https://www.newhorizonsdaycamp.com/our-program)

Our 2nd - 8th Grade campers have the unique ability to customize THEIR perfect summer experience! Featuring over 100 unique activities, your child will choose their individual activities, allowing them to try something new or take a deep-dive into an existing interest.   
  
From athletics, swimming, art & archery, to media, coding, engineering, & performing arts, we have it all! -- Your camper is never stuck in an activity that doesn't match their interests!

![Image 19: Archery Cropped.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/e09dd3_67e95b99ffe647cb8004c9691c889289~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_208,h_208,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/Archery%20Cropped.png)

#### 9th Grade & CIT

[View More](https://www.newhorizonsdaycamp.com/our-program)

Our 9th Grade campers have the option to choose "Counselor in Training" as a component of their final summer as a New Horizons Camper. Working with each individual family and camper, our CIT Director will custom fit the perfect day for your child.

While still enjoying all their favorite activities, their day will also include two activities of Counselor Instruction, and work with existing staff members to receive hands-on training as they prepare to join our staff the following summer!

### Our Program & Activities

### Mission Statement from our Directors

"Help every camper experience THEIR perfect summer!"
----------------------------------------------------

Every single camper is different which is why we have built New Horizons to allow children from Pre-K through 9th Grade to try something new, take a deep-dive into an existing interest, or mix-and-match their day to create the summer of a lifetime!

​

At NHDC every activity and grade group is led by an 18+ Head Counselor with professional educators leading nearly all our major activity areas. Extensive off-season training, a 3.5 to 1 staff ratio, and highly specialized counselors allows us to offer an unparalleled program from athletics to coding... art to archery... cooking to podcasting consisting of OVER 100 UNIQUE ACTIVITIES!

#### K/1 Program

It’s important for your child’s first experiences with camp to be happy ones. At this early age, children thrive when they are protected and nurtured, as well as flourish when they are encouraged to explore their own interests.  
  
Managed by our dedicated K1 Directors Katherine Cawley & John Odell, the program offers a small, nurturing environment in which your child gets a chance to experience all New Horizons has to offer while learning new sports, academic and social skills everyday.

#### 2nd - 8th Grade

The 2nd Grade Jump Start Program helps our campers transition from the K/1 Program.

Second Grade Campers will participate with their group in a sport, art, swim and technology during the first half of the day and then build their custom afternoon! This gives young campers a chance to get comfortable with the upper program while being exposed to all New Horizons has to offer.

​

The 3rd – 8th Grade Program offers a traditional camp experience while believing in the element of CHOICE. Your camper customizes their entire schedule with a variety of activities in the areas of: Sports, Technology, Creative Arts, Performing Arts, Innovations, Academic Enrichment, Media, Coding, Swimming. Activities change bi-weekly so your child will have the opportunity to enjoy new experiences throughout the entire summer!

​

At New Horizons you're never stuck in an activity. Campers may elect to switch from one activity to another at any time during a session!

#### 9th Grade & CIT

At New Horizons campers entering the 9th grade are allowed to participate in our Counselor in Training (CIT) Program.

Under the leadership of our CIT Director, your camper will experience what it's like to be a counselor. We custom fit the CIT Training for each camper, allowing them to continue to participate in their favorite camp activities while also learning valuable skills and working with our fantastic staff. The goal of the CIT program is to prepare your child for opportunities with New Horizons Day Camp for the summer before entering 10th grade.

# Sub-Page: Our Staff
### OUR STAFF

Seth Blender
------------

Owner, Founder, & Director
--------------------------

Seth has been involved in day camps for 20 years. He spent the majority of his camping career at Camp Horizons in Livingston, NJ. During his 10 summers at Camp Horizons, Seth was a Kindergarten and 1st grade counselor and during his last 2 summers was the Director of the Shadow Counselor program at Camp Horizons with direct supervisory responsibility for special needs campers in grades 5 through 9. Currently, Seth is a Special Education Teacher for the Glen Ridge Public Schools and holds a Masters Degree in Curriculum, Assessment and Instruction. Seth lives in Cedar Grove, NJ with his wife, and three children.

Chris Purdue
------------

Owner, Founder, & Director
--------------------------

Chris is a Health and Physical Education Teacher at Collins Elementary School in Livingston, NJ with 12 years of experience teaching at multiple schools within the District. Chris holds a Master’s Degree in Exercise Physiology from Montclair State University as well as one in Educational Leadership. He holds both his Supervisor’s Certificate and Principal’s License. Before New Horizons, Chris directed the sports program at Camp Horizons for 8 summers from 2005 through 2012. Chris currently lives in Kinnelon, NJ with his wife and two sons.

Mike Wynne
----------

Owner and Program Director
--------------------------

Mike Wynne, aka The King of Camp™, is entering his 20th camp summer. After running the Media Programs at Camp Horizons and New Horizons Day Camp, he took over the Unit Head position for 6th-9th grades. In his current role of Program Director, Mike focuses on activities, special events, and ensuring every camper has the best summer experience of their lives. In addition to his duties as Program Director, he also serves as Media Director, Head of Assistant Counselor Development, and Color War High Chancellor. Easily recognizable by his shockingly blue sunglasses, booming voice, and propensity for carrying around a bull-horn, Mike gives 172% every day of the summer to ensure our campers have the best 8 weeks of their lives.

Katherine Cawley  
K/1 Director

Katherine is an elementary school teacher within the Cedar Grove School District. She has worked with various age groups from Pre-K 3 all the way to fourth grade. She is excited to return to another great year at NHDC and loves helping our youngest campers launch their camp careers! Her excitement and dedication to our youngest campers is contagious! Katherine lives in Bloomfield with her handsome cat, Binx.

Will Fanslau  
Shadow Program Director Inclusion Specialist

William has been part of the New Horizons family for four summers and is looking forward to a fifth! He was a sports counselor for a year, the head counselor of the first grade for two years, and is entering his second year as the Director of the Shadow Program. William oversees campers with special needs and assistant staff members throughout the summer. William is a graduate of Montclair State University where he received his degree in Psychology. William is currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology as well as a certification to be a School Psychologist.

Will Beck  
Unit Head 2nd-9th Grade

Will has been a member of the Horizons Family for over a decade. He eats, breathes, and lives for only one purpose; New Horizons Day Camp! Over his career, Will has served as a Shadow Counselor, Assistant Counselor, Grade Head Counselor, and an amazing Green Team Color War Captain. Posted by: Naida Wolf - January 24, 2025

Get ready for a summer full of excitement, exploration, and unforgettable memories at **New Horizons Day Camp** in Florham Park, NJ! As the only fully customized day camp in the area, New Horizons offers a unique experience where campers can build their own summer schedule, ensuring each day is filled with activities they love. Whether your child is into sports, arts, science, or just wants to make new friends, New Horizons has something for everyone.

With over 100 unique programs and activities to choose from, for kids from kindergarten to 9th grade, New Horizons combines traditional camp favorites like swimming, sports, and crafts with modern offerings like STEM workshops, cooking, and performing arts. The flexible schedule allows campers to try new things and develop their skills in a safe, inclusive, and nurturing environment. Plus, with options for full-day or half-day programs, busy parents can rest assured knowing their child’s summer is filled with meaningful engagement and fun.

Led by a team of experienced counselors and educators, New Horizons Day Camp focuses on building confidence, fostering friendships, and encouraging creativity. Conveniently located in Florham Park, NJ, the camp is easily accessible for families across the region. Don’t let your child miss out on the chance to design their best summer ever! Spaces are filling up fast—secure your camper’s spot now!

Visit [New Horizons Day Camp](https://www.newhorizonsdaycamp.com/) to learn more and register today.

# Main Page: Camp NMOA 2024 — The Newark Museum of Art
Welcome to Camp NMOA 2024, an extraordinary six-week summer adventure at the heart of Newark, NJ! From July 8 to August 16, 2024, let your child embark on a journey of artistic and scientific discovery, surrounded by the rich cultural landscape of our renowned art museum.

General Information & Pricing
-----------------------------

Join us for six weeks of project-based learning where campers can develop their skills in art and science while building community.

Enrich your child’s summer at Camp NMOA – where creativity knows no bounds!

**Camp dates:** July 8 – August 16, 2024

**Ages:** 3 – 13

**Camp day:** 9am–3:45pm  
One-hour break includes lunch and recess.

**Members & Newark Residents  
**$290 per child, per week

**General Public  
**$320 per child, per week

**Pre-care: 8:15–9am  
**$30 per child, per week

**Aftercare: 4–4:45pm  
**$30 per child, per week

**Extended day bundle, includes pre-care and aftercare  
**$50 per child, per week

Registration
------------

Registration for Camp NMOA 2024 is officially open. Remember, Camp NMOA is made up of six one-week sessions. You can sign up for any of the weeks at random or in order!

Each week we will explore a different theme!
--------------------------------------------

**Week 1: July 8-12 |** **Pixels & Portraits: Art Meets Tech!**  Unleash your creativity in a digital art adventure! Dive into pixel art and portraiture, discovering the blend of traditional techniques with digital art.

**Week 2: July 15-19 |** **Ride the Wave: Ocean Adventure!**  
Join us for an ocean-inspired exploration and create your own sea-inspired masterpieces. Surfers of creativity will explore the wonders of the _Animal Kingdom_ and oceanic marvels.

**Week 3: July 22-26 |** **Rhythm Nation: Art & Beats!**  
Discover the art of sound and movement! Drum into the world of music and visual arts, connecting beats, brushstrokes, and self-expression.

**Week 4: July 29-August 2 |** **Earth Allies: Planet Protectors!**  
Befriend our planet through art and science! Engage in eco-friendly activities, delve into sustainability, and create Earth-inspired art. Explore the wonders of nature through Global Arts and express love for the planet.

**Week 5: August 5-9 |** **Going for the Gold: Art & Science Champions!**  
Embark on a journey celebrating art and science excellence! Explore the history of achievements and how they inspire greatness.

**Week 6: August 12-16 |** **Vintage Voyage: Time Travelers’ Art & Science Quest**  
Embark on a time-traveling adventure exploring historical art and scientific innovations! Dive into different eras, revive traditional artistry, and uncover ancient scientific marvels in this thrilling journey through history.

![Image 1](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/campweb2-1440x1360.jpg)

Each week includes:
-------------------

**Artmaking** – Create art inspired by our galleries. New projects every week.

**Science Experiments** – Explore a wide variety of science topics!

**Maker** – Learn different art techniques and create your own designs.

**Planetarium** – Go beyond our planet and discover new worlds with our astronomer.

**Yoga** – Introduction to child-friendly yoga.

**Music & Movement** – Learn quick dance routines while getting a workout.

**Funday Fridays** – Enjoy games, team-building activities, and so much more on Fridays!

Contact Info
------------

Questions? Contact Jessica Nuñez at [camp@newarkmuseumart.org](mailto:camp@newarkmuseumart.org).

FAQ
---

Camp NMOA is made up of six one-week sessions. You can sign up for any of the weeks at random or in order. For example, you can sign your child up for weeks 1 & 3 only, if you prefer.

Keep in mind that performance showcases happen only in Weeks 2, 4 & 6. The other weeks end with just an art exhibition.

Our camp staff is made up of professional educators and teaching artists. Some have worked at the camp and as Museum educators for many years. Our high school assistants take part in The Newark Museum Explorers Program, a highly competitive college and career preparation program for high school students.

We offer Museum members and Newark residents a 10% discount on weekly rates. To receive more information about becoming a member, [click here](https://newarkmuseumart.org/join-give/membership/). Unfortunately, we do not currently offer any sibling discounts. We offer a limited number of scholarships. Please contact Jessica Nuñez for more information.

Each age group’s day is slightly different, but all campers participate daily in art workshops, gallery tours, science activities, planetarium, and performance art classes. Your child will also enjoy a variety of other special events. Friends and family are invited to our Performance Showcase and/or Exhibitions on alternating Friday afternoons to see what campers have been learning and creating throughout the week.

The Performance Showcase takes place on Friday afternoons (Weeks 2, 4, & 6), at 3:00pm in the Billy Johnson Auditorium, located on the lower level of the South Wing. Friends and family are invited to watch child-centered performances by the campers. Each camp group will perform a short song, dance, poem, or play that they learned or composed that week. Immediately following the show, guests are invited to the 2nd floor in the South Wing for an exhibition of campers’ artwork from the week.

During morning drop-off, please leave your car on the Museum side of the driveway and walk your child in through the South Wing entrance. Camp staff will be waiting to help sign your child in on the attendance sheet and escort your child to the auditorium. Unless you signed up for pre-care, please drop your child off between 8:45 and 9am. During afternoon pick-up, please leave your car on the Museum side of the driveway again and head to the auditorium, which is down a short flight of stairs and to the left, in the South Wing lobby.

**IDs must be provided by anyone picking up a child**.  After ID check, please find your child’s teacher and sign your child out on the attendance sheet before leaving. Regular pick-up is from 3:45 to 4pm. If you need to pick up your child early, please let us know in advance.

Late pick-up fees are $1 per minute for both regular and extended days. If you are running late, please call ahead and let us know. While awaiting your arrival, your child can attend after-care where there are plenty of activities for them.

We offer both pre-care and aftercare, which is priced separately at an additional $30 for each. Pre-care runs from 8:15 to 9:00am and aftercare is from 4 to 4:45pm. During these times, campers have several free-play options. They can draw or read quietly, play games, and make simple crafts like lanyards or origami. Please pick up your child by 4:45pm at the latest. The Museum is closed to the public at 5pm and all visitors must be out of the building by that time. Late pick up fee is $1 per minute for both extended-day and regular-day campers.

Payment by credit card can only be made online through the registration website. We also accept payment by electronic check on the registration website. Payments by check, cash or money order can be made in person, by appointment, at the Museum or mailed to the Museum at the address below. Payments must be postmarked on or before the dates of the price changes in order to receive that rate. Please send mail to:

Attention:  
Camp NMOA  
49 Washington Street  
Newark, NJ 07102

A username is associated with an account that is used by you to maintain your and your child’s information. Our registration system also functions as a database, which stores campers’ vaccination and health records. Each child is registered separately to create an individual medical file used to accommodate those with allergies and other medical issues. Having an account and associated username also enables parents to register and pay for a session, then log in later to fill out the medical information and complete their child’s file. The database will also make future registration easier.

Each registered camper will receive one tee shirt on the first day of camp. Campers are required to wear a Camp NMOA tee shirt every day. Additional tee shirts are available for $5 each.  Other clothing should be loose and comfortable and allow campers to move around freely during movement class. We advise against wearing expensive clothing, as art and science projects are frequent and messy.

Campers are grouped according to age: 3 & 4 years old, 5 & 6years old, 7 & 8 years old, 9–10 years old and 11–13 years old. Enrollment is limited to ensure campers receive personal attention. Instructors are professional educators and teaching artists experienced in working with a range of age groups and abilities. Each art, science, and performance art workshop is designed to fit a particular camp group’s age and developmental ability.

Yes, the 3- & 4-year-old group has daily nap time in the afternoon. We ask that you pack a blanket and pillow for your child to rest with. We also ask that you pack an extra set of clothes in a plastic bag. Although campers must be toilet-trained, we understand that accidents happen and would like them to be well prepared. Camp NMOA is not classified as a daycare by our state license.

**As such, we are not permitted to change diapers or pull-ups for our younger campers or enter the bathroom to assist them. Please make sure your 3- & 4-year-olds are completely toilet-trained before sending them to camp. The cutoff date by which all campers must be 3 years old is March 1, 2024.**

The Museum no longer requires proof of vaccination, negative COVID-19 tests, or temperature screenings.

Lunch is not provided by the camp. We are a nut-free camp, so please do not send your child to camp with any food that contains nuts. Please pack a healthy lunch and water bottle for your child. We also ask that 3- & 4-year-olds bring two additional snacks and 5- & 6-year-olds bring one additional snack for the day. We also recommend packing an additional snack for the other age groups.

Campers do not have the option to buy lunch at camp.

The vending machines are off limits to campers.

All camp staff are trained in CPR and first aid. If there is a minor injury, camp staff will administer first aid such as a band aid or an ice pack. If your child requires more assistance, or if your child is ill, we will do our best to get in touch with you or your emergency contact using all the contact information you provided us. If we cannot reach you and feel that your child needs to go to the hospital, a camp staffer will escort your child to the emergency room across the street and stay with him or her until you arrive.

90% of the camp registration fee is refundable if cancelled before June 1, 2024. 50% of camp registration fees is refundable if cancelled between June 2 and June 30, 2024. After July 1, 2024, no refunds will be offered, which also applies to any registrations after that date.

The main Camp NMOA phone number is 973.596.6637. You can also call the Museum’s main number at 973.596.6550 for general inquiries.

---------------------

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/29808/shell-trumpet?ctx=5078e8b481c756adbbcd94d9e259bc17edb50d4c&idx=0)

![Image 88](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2024.4.1-1-1440x1021.jpg)

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/232368/prison-industrial-ii?ctx=c66131337a73c33052134ddf9e7b8c67ba560a66&idx=0)

![Image 89](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2007.46.9-1120x1440.jpg)

Toshiko Takaezu, Vessel, 1975‑1979​ Porcelain, 6 x 5 1/2 in. (15.2 x 14 cm)​ Gift of the artist, 2007 2007.46.9​ © The Family of Toshiko Takaezu​ Photo by Richard Goodbody

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/175223/vessel?ctx=12adacf055d19c453eb78f0c45622ac3824fe12c&idx=0)

Shikeith, O' my body, make of me always a man who questions!, 2020​ Inkjet print, 50 7/8 × 61 7/8 in. (129.2 × 157.2 cm)​ Purchase 2022 Helen McMahon Brady Cutting Fund 2022.5.1​ © Shikeith, Courtesy Yossi Milo Gallery, New York

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/231607/o-my-body-make-of-me-always-a-man-who-questions?ctx=3a857b76fdb5e9f5060b8c18d337e434b523e413&idx=0)

Wendy Red Star (Apsáalooke/Crow), Winter ‑ The Four Seasons Series, 2006​ Archival pigment print on sunset fiber rag, 23 x 26 in. (58.4 x 66 cm)​ Gift of Loren G. Lipson, M.D., 2016 2016.46.1.3​ © Wendy Red Star

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/221043/winter--four-seasons?ctx=90f6011d925ba66cd429a24d7e9c5cd8513d0490&idx=4)

Vivan Sundaram, Re‑Take of Amrita ‑ Bourgeois Family ‑ Mirror Frieze, 2001​ Digital photomontage printed on archival paper, 15 x 26 in. (38.1 x 66 cm)​ Purchase 2008 Helen McMahon Brady Cutting Fund  2008.57

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/180120/retake-of-amrita--bourgeois-family--mirror-frieze?ctx=13c0f7b4509507781b53e7a2ee8c5aad23e6ad9d&idx=0)

Gilbert Hsiao, Tango Nuevo, 2006​ Acrylic on wood, 48 x 48 x 1 ¾ in. (121.9 × 121.9 × 4.4 cm)​ Purchase 2023 The Alberto Burri Memorial Fund, established by Stanley J. Seeger 2023.5.2​ © 2023 Gilbert Hsiao​ Photo by Richard Goodbody

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/231887/tango-nuevo?ctx=6be441013c044da58eb0a8ca60a8617f60dd315b&idx=0)

![Image 94](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2022.7.2-View-1-previously-TR64.2022.2-1440x1203.jpg)

Johnny Nelson, Her Freedom Ring, 2022 ​ 14K yellow gold, 3 1/2 x 1 1/4 in. (8.9 x 3.2 cm)​ Purchase 2022 Barbara Harrison Wescott Fund 2022.7.1.2​ Photo by Richard Goodbody

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/231645/her-freedom-ring?ctx=6d011137868411a2572befeed92ce2ec47a96879&idx=1)

![Image 95](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/28.1160-1-975x1440.jpg)

Azume, Horse and Rider, Before 1928​ Ceramic, pigments, 17 1/2 x 6 x 12 in. (44.5 x 15.2 x 30.5 cm)​ Gift of Mrs. Erick Berry, 1928 28.1160​ Photo by Richard Goodbody

[Learn More](https://collections.newarkmuseumart.org/objects/84554/horse-and-rider?ctx=05aa9df056fcaf9a3698b3a84256cf965a489c5c&idx=0)

[![Image 96](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Linda-headshot-scaled-1440x1152.jpg) #### Art, Celebration & Transitions Welcome the special season of celebration, light and transition. Our world is offering us change on many fronts, but what endures are our traditions, our relationships, and the strength of the institutions we have created. Let’s celebrate all that we have and share gratitude for what we have built together. A Museum of courage, joy and wonder. Read More](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2024/12/12/art-celebration-transitions/)

Our Community
-------------

[![Image 97: Roundtable: What Does it Mean to be an Artist in Newark in 2020 video screen](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Screen-Shot-2021-12-02-at-3.16.55-PM-1440x791.jpg) #### Roundtable: What Does it Mean to be an Artist in Newark in 2020? Dexter Wimberly, independent curator and entrepreneur, is in conversation with five Newark artists. Read More](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2021/12/02/roundtable-newark-artist/)

[![Image 98: Jo-El Lopez](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/jo-el-lopez-1-1440x864.jpg) #### Artist Talk: Jo‑El Lopez Newark‑based artist Jo‑El Lopez discusses his work in this presentation and Q&A session. Read More](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2024/04/02/artist-talk-jo-el-lopez/)

[![Image 100: Patricia Dahlman photo by Colleen O'Neal](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/PatriciaDahlman_photo_by_Colleen_ONeal.jpg) #### Studio Snapshot: Patricia Dahlman Artist Patricia Dahlman discusses how she was inspired by the arts scene of Newark and how her work responds to our current times. Read More](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2024/04/03/studio-snapshot-patricia-dahlman/)

[![Image 101: Willie Cole](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/willie-cole-1-1440x883.jpeg) #### Artist Talk: Willie Cole In this talk, Newark‑based contemporary artist Willie Cole focuses on his more recent work, The Water Bottle Giant. Read More](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2024/04/03/artist-talk-willie-cole/)

[![Image 102: 2023 Impact Report inside newark museum of art](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/2023-Impact-Report-inside.jpg) #### Explore Our Journey: NMOA’s 2023 Impact Report Explore how The Newark Museum of Art made a difference in 2023. Read More](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2024/03/04/explore-our-journey-nmoas-2023-impact-report/)

### Our Mission

We welcome everyone with inclusive experiences that spark curiosity and foster [community](https://newarkmuseumart.org/visit/our-city/).

Through your [membership](https://newarkmuseumart.org/join-give/membership/) and [donations](https://newarkmuseumart.org/donate/) you are supporting us in offering access to world renowned [collections](https://newarkmuseumart.org/collections/collection-areas/) of American art, decorative arts, contemporary art, and arts of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and the ancient world. # Main Page: About Us — The Newark Museum of Art
Who We Are
----------

The Newark Museum of Art (NMOA) was founded with the belief, radical among museums in 1909, that art and learning are for everyone. Today, New Jersey’s largest fine art museum is a vibrant center for the arts and community and places special emphasis on public programming that engages local artists and audiences.

As a leading cultural institution for more than a century,  NMOA stewards collections of more than 300,000 artworks and artifacts in science and natural history – the 12th largest museum collection in the nation. Known as the first institution to give sustained support to modernism in America, NMOA continues to pursue new definitions of cultural innovation and is among the 3% of U.S. museums that are nationally accredited.

The Museum’s 3.1 acre campus offers a range of settings to explore, wonder, and create including the National Historic Landmark Ballantine House (1885); the Ward Carriage House (1860); the Old Stone School House (1784); the Dreyfuss Memorial Garden; the Dreyfuss Planetarium (1954),  New Jersey’s the first planetarium.  NMOA partners with our community to preserve and advocate for the arts, history and culture, and to host special events such as the [Newark Black Film Festival](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2023-newark-black-film-festival/), the longest-running Black film festival in the United States, and the [Newark Arts Festival](https://newarkmuseumart.org/exhibition/cross-cultural-perspectives/), a four-day catalyst for the collaborative power of the arts in the city.

NMOA puts the people of Newark, their creativity and strength at the center of its work, responding to the evolving interests of diverse audiences and critically examining its responsibility to equity.

[![Image 1](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Washington-Street-and-the-James-Street-Commons-Historic-District-Neighborhood-.jpg)](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Washington-Street-and-the-James-Street-Commons-Historic-District-Neighborhood-.jpg)

Washington Street and the James Street  
Commons Historic District Neighborhood

Our Mission
-----------

We welcome everyone with inclusive experiences that spark curiosity and foster community.

### Our Vision

Founded in 1909 on the radical belief that art is for everyone, our Museum engages with the public to build a more equitable, kinder, and sustainable world.

Engagement Principles
---------------------

### We are _of_ the Community

#### WELCOME

_We welcome everyone_

We lower barriers to entry and participation and reflect the community around us.

#### CONNECT

_We connect personally_

We focus on personal connections and ongoing relationships.

#### PARTICIPATE

_We enable meaningful participation_

We foster the exchange of ideas and information through immersive, playful, and interactive experiences.

#### ACT

_We take action on equity issues that matter_

We instigate programs, partnerships, and outreach that address issues of social needs and justice.

### Initiatives

DEAI Statement
--------------

The Newark Museum of Art (NMOA) is dedicated to embedding the principles of diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion (DEAI) in all aspects of its work and organizational culture. In undertaking this work, the Museum is committed to anti-racism–conscious efforts and deliberate actions intended to create equal opportunities for all on both an individual and systemic level. Since its founding in 1909, the Museum has been grounded in the belief that art and learning are for everyone. The Museum reaffirms its dedication to this inclusive vision that has informed its aspirations, if not all of its actions and policies, for over 100 years.

NMOA defines DEAI principles as follows:

*   **Diversity** – Diversity is all of the factors that shape the experiences, values and perspectives of individuals.  These include but are not limited to age, mental and physical ability, gender identity, race, national origin, religion, socio-economic status, and sexual orientation.
*   **Equity** – Equity is the promotion of fair and just treatment, access and opportunities for all staff and members of our global community.
*   **Accessibility** – Accessibility is the equitable access of all people to use, experience or participate in activities, resources, facilities, and services, regardless of human ability or socio-economic status.
*   **Inclusion** – Inclusion refers to the intentional effort of creating environments in which all individuals or groups can feel welcomed, respected, empowered and valued. It is also an effort to cultivate leaders at all levels to fully participate in the Museum’s work with equal agency.

To advance these principles and serve our community, NMOA:

*   Ensures that all exhibitions, programming, facilities and services are accessible to everyone.
*   Provides a forum for public discussion of vital community issues, including social justice, and equality for historically marginalized groups.
*   Includes under-represented voices, stories and perspectives in exhibitions and programming.
*   Ensures that the Museum’s exhibitions, programming, collections, publications and public communications present historical facts and events accurately, and represent diverse cultures in a respectful and culturally competent manner.
*   Forges meaningful and mutually beneficial relationships with diverse individuals and organizations in the community, including local BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and disability advocacy groups, which will help ensure that all visitors feel welcome, valued and heard in the Museum community.
*   Diversifies NMOA’s Board, leadership, staff and volunteers at all levels. These efforts will include the implementation of more equitable hiring and retention practices, the expansion of job qualifications and recruitment strategies to reach diverse candidates, and public transparency about the membership of our Board of Trustees and senior management team.
*   Conducts ongoing staff-wide DEAI professional development on issues such as developing cultural competency, and strategies for identifying, addressing and preventing discrimination, including unconscious bias, on both a personal and institutional level.
*   Creates zero-tolerance policies regarding racism and microaggressions that arise within our institution and in our work with the public. These policies will be implemented through a timely and thorough complaint process followed by necessary corrective actions.

Our Impact
----------

Financial Information
---------------------

The Museum’s financial statements and 990 IRS filings are available for download as PDFs. These reports provide information on the Museum’s financial strength and provide transparency into its accounting and financial practices.

Letters from the Director
-------------------------

![Image 2](https://newarkmuseumart.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Linda-headshot-scaled-720x576.jpg)

### Art, Celebration & Transitions

December 12, 2024

Welcome the special season of celebration, light and transition. Our world is offering us change on many fronts, but what endures are our traditions, our relationships, and the strength of the institutions we have created. Let’s celebrate all that we have and share gratitude for what we have built together. A Museum of courage, joy and wonder.

[Continue Reading](https://newarkmuseumart.org/2024/12/12/art-celebration-transitions/)

[Refund Policy](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4675)
--------------------------------------------------------------

With written notice, you will receive a full refund, less $100 administrative fee, if your child withdraws from a program before April 1. After April 1, tuition fees are non-refundable, without exception.

[Registration Fee](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4677)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

A fee of $50 will be charged for all registrations not received on or before May 1.

[Transfer Changes](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4679)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Transfers or changes from original registration are based on availability, and approval is at the discretion of camp administration. There will be a $30 transfer fee for any change from the original registration form. This includes switching weeks or camps (i.e., Day Camp to Extreme Sports Camp).

[Payment](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4681)
--------------------------------------------------------

The required deposit must be made with registration. We cannot hold a spot for your child without a deposit. Full payment must be made by May 1. There is a $100 returned check fee.

[Camp Groups](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4683)
------------------------------------------------------------

Groups are created as registration is processed. Early registration provides the best chance of all requests being met. We try to accommodate all requests for friends to be grouped together. For school-age children, the groups are based upon the grade entering this fall. Requests for special groupings are not guaranteed. No refunds will be given for this reason.

[Behavior](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4685)
---------------------------------------------------------

We expect each girl and boy to contribute to the safe and supportive learning environment established at Oak Knoll. Inappropriate behavior may necessitate a private conference with the participant and his or her parent. Camp reserves the right to dismiss a camper without refund of tuition if conduct is determined to be detrimental to the well-being of the camp or campers. The camp also reserves the right to dismiss a camper if camp administration reasonably concludes that the partnership between a parent/guardian and camp makes a positive and constructive relationship impossible or seriously interferes with the camp’s accomplishments of its mission and purpose. The decision of Summer Adventures in this regard shall be final.

[Insurance](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4687)
----------------------------------------------------------

Certain activities at camp have risks that are inherent to the activity. When participating in these activities, campers and parents assume responsibility for these risks. If you have any questions about risks that may be inherent to certain activities, please contact the Adventures Office. Since most campers have health and accident insurance, the cost of including additional insurance has not been included in the registration fees. Camp is not responsible for any items that are lost, stolen or broken.

[Camp Information](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4689)
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Just prior to the start of camp, all registered participants will receive an email of general information including what to bring, what not to bring, car line procedures, etc., and all forms required for camp.

[Cancelation](https://www.oakknoll.org/summer#fs-panel-4691)
------------------------------------------------------------

Oak Knoll’s duties and obligations shall be suspended or terminated immediately without notice during all periods that Oak Knoll School is closed because of force majeure events including, but not limited to, any war, riots, fire, act of God, governmental action, act of terrorism, epidemic, pandemic, or any other event beyond Oak Knoll’s control. If such event occurs, OKS’s duties and obligations will be postponed until such time as the school, in its sole discretion, may safely reopen. In the event that Oak Knoll School cannot reopen due to an event under this clause, the school is under no obligation to refund any portion of the fees paid.

### SUMMER CAMP

**2½-6 years  
9am-1pm, 3pm or 5:30pm  
5 days per week  
Early drop off at 8am is available.**

Summer at Playhouse offers a nurturing environment filled with hands-on activities and many opportunities for outdoor play. Our experienced teachers create a welcoming and comfortable atmosphere for children to play and grow. Some of our activities include:

Water play/splash pad  
Weekly trips to the town splash pool  
Chick hatching, animal care and gardening  
Outdoor art, music, and cooking  
On-site playground with sandbox

Camp runs for 8 weeks in July and August, and is divided into two 4-week sessions. A child may enroll for one or both sessions. Schedule choices are 9am-1pm, 3pm or 5:30pm. Other scheduling options are available to current Playhouse families. Early drop-off is available at 8am.

### Inside the classroom

Our bright and airy building has been purpose-built to offer a wide range of exciting and stimulating learning areas; this includes:

*   A bespoke kitchen with a low bench for children’s cooking
*   A dedicated story and role-play corner
*   Literacy and numeracy zones
*   Areas for investigative and imaginative challenges

Focusing on learning through play, we follow the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum to ensure that activities engage and challenge youngsters in a setting where children feel safe, happy, secure and confident.

#### Teacher Led Sessions

Being a part of the Churcher’s College family means our children are blessed with the opportunity to take part in special teacher led sessions both within the Nursery and in other parts of the Junior School, in such subjects as Spanish, Music, Computing, PE, and Art.

#### Yoga Sessions

We offer yoga once a week which offers the children fun yoga poses and exercises to help cultivate self-health, relaxation, and body awareness.

### Outside the classroom

Children love exploring the school grounds and a great emphasis is placed on the ‘outdoor classroom’.

> The sandpit, garden, mud kitchen, playhouse and water and role-play areas provide an invigorating environment in which to learn.

There is also a hard surface for riding bikes and covered space to play, whatever the weather.

![Image 10](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/61b20da6ea6b8e6ab918791b/611e1d88-5a9e-41e9-b3c5-641e923bf2df/SUMMER22.png)

![Image 11](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/61b20da6ea6b8e6ab918791b/2d1157e9-6667-4d99-8053-4ceff05e3654/BOUNCY.png)

![Image 12](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/61b20da6ea6b8e6ab918791b/736e78b1-92c9-4146-978c-dc9c27b43e05/LEGO.png)

![Image 13](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/61b20da6ea6b8e6ab918791b/b0eb147d-85ea-4fd8-959d-4391ed59de14/S25.png)

![Image 14](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/61b20da6ea6b8e6ab918791b/c3250a80-fd62-4361-b5c0-45c0b677d0b6/CONNOR.png)

#### **Summer ‘25 ‘Open House’ dates:**

*   #### May 3rd/10th at SummerHill Park.
    

#### **Typical camp day** **schedule :**

*   #### 8.30am \*Optional ‘before care’
    

*   #### 9 - 9.15am: Arrivals, registration, and camp welcome. Rules on camp, daily behavior awards and divided into camp age groups.
    
*   #### 9.15 -10.15am: x2 (30 minute sport station rotations)
    
*   #### 10.15 -10.30am: Snack break
    
*   #### 10.30am -11am: x1 Final sport station rotation
    
*   #### 11am: Half Day departures (15 mins free play)
    
*   #### 11.15 -11.45am: Lunch
    
*   #### 11.45-12pm: Trail walks
    
*   #### 12-1pm: Combined camp games & activities (Capture Flag, Dodgeball etc)
    
*   #### 1pm: Camp departures
    
*   #### 3pm Extended day ‘after care’ departures  
    

#### We have a ‘arts and crafts’ station located in the shaded tree area. This can be used for downtime and/or children who want this outlet. On FUN Fridays we have a water event and a bouncy castle onsite!!

*   #### 9-11am (Half Day) $205
    
*   #### 9-1pm (Full Day) $385
    
*   #### 9-3pm (**NEW** Extended Day) $450
    
*   #### **NEW** Multi-package camp week options : two, four-week and full summer program packages!
    
*   #### **NEW** Early drop off available (from 8.30am) each camp day ($10 Daily or $50 for full week can be vemnoed to @ProventusKids
    
*   #### In the event of inclement weather during your camp week, we do have access to local indoor gymnasiums we are partners with.
    
    #### **2025 Dates and Times :**
    
*   #### Week 1 June 16 - 20th (9-3pm option)
    
*   #### Week 2 June 23 - 27th (9-3pm option)
    
*   #### Week 3 June 30 - July 3 \*4 Day camp - no camp July 4th
    
*   #### Week 4 July 7 - 11th
    
*   #### Week 5 July 14 - 18th
    
*   #### Week 6 July 21 - 25th
    
*   #### Week 7 July 28 - Aug 1
    
*   #### Week 8 Aug 4 - 8

Iva Krmelova

USAG Head Coach

Recreational Coach

Pre-School Director

Iva became a member of the Czechoslovakian Junior National Team at age 12.  In 1983, Iva was the Junior National All-Around Champion.  She became the Czechoslovakian National Champion in 1986.  Iva competed at the 1987 World Championships held in Rotterdam, Holland and in 1988, the Olympic Games which were held in Seoul, Korea where her team. (Czech Republic) took 7th. During her competitive years, Iva was always coaching younger girls.  In 1988, Iva went on to study at the Sports Institute of Charles University in Prague, Czech Republic where she later graduated in 1993.  She also became a gymnastics Judge with a No. 2 Judges Rating.  After a few years of coaching in her hometown, Iva moved to the United States and began coaching in Florida.

​

USAG Safety, First Aid  & CPR Certified

Joined Sunburst August 1998.

Paul Lakomy  
USAG Head Coach

Recreational Coach

Paul became a member of the Czech Junior National Team in 1990.  He has four Junior National Championship titles and was a member of the Czech National Team in 1993.  Paul competed at the Junior European Championships held in Geneva, Switzerland in 1992 and in 1993 at the European Championships held in Prague, Czech Republic.  In 1996 he competed again in the European Championships which were held in Jyavesjyka, Finland.   Paul also competed at two World Championships, the first in 1994 held in Dortmund, Germany and the second in 1995 held in Sabae, Japan. Paul started coaching gymnastics in 1992.  Even while training for his world class competitions, he always found time to help the younger gymnasts. He studied at the Sports Institute of Charles University in Prague, Czech Republic. He also holds a No. 2 Judges Rating.

USAG Safety, First Aid and CPR Certified

# Main Page: USAG Team and Xcel | San Antonio, TX
SGA Team
--------

Gymnastic

SGA Girls Developmental, acrobatic, and xcel program
----------------------------------------------------

 Competitive Team
-----------------

Sunburst Gymnastics has a team program for all ages and abilities. From 3 hours a week to 25 hours a week, 4 years old to high school age, and beginner to advanced, we have it all.

Artistic Gymnastics has Pre-team groups, Developmental Program (Compulsory and Optional) teams,  and Xcel teams training in the gym every day. These team programs compete on all 4 Olympic events (Vault, Uneven Bars, Balance Beam, and Floor Exercise). Athletes train strength, flexibility, dance, and skills daily to perfect set or choreographed routines at competitions around the country. USAG artistic gymnasts compete as individual and team competitors.

Also offered is Acrobatic gymnastics. This aspect of gymnastics combines the beauty of dance with the strength and agility of artistic gymnastics. Acrobatics is a partnership sport where athletes perform in pairs, trios or quads. It encompasses two skill types: balance and dynamic. Acro (as it is usually referred to) introduces the artistry of dance, balance, strength, and aerial awareness, seamlessly weaving in elements of tumbling, flexibility, and agility. Routines are choreographed to music and performed on a spring floor. Currently this program is only available in our Boerne facility.

Our competitive teams compete in San Antonio, all around Texas, and around the country. Sunburst has had multiple district, state, regional and national champions. If you are interested in learning more about the teams please contact us and we will be happy to help.

For team information please email:   San Antonio- **[sunburstgym@gmail.com](mailto:sunburstgym@gmail.com)**      Boerne- **[info@sgboerne.com](mailto:info@sgboerne.com)**

![Image 16](https://www.theconnectiononline.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/camp-banner.png)

### [**REGISTRATION NOW ONGOING!**](https://operations.daxko.com/online/5147/ProgramsV2/Search.mvc?category_ids=CAT625)

**WHAT’S NEW FOR 2025?**

*   There will now be two Guppies (age 3) groups so please be sure to add friend requests. Both Guppies groups with have have a dedicated room, bathroom, and outside area.
*   We now offer FULL DAY SummerFun –  Give your camper the best of both worlds with our NEW SummerFun full-day option! Campers will start their day enjoying all the fun and excitement of the classic SummerFun morning. Then, they’ll seamlessly transition into the afternoon, where they’ll choose from a variety of specialty camps tailored to their interests! Be sure to select an afternoon option to complete your camper’s day! You’ll register for the full day with one click to make registration easier.
*   There are no PM only camps other than Theater Camp to make the 1PM pick-up go smoothly.

[![Image 17](https://www.theconnectiononline.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/1-150x150.png)](https://operations.daxko.com/Programs/Redirector.aspx?program_id=43644&cid=5147)

**TIPS FOR REGISTRATION DAY**

*   If you have a 3 year old, sign up for guppies first – it’s our quickest filling camp! 
*   Complete your child care profile early to save time on registration day. Click your child’s name on your account, fill in any missing information on their profile, and answer the camp registration questions. 
*   Make sure your Program Membership is up to date through August 22, 2025. 
*   [Click here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Yy2oLsMis4NvkoydWLV9IOfVFuvJyaZIZ9Bym00V_-E/edit?usp=sharing) for a camp overview to see all camp offerings in one spot. 
*   Early Bird Discount: Use code FULL to save $20 off each full-day camp or use code HALF to save $10 off each half-day camp by Feb 4th.

The Connection’s summer camp is committed to providing campers with excellent recreational, educational, and fun experiences while creating a memorable summer in a physically and emotionally safe environment.  Campers will make friends, gain self-confidence, learn to work together, and acquire new knowledge and experiences.

*   [Click here to view our frequently asked questions about summer camp.](https://www.theconnectiononline.org/summer-camp-faq/) 

There are no refunds or credits for absence or withdrawal from Summer Camp. **[Click here](https://www.theconnectiononline.org/summer-camp-terms-of-enrollment/)** to read The Connection Summer Camp’s terms of enrollment.

If you are interested in financial assistance for Summer Camp, please [**click here.**](https://www.theconnectiononline.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Summer-Camp-2025-cover-sheet.pdf)

2025 Summer Art Camp for Teens (ages 13+)[Brian Riley](https://www.artcenternj.org/author/briley/ "Posts by Brian Riley")2024-12-10T22:06:25+00:00

**Monday–Friday, 10 AM–3 PM**  
Teens ages 13+ will gain an in-depth studio art experience that engages their creativity and enhances their skills. Each week, teens will concentrate on two focus areas during their studio sessions. Small class size enables our talented teaching artists to take a deep dive with teens to build their techniques and individual styles.

[**FULL-DAY Painting with Acrylics **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7607&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**June 16–20  
****Full-Day Painting with Acrylics:** Spend the whole week focusing on this one versatile medium. Teens will spend both morning and afternoon sessions learning how to paint with acrylics. Teens will learn how to block in a composition and see it come to life as they add paint to their canvas. They will learn the fundamentals of painting, including brush techniques, how to create light and shadow, and color mixing. Teens will also learn how to handle the materials properly. Students should wear clothes that can get messy—acrylics don’t wash out of clothes!

[**NEW! FULL-DAY Fashion & Fabric Design **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7608&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**June 16–20  
****Full Day Fashion & Fabric Design:** Teens will explore traditional and non-traditional fashion design. Campers will have a chance to sketch fashion ideas as they make vision boards to help fine tune their fashion vision. Students are encouraged to bring in a piece of clothing they will alter and embellish. Students will also design a t-shirt and will have the opportunity to make a tote bag from fabric they dye themselves during camp. Multiple sewing and fabricating techniques will be covered while we create wearable art!

[**The Magic of Mâché and Collage & Mixed Media **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7609&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**June 23–27  
****The Magic of Mâché:** This week is devoted to the art of taking ordinary items and transforming them into sculptures. Aluminum foil, glue, paper, and cloth with a heavy sprinkle of creativity is all that is needed. Exposure to different ways of creating three-dimensional forms opens the mind to different ways of problem solving for creative inspiration. Have some fun and get your hands dirty!  
**Collage & Mixed Media:** Mixing it up is what collage and mixed media is all about! Campers will have the opportunity to use a variety of supplies such as paint, patterned paper, fabric, fibers, and more. During this camp week, students will learn about shape, color, texture, and light, all while creating both representational and abstract works of art.

[**Back by Popular Demand! Tiny Week and New! Non-Traditional Painting (4 days) **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7610&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**June 30–July 3  
****Tiny Week:** It’s a short week, so let’s go small! Students will use multiple mediums to create unique sculptures and figures while exploring the art world at a miniature level. Have fun creating tiny art you can hold in your hand.  
**New! Non-Traditional Painting:** During this 4 -day camp, students will learn to paint using non-traditional painting tools. Students will paint using wax paper, plastic bags, fibers, textured fabric, objects from nature, and more. They will even learn to use their hands to paint (gloves provided for those who prefer). Campers will get to create paintings using both representation and abstract styles.

[**Oil Painting and Soft Sculpture **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7611&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**July 7–11  
****Oil Painting:** Painting can seem difficult, but it doesn’t have to be! Students will learn the foundational skills of painting in oils. This camp will cover the basics, including blocking in a composition, color mixing, value studies, and proper handling of materials. Students should wear clothes that can get messy.  
**Soft Sculpture:** This camp takes the best of fiber arts and sculpture and merges them into a whole new art form: soft sculpture! Using textural materials such as felt, fibers, and notions—along with imagination and creativity—campers will design, prototype, and create both relief sculpture and sculpture in the round. Being able to sew is a bonus, but not necessary, since multiple methods of soft sculpture construction will be covered. Students will create several projects ranging in scale over the course of the week.

[**New! Paper Art and Painting with Acrylics **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7612&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**July 14–18  
****Paper Art:** During this week, campers will make art using a variety of different kinds of paper. Students will learn to fold paper, use pulp to paint, explore quilling techniques, collage with printed material, and build sculptures with paper. Students will learn how to use paint, fibers, and other materials to enhance their paper creations.  
**Painting with Acrylics:** Have fun exploring this versatile medium. Students will learn how to block in a composition and see it come to life as they add paint to their canvas. They will learn the fundamentals of painting, including brush techniques, how to create light and shadow, and color mixing. Campers will also learn how to handle the materials properly. Students should wear clothes that can get messy—acrylics don’t wash out of clothes!

[**New! Comics & Story Illustration and Jewelry Design **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7613&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**July 21–25  
****Comics & Story Illustration:** Students will be guided in the process of creating their own comics by building characters and stories. Learn the process of making your ideas come to life in a visual format!  
**Jewelry Design:** Make wearable art! Students will experiment with jewelry-making techniques to create pendants and bracelets of their own original designs. After starting with a sketch, the instructor will help students use a variety of materials to create their vision. Projects may include, but are not limited to, wrapped wire pendants, polymer clay canes, and recycled paper beads.

[**Everything Clay and Character Design **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7614&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**July 28–August 1  
****Everything Clay:** This camp is perfect for the student looking to explore various types of clay. During the week, we will get to use the pottery wheel to throw and embellish a functional ceramic piece that will be glazed and fired in the kiln. We will also learn the techniques for working with paper clay, from building an armature to give the clay structure to ways to decorate their creations using paint, decoupage, or other materials. Finally, we will explore polymer clay by making everyday objects in miniature.  
**Character Design:** During this week of camp, students will learn to design their own character(s) for comic books, graphic novels, or cartoons. They will focus on personality and expression plus learn anatomy and posing using the human body as reference. We will also have a chance to explore costume design for their character. All this will come together in a project that features the character(s) they created.

[**Assemblage and Essential Drawing & Painting **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7615&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**August 4–8  
****Assemblage:** Campers will transform everyday items into expressive, personal sculptures! Imagine all the artistic possibilities in combining materials such as paper, plastic, clay, and wire with found objects. Through demonstrations and hands-on practice, campers will learn various techniques to manipulate the materials and create one-of-a-kind sculptures.  
**Essential Drawing & Painting Techniques:** This camp is perfect for the student looking to develop the foundational skills of drawing and painting. Campers will use observational skills and gain familiarity with diverse media, such as graphite, charcoal, acrylics, and watercolors, through drawing exercises that may include gesture drawings, blind contours, and contour drawings. Linear perspective, color theory, and building form with light and shadow will also be covered as campers render their artistic creations.

[**New! Collage, Mixed Media & Mask Making and Essential Drawing & Painting **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7616&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**August 11****–15  
****Collage, Mixed Media & Mask Making:** Mixing it up is what collage and mixed media is all about! Campers will have the opportunity to use a variety of supplies such as paint, patterned paper, fabric, fibers, and more. During this camp week, students will learn about shape, color, texture, and light, all while creating both representational and abstract works of art. Our featured project will be putting these skills to use creating amazing papier-mâché masks!  
**Essential Drawing & Painting Techniques:** This camp is perfect for the student looking to develop the foundational skills of drawing and painting. Campers will use their observational skills and gain familiarity with diverse media such as graphite, charcoal, acrylics, and watercolors through drawing exercises that may include gesture drawings, blind contours, and contour drawings. Linear perspective, color theory, and building form with light and shadow will also be covered as campers render their artistic creations.

[**Printmaking Techniques & Fiber Arts **](https://artcenternj.augusoft.net/index.cfm?method=ClassInfo.ClassInformation&int_class_id=7617&int_category_id=0&int_sub_category_id=0&int_catalog_id=0)**August 18****–22  
****Printmaking Techniques:** In this unique camp, students will create their own limited-edition prints on our professional presses. Learn various techniques, styles, and tools of the printmaking trade through demonstrations and hands-on practice. This camp will cover techniques including plexiglass drypoint and monoprinting as we create original prints that are either one-of-a-kind or editionable.  
**Fiber Arts:** Vibrant fibers and textures surround us—explore the wonderful world of fiber arts! Campers will create several skill-building projects during this exciting week of camp. A variety of fiber arts will be visited and may include weaving, hand sewing, embroidery, felting, pom-pom making, and more. Let the creativity unfold!

**SCHEDULES & PRICING**

**Daily Schedule  
**8 AM – Extended care begins (optional)  
9:30–10 AM – Car line drop-off  
10 AM–12:15 PM – Morning studio session  
12:15–12:45 PM – Lunch (brought from home)  
12:45–3 PM – Afternoon studio session  
3–3:30 PM – Car line pickup  
5:30 PM – Extended care ends (optional)

**Pricing Per Week**

(Member discounts apply to members at the Dual/Family level and above)  
Early Bird Tuition (last day to save is 2/17/25):  $500/week members; $510/week non-members  
Tuition (as of 2/18/25): $515/week members; $525/week non-members  
\*Week of June 30–July 3: $425/week members; $435/week non-members (4-day week)

**Optional Extended Care**

We offer early drop-off starting at 8 AM, and late pick-up until 5:30 PM. The following options are available:

STUDIO SCHOOL
-------------

Art Camp
========

Send your child to one of the area’s most popular camps! For the past several seasons, our Summer Art Camp for Kids has almost completely sold out. Why? Because our Summer Art Camp is a fun, relaxed, and creative atmosphere where children gain the wellness benefits of artmaking, including a sense of self-empowerment and improved social and emotional well-being. Individual class sizes are small for maximum instructor and counselor attention. For caregiver convenience, a carline will be used for camper drop-off and pick-up.

##### **Kids (ages 5–9)**

Art Camp for Kids is for children ages 5–9 and focuses on project-based instruction, centered around weekly themes. Our camp instructors will guide your young ones through a variety of projects that utilize an assortment of media, including painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, mixed media, and more.

[2025 SUMMER ART CAMP FOR KIDS](https://www.artcenternj.org/school-studio/art-camp/2025-summer-art-camp-for-kids-ages-5-9/)

[2025 SATURDAY ART CAMP FOR KIDS](https://www.artcenternj.org/school-studio/art-camp/2025-summer-saturday-art-camp-for-kids-ages-6-9/)

##### Tweens (ages 10–12)

Our Tween Art Camp provides campers the opportunity to further explore art media and techniques in greater depth. Daily studio sessions will offer tweens the opportunity to begin developing their own personal style, while they learn and refine their art skills.

[2025 SUMMER ART CAMP FOR TWEENS](https://www.artcenternj.org/school-studio/art-camp/2025-summer-art-camp-for-tweens-ages-10-12/)

##### Teens (ages 13+)

Our Teen Art Camp offers in-depth studio art experience that engages campers’ creativity and enhances their skills. Each week teens will concentrate on two focus areas during their studio sessions. Small class size allows campers to dive deep and build technique and individual style.

[2025 SUMMER ART CAMP FOR TEENS](https://www.artcenternj.org/school-studio/art-camp/2025-summer-art-camp-for-teens-ages-13/)

# Sub-Page: Our Directors - Willow Lake Day Camp
Willow Lake has been under the same family ownership for over 40 years offering healthy summer experiences filled with personal growth, character development and fun. Wendy Saiff – Owner & Director

Wendy has a master’s degree in education and was a teacher for 20 years before becoming the full time owner and director of Willow Lake in 1996. Willow Lake Day Camp has been in her family since 1980. Wendy has seen firsthand the positive impact a camp experience has on children- developing independence, confidence and competence. The mother of 3 children and now also a grandmother, Wendy realizes that selecting an appropriate camp program can be difficult. Charles Maltzman – Owner/Director

His extensive background in day and resident camp make him a valuable friend and advisor to our campers, staff and parents. Charles is passionate about camp and is committed to providing a healthy, safe and fun camp experience. He is actively involved with American Camp Association and is a former member of the Tri-State Conference Steering Committee and a former committee member of SCOPE, an organization that helps send disadvantaged kids to camp. Charles has two daughters who will be Willow Lake campers for many years.

Jake Weissman – Director

# Sub-Page: FAQ - Willow Lake Day Camp
Willow Lake Day Camp is located in Lake Hopatcong, New Jersey.

You can view our most up-to-date list of session dates by .

Our campers come from Essex, Morris, Union and Sussex counties.

A typical group has 15-17 campers. Our Pre-K groups are coed and the remainder of camp groups are single sex. Each group and unit consists of campers going into the same grade in the fall.

Our typical camp day runs from 9:00am – 4:00pm. Each day we expose each camper to a carefully balanced schedule of our key areas: swimming, athletics, arts, outdoor adventure and special events.

The number of counselors varies by age group. Our Pre-K has 4 counselors per group, our Kindergarten through 3rd grade have 3 counselors per group, and the rest of our groups have 2 counselors and a counselor-in-training. These group counselors stay with the group all day and are active participants at each activity.

Each age group is also assigned a Unit Leader. Each Unit Leader is a parent, teacher or coach who takes part in our year round training meetings to constantly review and improve everything about Willow Lake. Unit Leaders contact each camp family before the summer begins and remain your camp liaison throughout the summer. Unit Leaders spend their day out on the grounds ensuring that each child is safe, is participating and is having fun! At the end of camp, unit leaders will return any phone calls that come in during the day.

Activity specialists are hired to instruct specific activities. Each specialist is a teacher, coach or professional in their field and is able to teach age appropriate skills which foster personal growth and build self-esteem.

Willow Lake employs a full time registered nurse. We also have water fountains and water coolers all around camp and our staff constantly encourage all campers to stay hydrated. We ask for you to apply sunblock before your child gets on the bus and then we will reapply sunblock throughout each day as needed.

We are very fortunate to have so much indoor space that rainy days are easy for us to handle! To ensure that things run smoothly, we have a rainy day schedule already made before camp starts. We review the schedule with our staff during orientation and camp is able to transition smoothly to the schedule when needed.

We supply everything your child will need except for 2 bathing suits, a towel and sunblock. Enrolled families will receive a list of things that you should send as the summer gets closer.

Willow Lake emphasizes active participation and skill acquisition over winning and losing. Our camp community encourages campers to cheer for and support each other and show good sportsmanship when winning and in defeat.

As campers get older and take part in our elective program, they can chose to participate in more competitive games, leagues and instruction.

We would love to hear from you! Please send us an email or call us any weekday between the hours of 9:00 and 5:00. Wendy and Charles will happy to speak to you and schedule a tour of our campus.

The Willow Lake staff are patient, friendly, warm and caring. All staff takes part in our extensive orientation process where we spend time training how to work with campers experiencing a more difficult transition adjusting to camp. Our small group sizes and mature staff are a perfect blend to allow us to closely monitor group dynamics and ensure group cohesiveness throughout the summer.

Camp is made for making friends! Many of our campers come to camp not knowing anybody and make friends after their first day at camp.

You bet! Willow Lake is steeped in tradition with certain special events that take place each year like our Color Olympics, Carnival, MTV day, Wild Water Day, etc. We also have many other special events each year such as Bubble Day, Graffiti Day, Halloween in July, Friendship Day, Tattoo Day and Pajama Day to name a few. When you add shows by professional musicians, magicians, etc. as well as trips out of camp, every day at Willow Lake is a Special Event!

Since space is limited in each age group, we encourage families to enroll early. We offer an early enrollment discount – see the enrollment application for more information!

# Sub-Page: Aquatics - Willow Lake Day Camp
Instructional & Free Swim
-------------------------

Swimming is at the core of the Willow Lake program.  Our staff focuses on building confidence while teaching skills.  Pre K – 4th grade campers swim in one of our 4 heated pools for both instructional swim in the morning and “free” swim in the afternoon.  5th – 8th grade campers have free swim twice each day with the option of taking instructional swim as an elective choice.  Our pool complex is designed to accommodate a wide range of ages and skill levels.  Campers are placed in small sized swim groups based upon their individual ability.

Each member of our swim staff is Red Cross Certified and has teaching experience to provide the highest level swim instruction for each camper.  We are acutely aware that some campers have a fear of water and our staff is always caring and patient creating a learning environment comfortable for all campers. Swim instructors teach in the water to ensure contact interaction and support for each camper.

*   4 heated pools
*   Two exciting waterslides
*   Red Cross swim program
*   Certified and qualified swim instructors

*   Emphasis on safety
*   Daily instructional swim and free swim
*   Individualized instruction so campers progress at own pace

We have designed a unique swim program specifically designed to create a positive and healthy learning environment.  The Willow Lake “fish” program breaks down the Red Cross swim levels into a format which is easier for instructors to teach and more fun for campers to learn!   As campers pass each level, we present them with a certificate at camp.  Our campers love to share their certificates with parents and parents love to celebrate their child’s success!

# Sub-Page: Staff - Willow Lake Day Camp
Willow Lake Day Camp is committed to providing an incredible experience for our campers.  We know that our staff has the biggest impact on a camper’s summer and we are proud that so many staff return each summer to be part of our camp community.  Our staff are fun, friendly, caring and enthusiastic, yet understand the importance of both safety and responsibility.  We look to hire staff that are so dedicated to our campers that they will always go the extra mile each day to help make every camper’s day better.  Our staff spends the day supporting, nurturing, teaching and interacting with campers.  It is because of this that our staff forms meaningful relationships with our campers and each other.  Working at Willow Lake provides the opportunity to make life-long friends.

---

# Sub-Page: Why Willow Lake? - Willow Lake Day Camp
Working at Willow Lake is:

### Incredible People

What makes Willow Lake really stand out is the quality of people, both campers and staff, who spend their summers here.   Our camp community is supportive, fun and bursting with enthusiasm and excitement.

### Fun

We are great at fun!  Fun is what we do.  There are always new activities to try, special events to make you smile and friends to make you laugh.

### Making a Difference

Working at Willow Lake allows you to impact campers’ lives in meaningful ways.  You will help create memories that will stay with children forever.  Cheering on campers when they score a goal, encouraging campers to try and climb a little higher and just listening to a camper when they need an ear to hear them out- this is what camp is about…

### Small Camp Feel

Our campers and staff both tell us that Willow Lake has a sleep away camp feel.  Our directors and leadership team are easy to approach and we are hands on in the day to day decision making in camp.  Our staff is large enough where you can meet a variety of new friends, yet small enough where nobody is a stranger.

### Tradition

We have been building a camp community filled with tradition for over 40 summers.  While we often add new events, programs and activities each year, we also keep the same traditions that have become the fundamental core of Willow Lake over the years.

### Organization and Attention to Detail

We prepare for rainy days, humid and hot days and perfect days.  We dissect the camp schedule each year to evaluate every aspect of it and make sure that it works best for every age group in camp.  We are constantly coming up with new activities, new programs and new special events.  We are also always looking to tweak any existing programs until they work exactly the way we want them to.

### Partnering with our Staff

We appreciate and value our staff and believe in giving our staff the tools they need to succeed.  We encourage our staff to be creative and bring new ideas to camp.  We also have a wealth of information of what has worked and not worked in the past.  We share all of this with you during our staff training and are always willing to help guide you before and during the summer.

### Great Benefits

Willow Lake is working outdoors every day, interacting with great people, teaching and learning.  Willow Lake is decision-making, public speaking, organizing and initiating.  Willow Lake is free lunch, letters of recommendation and friends and memories that will last forever.

---

# Sub-Page: Available Positions - Willow Lake Day Camp
You will find descriptions of our summer positions below.

Unit Leaders
------------

Unit Leaders are teachers and adults who supervise an entire age group/ unit.  They are responsible for everything in the unit and directly supervise the counselors and campers in every aspect of their camp experience.  Unit Leaders meet with the Directors before and after camp each day to review all pertinent information that arises regarding group dynamics, food issues and scheduling.

Unit Leaders also serve as the liaison between the camp and camp families.  Unit Leaders are also responsible for all contact with parents from the pre camp phone call through the last day of camp.  Because Unit Leaders are always around their campers, they know everything about them and are able to communicate with parents about personal situations which may arise.

Senior Counselors
-----------------

A Senior Counselor is in charge of a group of 15 campers.  They supervise the staff working under them and make sure that the group dynamic is positive and that the group is safe and enjoying camp!  All Senior Counselors must be entering the equivalent of their sophomore year of college.

Counselors
----------

Every camp group has a counselor(s) who are active participants in every aspect of every camper’s day.  The bond formed between camper and counselor is extremely important and often dictates how a camper likes camp.  Willow Lake counselors are active, patient, warm, friendly, fun, energetic and responsible.  They also must demonstrate good listening skills and be able to relate to children and sincerely care about their needs.  Counselors must be entering a minimum of either 11th grade or 12th grade.

Lifeguards
----------

Lifeguards teach swim instruction each morning to campers in small groups.  In the afternoon, lifeguards are in charge of guarding our heated pool complex. Lifeguards must be certified through the last day of camp.

Specialists
-----------

Specialists are in charge of providing instruction to campers in a specific activity area with the support of the group counselors.  While we have a curriculum in place for each activity, we tend to hire specialists who want to add their own ideas and continue to develop the program further staying within the camp’s philosophy.
